body: 'Siapa Hijjas Kasturi? Tokoh Sebalik Mercu Tanda Di Malaysia Beliau turut membina mercu tanda seperti Menara Maybank, Menara Telekom, Shahzan Tower dan lain-lain. - Hijjas Kasturi, bapa seni bina moden Malaysia, mencipta bangunan ikonik yang mencerminkan identiti budaya dan Islam negara. - Karya terkenalnya termasuk Menara Tabung Haji, Menara MBPJ, dan PICC, setiap satunya menggabungkan elemen tradisional Melayu. Pemandangan ibu kota Kuala Lumpur dipenuhi dengan pelbagai bangunan dan pencakar langit yang mempunyai identiti, cita rasa serta seni bina tersendiri menghasilkan rupa unik. Namun, ramai tidak sedar bahawa di sebalik beberapa bangunan menghiasi ibu kota, terdapat satu nama yang sama. Nama tersebut ialah Hijjas Kasturi, seorang tokoh yang digelar sebagai bapa seni bina moden Malaysia. Sehingga kini, karyanya bukan sahaja menghiasi landskap negara, malah menjadi inspirasi kepada ramai generasi muda. Bermula Di Singapura Pada Tahun 1936 Hijjas Kasturi dilahirkan di Singapura pada 26 September 1936. Ibunya berketurunan Cina telah berkahwin dengan seorang lelaki berketurunan Jawa-Singapura. Beliau mendapat pendidikan di Raffles Institution, sebelum menerima biasiswa dari Kerajaan Australia untuk menyambung pelajaran. Menariknya, Hijjas telah mula belajar di University of Adelaide, sebelum menjadi graduan daripada University of Melbourne. Pada tahun 1967, Hijjas berpindah ke Malaysia dan mengasaskan program ijazah profesional pertama di negara ini, iaitu School of Art and Architecture di Institut Teknologi MARA (ITM). Bermula Sebagai Seorang Pelukis Pelan Perjalanan kerjaya Hijjas bermula seawal tahun 1956 sebagai seorang Draughtsman bersama Singapore Housing Trust. Dia bertanggungjawab untuk menyediakan master plan bagi kawasan Queenstown dan rumah apartment kos rendah. Kemudian, kerjayanya berkembang merentasi dua buah negara menerusi beberapa jawatan penting seperti: - 1959: Menyertai South Australian Housing Trust, menyediakan master plan Elizabeth Town dan skim perumahan. - 1961: Menjadi Pembantu Seni Bina dengan Brown & Davis yang terlibat dalam perancangan hospital, bangunan komersial dan perumahan. - 1965: Menjadi arkitek dengan Hume Proprietary Ltd, Melbourne bertanggungjawab merancang pembinaan kilang, gudang dan pejabat. - 1966: Kembali semula ke Singapura sebagai Arkitek / Perancang dengan Housing and Development Board (HDB). Hijjas turut mengetuai pasukan kajian penubuhan ITM dan menjadi Ketua Pengasas School of Art and Architecture. Pada tahun 1969, Hijjas menjadi rakan kongsi pengasas Arkitek Bersekutu, sebelum akhirnya menubuhkan firma sendiri, iaitu Hijjas Kasturi Associates Sdn (HKAS). Proses Mencari Identiti Seni Bina Melambangkan Malaysia Bagi Hijjas, seni bina bukan sekadar membina bangunan, tetapi membentuk identiti sebuah bangsa. “Saya mahu menyumbang kepada kebaikan budaya dan rakyat dengan mencipta landskap visual yang mencerminkan identiti Malaysia.” Pencarian identiti itu merupakan satu tindak balas selepas tamatnya zaman penjajahan di Tanah Melayu. Ketika negara kita mencapai kemerdekaan pada tahun 1957, kita masih belum mempunyai gaya seni bina nasional yang jelas. Apa yang ada pada waktu itu ialah seni bina rumah kampung tradisional dan telah menjadi inspirasi pertama Hijjas. Contohnya, rumah kampung Melayu terkenal dengan bumbung tinggi, dibina atas tiang dan mempunyai ruang seperti anjung untuk menyambut kehadiran tetamu. Elemen-elemen tradisional dan agama Islam tidak diterapkan secara bulat-bulat. Sebaliknya diolah menjadi sentuhan halus dan mempunyai maksud tersirat dalam setiap reka bentuknya. Menara Tabung Haji Menjadi Antara Karya Paling Ikonik Antara karya Hijjas yang paling dikenali ialah Menara Tabung Haji, siap sepenuhnya pada tahun 1984. Menara pejabat setinggi 37 tingkat mempunyai siluet dramatik, dengan bahagian sisi melengkung dan tirus menyerupai bentuk jam pasir. Pelan lantainya mempunyai bentuk bulat direka dengan lima tiang di bahagian sisi melambangkan Rukun Islam. Di samping itu, bangunan ini turut direka bagi menampung kemasukan jemaah haji setiap tahun, lengkap dengan ruang masuk kenderaan yang luas. Ia juga dibina sebelum kemunculan aplikasi perisian komputer (CAD) yang canggih menggabungkan lukisan tangan bagi setiap tingkat dengan teknik pembinaan pada zaman tersebut. Menara MBPJ Berdiri Megah Dalam Persekitarannya Satu lagi karya Hijjas yang menarik ialah Menara Majlis Bandaraya Petaling Jaya (MBPJ). Berbeza dengan bangunan lain, menara 27 tingkat ini mengutamakan sebuah dataran bandar yang luas dan kawasan membeli-belah di bahagian bawahnya. Dataran tersebut telah berhubung dengan kawasan pejalan kaki memudahkan orang untuk masuk ke dalam. Selain itu, bahagian menara turut berhubung dengan kawasan jalan sekeliling menerusi jambatan berbumbung. Reka bentuk bangunan ini cuba menyesuaikan diri dengan kawasan kedai-kedai di persekitarannya. Disebabkan itu, bangunan ini dihias bagi mengurangkan ketinggiannya dan melembutkan penampilannya secara semula jadi. Pusat Konvensyen Yang Menjadikan Kerongsang Sebagai Inspirasi Sering disebut sebagai antara karya Hijjas paling hebat ialah Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) yang dibina atas sebuah bukit di Putrajaya. Siap pada tahun 2003, bentuk bumbung yang menyerupai pending perak, iaitu kepala tali pinggang tradisional digunakan oleh golongan diraja Melayu. Malah, reka bentuk bangunan ini juga mesra alam dengan menggabungkan penggunaan cahaya siang secara semula jadi. Selain itu, ia turut menampilkan laluan lapan, bumbung tergantung untuk menyejukkan ruang di bawahnya. Hasilnya ialah sebuah permata seni bina yang sangat cantik di atas sebuah bukit hijau. Dedikasi terhadap seni bina dan peka kepada budaya tempatan bukan sahaja telah mengubah pemandangan ibu kota negara, malah mengajar kita untuk menghargai setiap satu bangunan yang telah wujud. title: 'Maybank Santuni 50 Warga Emas PAWE Kuala Kubu Bharu - Malaysiaaktif
body: 'Laporan/foto: Asmadi Ahmad/PAWE Kuala Kubu Bharu (Hulu Selangor) KUALA KUBU BHARU, 7 Sept (MalaysiaAktif) – Seramai 50 ahli Pusat Aktiviti Warga Emas (PAWE) Kuala Kubu Bharu menerima manfaat menerusi Program Maybank Global CR Day 2026 – Cahaya Kasih Challenge yang berlangsung di PAWE Kuala Kubu Bharu, kelmarin. Program anjuran Maybank Malaysia Berhad dengan kerjasama PAWE Kuala Kubu Bharu dan Pejabat Kebajikan Masyarakat Daerah Hulu Selangor itu turut menjadi platform bagi memperkukuh hubungan antara sektor korporat dengan komuniti setempat, khususnya dalam menyokong kesejahteraan golongan warga emas. Pengerusi PAWE Kuala Kubu Bharu Shamsul Akhyar Abdullah berkata program berkenaan bukan sekadar aktiviti tanggungjawab sosial korporat (CSR), malah mencerminkan keprihatinan dan penghargaan terhadap golongan warga emas. “Program seperti ini bukan sekadar satu aktiviti CSR, tetapi merupakan satu bentuk keprihatinan, penghargaan dan kasih sayang kepada golongan warga emas. “Inisiatif yang dilaksanakan Maybank membuktikan organisasi korporat bukan sahaja cemerlang dalam bidang perbankan, tetapi turut mempunyai jiwa dan tanggungjawab terhadap masyarakat,” katanya ketika berucap pada majlis berkenaan. Menurut beliau, penglibatan pihak korporat bersama warga emas turut memberi nilai tambah kepada usaha PAWE menyediakan ruang yang lebih aktif, sihat dan bermakna kepada ahlinya. Katanya, program seumpama itu bukan sahaja memberi manfaat dari aspek kemudahan dan aktiviti sosial, malah membuka ruang kepada warga emas untuk terus aktif, berinteraksi serta menjalani kehidupan yang lebih bermakna dalam komuniti. Program berkenaan dirasmikan oleh Ketua Penolong Pegawai Daerah merangkap Pengerusi Jawatankuasa Pembangunan Warga Emas Daerah Hulu Selangor, Mohamad Marwan Ahmad Tajuri. Turut hadir Ketua Perbankan Pengguna Maybank Sukhbir Singh, Ketua Prestasi Perniagaan dan Produktiviti, Zon Sri Damansara Khairulnizam Yusof serta Pengurus Cawangan Maybank Kuala Kubu Bharu Mohd Sabri Ahmad. Dalam perkembangan sama, Maybank turut menyumbangkan dua set kerusi batu marmar kepada PAWE Kuala Kubu Bharu untuk kegunaan ahli-ahli pusat berkenaan. Turut menjayakan program ialah Jawatankuasa Pembangunan Warga Emas Daerah Hulu Selangor, Pejabat Kebajikan Masyarakat Daerah Hulu Selangor, PAWE Kuala Kubu Bharu serta ketua-ketua komuniti setempat. -RI

title: 'Sebungkus nasi bahagi dua, duit poket hanya RM300
body: 'TUMPAT: “Setiap hari saya beli sebungkus nasi pada waktu tengah hari. Separuh saya simpan untuk makan malam sepanjang tiga minggu di Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM).” Demikian cerita Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah Sudin, 20, apabila ibu bapanya hanya mampu memberikan wang saku RM300 ketika menghantarnya ke USM di Pulau Pinang. Katanya, itu sahaja simpanan yang ada kerana telah membayar yuran pendaftaran sebanyak RM850 bagi mengikuti pengajian Sarjana Muda Pendidikan Khas. Katanya, yuran pengajian sebanyak RM1,232 belum dijelaskan meskipun sudah tiga minggu belajar di USM. “Jika ibu dapat pinjam dengan saudara-mara, dia akan kirim wang dalam masa terdekat untuk jelaskan yuran pengajian tersebut,” katanya menerusi panggilan video semasa kunjungan Ahli Majlis Presiden Gabungan Pelajar Melayu Semenanjung (GPMS), Che Muhammad Redzuan Jihad di rumahnya di Kampung Bunohan di sini. Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah berkata, dia rela mengikat perut kerana tidak mahu menyusahkan ibunya, Ramlah Abdul Rahman, 52, yang tidak dapat berjalan sejak empat tahun lalu selepas menjalani pembedahan kaki kiri akibat penyakit kencing manis. Katanya, demi membiayai pengajiannya, ibunya yang berkerusi roda gigih membuat kuih bersama bapanya, Sudin Matsan, 63. Bagi Ramlah, doanya sentiasa mengiringi Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah yang bercita-cita mahu menjadi seorang pendidik meskipun berdepan masalah kewangan. “Wang simpanan sudah habis digunakan untuk rawatan perubatan saya. “Walaupun menghadapi kekangan kewangan, saya tahu anak saya kuat semangat untuk menempuhnya,” katanya. Sementara itu, Che Muhammad Redzuan berkata, GPMS akan menyalurkan maklumat kepada Bahagian Hal Ehwal Pelajar (HEP) USM untuk membantu Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah termasuk wang saku, baki yuran dan sumbangan komputer riba. Sumbangan boleh disalurkan ke akaun CIMB 7657421192, Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah. – UTUSAN The post Sebungkus nasi bahagi dua, duit poket hanya RM300 appeared first on Utusan Malaysia.

body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 18 Sept - Belanjawan 2027 berkemungkinan menyaksikan pengecualian cukai jualan dan perkhidmatan (SST) diperluaskan bagi mengurangkan kos cukai yang terkandung dalam perbelanjaan perniagaan, selain kemungkinan pelepasan cukai pendapatan individu untuk pembayar cukai berpendapatan sederhana, menurut CIMB Securities. Firma penyelidikan itu berkata, kerajaan mempunyai ruang untuk memperluaskan pengecualian SST ke atas input berkaitan pengeluaran ketika perniagaan terus berdepan kos tenaga, logistik dan operasi lain yang tinggi. CIMB Securities turut menjangkakan pelepasan SST tambahan akan mengurangkan kutipan kerajaan kira-kira RM1 bilion, namun pertumbuhan asas masih dijangka meningkatkan hasil SST sebanyak 5.5% kepada RM72 bilion pada 2027. Berbeza dengan cukai barang dan perkhidmatan (GST), SST tidak mempunyai mekanisme kredit cukai input secara umum. Ini bermakna perniagaan mungkin perlu membayar cukai ke atas input tanpa dapat menolaknya daripada cukai yang dikenakan terhadap jualan mereka sendiri. Menurut CIMB Securities, keadaan itu boleh menyebabkan kos cukai terkumpul dan terkandung dalam harga di sepanjang rantaian bekalan. "Peluasan beberapa pengecualian terpilih berkemungkinan menjadi pilihan yang lebih segera dalam Belanjawan 2027, manakala mekanisme kredit cukai input yang lebih menyeluruh mungkin diperkenalkan mulai 2028 atau selepasnya berikutan keperluan menyediakan rangka kerja pentadbiran dan bayaran balik tambahan," kata firma itu dalam nota penyelidikan hari ini. Pelepasan cukai untuk golongan pertengahan Pada masa sama, CIMB Securities melihat terdapat ruang untuk kerajaan menawarkan pelepasan cukai pendapatan individu secara bersasar kepada pembayar cukai berpendapatan sederhana, khususnya isi rumah yang berdepan peningkatan kos sara hidup tetapi menerima bantuan tunai langsung yang lebih rendah. Sebagai gambaran, firma penyelidikan itu berkata, kadar cukai bagi pendapatan bercukai antara RM50,001 hingga RM70,000 dan RM70,001 hingga RM100,000 boleh dikurangkan masing-masing sebanyak satu mata peratusan kepada 10% dan 18%. Kategori cukai semasa pada kadar 25% juga boleh dipecahkan dengan kadar 24% dikenakan terhadap pendapatan bercukai antara RM100,001 hingga RM150,000. Pakej itu berpotensi memberikan penjimatan cukai tahunan sebanyak RM200 kepada individu dengan pendapatan bercukai RM70,000, RM500 bagi pendapatan bercukai RM100,000 dan sehingga RM1,000 kepada mereka yang mempunyai pendapatan bercukai RM150,000 dan ke atas, menurut anggaran CIMB Securities. Firma penyelidikan itu berkata, pakej berkenaan yang dikemukakan sebagai gambaran akan melibatkan kos kira-kira RM800 juta setahun kepada kerajaan. Defisit fiskal dijangka mengecil Secara keseluruhan, CIMB Securities menjangkakan Belanjawan 2027 terus menyediakan sokongan kepada isi rumah sambil mengekalkan usaha konsolidasi fiskal. Ia mengunjurkan defisit fiskal mengecil sedikit kepada 3.4% daripada keluaran dalam negara kasar (KDNK) pada 2027 berbanding anggaran 3.5% pada 2026. Firma penyelidikan itu turut menjangkakan bantuan tunai menerusi Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) dan Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) meningkat sebanyak RM2 bilion kepada RM17 bilion, yang sebahagiannya disokong oleh pengurangan perbelanjaan subsidi bahan api. CIMB Securities mengunjurkan subsidi petrol dan diesel berkurangan kepada RM32 bilion pada 2027 daripada RM41 bilion, sekali gus menyediakan ruang untuk meningkatkan bantuan isi rumah dan perbelanjaan pembangunan sambil memastikan kerajaan kekal pada landasan konsolidasi fiskal. Dibentangkan pada 9 Oktober Belanjawan 2027, yang merupakan Belanjawan MADANI kelima dan belanjawan kedua di bawah Rancangan Malaysia Ke-13 (RMK13), dijadualkan dibentangkan di Parlimen pada 9 Oktober 2026. Kementerian Kewangan berkata, belanjawan itu akan memberi tumpuan kepada beberapa bidang termasuk tekanan kos sara hidup, daya saing perniagaan dan produktiviti, di samping mengekalkan disiplin fiskal. — DagangNews.com

title: 'Bursa Malaysia pulih pada dagangan awal hari ini
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia meningkat semula untuk dibuka tinggi pada Jumaat didorong oleh hasil Perbendaharaan Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang rendah dan sentimen Rizab Persekutuan (Fed) yang berhati-hati memberikan kelegaan kepada pelabur. Pada 9.10 pagi, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 1.49 mata atau 0.09 peratus kepada 1,631.85 daripada 1,630.36 semasa ditutup pada Khamis. Indeks dibuka tinggi 3.51 mata kepada 1,633.87. Dalam pasaran secara menyeluruh, kaunter untung mengatasi kaunter rugi sebanyak 239 berbanding 137 manakala 270 kaunter tidak berubah, 2,127 tidak diniagakan dan 24 yang lain digantung. Jumlah dagangan sebanyak 173.94 juta saham bernilai RM95.98 juta. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, Thong Pak Leng, berkata penurunan terkini telah mendorong indeks kembali kepada keadaan terlebih jual, yang boleh menggalakkan aktiviti belian saham pada harga rendah. "Bagaimanapun, dengan situasi jualan asing yang dilaporkan, kami percaya sebarang peningkatan awal mungkin kekal sederhana. "Namun demikian, aliran penurunan membuka peluang untuk membeli secara terpilih saham yang mempunyai asas kukuh terutamanya dalam kalangan bank yang mapan, syarikat utiliti dan syarikat semikonduktor," katanya kepada Bernama. Pak Leng berkata, pemulihan yang lebih mampan memerlukan penyertaan yang lebih baik daripada kaunter saham wajaran tinggi dan peningkatan jumlah saham daripada pelbagai sektor. Oleh itu, beliau menjangka dagangan berhati-hati hari ini dalam julat 1,625 hingga 1,640. Dalam kalangan saham wajaran tinggi, Maybank mendatar pada RM9.95, Public Bank dan CIMB, masing-masing menurun satu sen kepada RM4.66 dan RM7.68, Tenaga Nasional naik empat sen kepada RM12.94 dan IHH Healthcare meningkat satu sen kepada RM7.71. Dalam dagangan aktif, Zetrix AI, Jaks Resources dan Genetec, masing-masing kekal tidak berubah pada 16.5 sen, 18 sen dan 32.5 sen, V.S Industry naik satu sen kepada 28 sen, bagaimanapun Kinergy Advancement menurun setengah sen kepada 39.5 sen. Kaunter paling untung ialah Malaysian Pacific Industries meningkat 58 sen kepada RM41.70, Hengyuan Refining naik 19 sen kepada RM3.83, Petronas Chemicals menokok 15 sen kepada RM4.28 serta UWC dan MI Technovation, masing-masing menambah 10 sen kepada RM7.20 dan RM5.36. Kaunter paling rugi termasuklah MISC menurun 14 sen kepada RM7.54, LPI Capital, Hong Leong Industries, MNRB dan RHB Bank, masing-masing merosot empat sen kepada RM12.80, RM16.10, RM2.78 dan RM7.43. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 meningkat 75.93 mata kepada 17,434.91, Indeks FBM Emas naik 17.18 mata kepada 12,160.71 dan Indeks FBM Top 100 menokok 21.58 mata kepada 11,954.73. Indeks FBM Emas Shariah menambah 34.76 mata kepada 12,047.77 dan Indeks FBM ACE naik 18.61 mata kepada 5,501.58. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk Perindustrian dan Perkhidmatan meningkat 1.10 mata kepada 178.83, Indeks Tenaga naik 9.45 mata kepada 844.46, Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan menurun 26.33 mata kepada 19,034.58 manakala Indeks Perladangan menokok 2.75 mata kepada 9,029.32. -BERNAMA

title: '债券收益率上升打击银行股 马银行9个月来首次跌破10令吉
body: '债券收益率上升打击银行股 马银行9个月来首次跌破10令吉 （吉隆坡1日讯）债券收益率上升，拖累银行股普遍下跌，而马银行（Malayan Banking Bhd）（KL:MAYBANK）股价更是近9个月来首次跌破10令吉。 收益率上升通常对银行不利，因为银行持有的债券价格下跌，导致更大的账面亏损，这会侵蚀资本，并迫使银行在出售时确认损失。银行还需要提高利率以吸引存款人，从而导致融资成本上升。 艾芬黄氏投资银行今日在报告中指出，这将影响银行的短期非利息收入以及资本比率。 马来西亚资产规模最大的银行马银行连续第三天下跌，收盘下跌0.4%，报9.95令吉。联昌国际集团（CIMB Group Holdings Bhd）（KL:CIMB）和丰隆银行（Hong Leong Bank Bhd）（KL:HLBANK）各跌逾1%。 大马交易所金融服务指数下跌至10个月以来的最低水平。 本月初，美联储3年来首次加息，导致马来西亚10年期基准国债收益率一度高达4.18%，之后有所回落。 越来越多经济学家预计，国家银行将在11月举行的年度最后一次货币政策评估会议上调高隔夜政策利率（OPR）。 艾芬黄氏指出，收益率上升通常会导致企业债券收益率上升，这也会与银行及其他企业的融资决策挂钩，进而影响银行的手续费收入。 根据该研究机构的分析，马银行和安联银行（Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd）（KL:ABMB）拥有最长的债券期限——即债券以现金流形式偿还本金所需的时间，同时也衡量了其对利率变动的敏感性。 与此同时，大众银行（Public Bank Bhd）（KL:PBBANK）和丰隆银行的期限最短。就资本充足率而言，马银行、兴业银行（RHB Bank Bhd）（KL:RHBBANK）和联昌国际集团的降幅可能最大，而大众银行和丰隆银行的降幅最小，因为它们的投资组合期限较短。 （编译：魏素雯） The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: 'Shamsul Iskandar mohon pasport dikembalikan untuk hadiri program luar negara
body: 'Kuala Lumpur: Bekas setiausaha politik kanan kepada perdana menteri, Datuk Seri Shamsul Iskandar Mohd Akin memohon untuk mendapatkan pasport antarabangsanya secara kekal bagi memudahkan beliau menghadiri beberapa program di luar negara. Pasport itu sebelum ini diserahkan kepada mahkamah sebagai syarat jaminan tambahan selepas beliau didakwa atas lima pertuduhan rasuah. Berdasarkan afidavit sokongan permohonan diperoleh media, Shamsul Iskandar berkata, permohonan tersebut adalah bagi membolehkan beliau melakukan perjalanan ke luar negara sebagai sebahagian daripada tugasnya dengan mudah. Shamsul Iskandar selaku pemohon berkata, dalam masa terdekat, beliau berhasrat untuk melakukan perjalanan ke Frankfurt, Jerman bagi menghadiri pesta buku bertajuk 'Frankfurt Book Fair' yang dianjurkan Rex Education, pada 7 Okt hingga 11 Nov ini. "Berdasarkan penglibatan saya dengan Akademi Kepimpinan Masyarakat Madani, penyertaan saya dalam pesta buku tersebut bertujuan untuk memupuk sinergi antara organisasi serta memberikan manfaat bersama kepada kedua-dua entiti. "Justeru, penyertaan ini akan bermanfaat bagi memperoleh pendedahan antarabangsa bagi menyokong serta mempertingkatkan inisiatif akar umbi yang sedang dijalankan bagi memperkasakan prinsip Masyarakat Madani, khususnya melalui promosi literasi, kepimpinan dan pemupukan ilmu," kata Shamsul Iskandar menerusi afidavit itu. Bagi lawatan di London, Shamsul Iskandar berkata, beliau mendaftar untuk Sidang Kemuncak AlBaraka ke-5 bertajuk Ethics in Action: Rebuilding Foundations and Advancing the Global Impact of the Islamic Economy' yang akan berlangsung dari 13 hingga 14 Okt ini. "Objektif utama sidang kemuncak tersebut adalah untuk memberi tumpuan kepada pengukuhan asas etika yang autentik bagi institusi kewangan Islam dan institusi bukan kewangan, sistem tadbir urus serta amalan pasaran," katanya dalam afidavit. Selain itu, Shamsul Iskandar berkata, beliau juga akan menghadiri program di Ireland serta Bosnia dan Herzegovina pada November dan Disember ini. Pada prosiding hari ini, peguam Yusmadi Yusoff yang mewakili Shamsul Iskandar memaklumkan kepada Hakim Mahkamah Sesyen Suzana Hussin bahawa selain permohonan bagi mendapatkan pasport secara kekal yang difailkan 30 Sept lalu, anak guamnya juga memohon agar pasport diserahkan secara sementara bagi membolehkan beliau menghadiri program di Frankfurt dan London bulan ini. Timbalan Pendakwa Raya Julaila Jamaludin yang membantah permohonan Shamsul Iskandar untuk mendapatkan pasport secara kekal berkata, dokumen dikemukakan dalam permohonan tersebut hanya berupa surat jemputan dan terdapat perbincangan yang boleh dijalankan secara dalam talian. Bagaimanapun, Julaila tidak membantah permohonan Shamsul Iskandar untuk mendapatkan pasport secara sementara. Hakim Suzana kemudian membenarkan permohonan Shamsul Iskandar untuk mendapatkan pasport secara sementara bermula hari ini dan perlu diserahkan semula kepada mahkamah pada atau sebelum 16 Okt ini. Selain itu, mahkamah memerintahkan pihak pendakwaan memfailkan afidavit balasan terhadap permohonan Shamsul Iskandar bagi mendapatkan pasport secara kekal pada atau sebelum 19 Okt ini dan menetapkan keputusan terhadap permohonan itu pada 8 Dis ini. Shamsul Iskandar, 51, didakwa atas dua pertuduhan bersetuju menerima suapan untuk dirinya, iaitu wang tunai RM140,000 daripada ahli perniagaan Tei Jiann Cheing atau turut dikenali sebagai Albert Tei sebagai dorongan membantu syarikat milik Tei untuk mendapatkan kelulusan lesen penerokaan mineral di Sabah. Dia turut didakwa atas dua lagi pertuduhan iaitu memperoleh untuk dirinya satu suapan berupa kelengkapan perabot dan barangan elektrik bernilai RM14,580.03 dan RM22,249 daripada individu sama bagi tujuan sama. Kesalahan itu didakwa dilakukan di premis di Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya; di tempat letak kereta sebuah hotel di Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin di sini; serta di Jalan P14A 1/1, Presint 14, Putrajaya, antara 7 Dis 2023 hingga 31 Jan 2024, serta antara 24 Nov 2023 hingga 5 Mac 2024. Shamsul Iskandar turut didakwa atas satu pertuduhan memperoleh suapan berjumlah RM64,924 yang dimasukkan ke dalam akaun CIMB Bank milik Rahmalidya Buyong bagi tujuan pembayaran penyewaan sebuah rumah di Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, di sini daripada Tei bagi membantu syarikat milik Tei untuk mendapatkan kelulusan lesen penerokaan mineral di Sabah. Kesemua pertuduhan dikemukakan mengikut Seksyen 17(a) Akta Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia 2009 (Akta 694) dan boleh dihukum di bawah Seksyen 24(1) akta sama, yang memperuntukkan hukuman penjara maksimum 20 tahun serta denda tidak kurang lima kali ganda jumlah atau nilai suapan, atau RM10,000, mengikut mana lebih tinggi, jika sabit kesalahan.

title: 'HLB Islamic Berjaya Lonjak Pendapatan Usahawan Berpendapatan Rendah Langkawi Sebanyak 94%
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, 23 SEPTEMBER 2026 – Selaras dengan komitmen untuk memperkasakan ekosistem perantaraan berasaskan nilai (“Value-based Intermediation” atau “VBI”), HLB Islamic (atau “Bank”) telah menyalurkan pembiayaan sebanyak RM138,600 kepada perusahaan sosial SURI Inspirasi (“SURI”) di bawah kerangka iTEKAD Bank Negara Malaysia (“BNM”). Inisiatif ini secara langsung menyumbang kepada peningkatan purata pendapatan bulanan sebanyak 94% serta menjana jumlah pendapatan baharu melebihi RM14,000 bagi usahawan yang menyertai program “Sustainable Reliable Income” (“SRI”) anjuran SURI. HLB Islamic Tingkatkan Pendapatan Usahawan Sebanyak 94% Melalui Program SRI Program SRI memperkasakan komuniti berpendapatan rendah untuk mengitar semula sisa fabrik menjadi barangan fesyen yang unik, yang secara langsung mewujudkan peluang pekerjaan dan memupuk semangat keusahawanan di samping mempromosikan fesyen sifar sisa serta pemerkasaan komuniti. Usahawan yang terlibat, yang majoriti ibu tunggal berpendapatan rendah, telah menghasilkan 1,000 pasang pakaian seragam sekolah untuk pelajar bagi lima buah sekolah di Langkawi, sekali gus menjana penjimatan sebanyak RM30,000 bagi keluarga tempatan. HLB Islamic meraikan pencapaian ini menerusi penyerahan mesin jahit berkualiti tinggi kepada para usahawan yang terlibat, menandakan peralihan daripada pembelajaran di dalam bilik darjah kepada pemilikan perniagaan secara aktif. Menurut Dafinah Ahmed Hilmi, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif HLB Islamic, “Visi kami mengenai pengurusan kewangan berteraskan Hayat @ HLB Islamic, di mana pengurusan harta dilihat sebagai satu perjalanan yang bermula dengan Penciptaan Harta. Melalui kerjasama dengan SURI, kami menyediakan alat dan latihan asas yang diperlukan oleh komuniti untuk mencungkil potensi keusahawanan mereka. Kami berharap usaha ini akan menjadi pemangkin kepada perjalanan pembinaan kekayaan berterusan ke arah kebebasan kewangan yang bakal memperkayakan komuniti untuk generasi akan datang.” Kejayaan ini menandakan satu pencapaian penting dalam kerjasama berterusan antara HLB Islamic dan SURI, yang mula menyertai ekosistem Bank ini sebagai peserta inisiatif HLB Jumpstart. Diperkenalkan bagi memupuk perusahaan sosial Malaysia yang berimpak tinggi menerusi bimbingan komersial, penjenamaan, serta pembinaan kapasiti digital, HLB Jumpstart telah menyediakan kerangka awal kepada SURI untuk memperluas operasinya. Hal ini membuktikan strategi jangka panjang Bank dalam memupuk usaha sosial menjadi rakan pelaksana berdikari yang mampu memberikan impak yang lebih meluas. title: 'FBM KLCI charts slight gain at midday
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's benchmark index lagged enthusiasm, weighed down by persistent fears over geopolitical risk, inflation risks and a weak sentiment for equities. At noon, the FBM KLCI was up 1.84 points to 1,632.71, with heavyweight banks helping to shore up the market. AMMB rose 11 sen to RM6.50, Hong Leong Bank jumped 26 sen to RM22.90 and Public Bank was up three sen to RM7.46. On the broader market, the sentiment remained weak with 560 decliners compared to 477 gainers. There were 2.93 billion shares traded for a value of RM1.39bil. The technology sector was the biggest gainer, jumping 1.69%, while financial services rose 0.4% Telcos dove 2.12%, utilities dropped 0.51%, property shed 0.43% and energy slid 0.37%. Meanwhile, Zetrix AI continued its fall after the trading halt was lifted at 10am. The share hit limit down after falling 3.5 sen to eight sen, after news broke last Friday it owed over RM200mil in collections. VS Industry rose four sen to 33 sen and Cuscapi slid 0.5 sne ot 4.5 sen. In regional markets, Japan's Nikkei was up 2.08% to 69,730 while South Korea's Kospi gained 0.46% to 7,003. China's Shanghai Composite index added 0.31% to 3,842. Hong Kong's Hang Seng was nearly flat at 23,952.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Opens Lower On Higher US Yields, West Asia Tensions
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 – Bursa Malaysia opened lower on Thursday morning, tracking a mixed overnight performance on Wall Street as rising US Treasury yields and persistent geopolitical tensions in West Asia dampened investor appetite. At 9:10 AM, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 3.74 points, or 0.22 per cent, to 1,647.43 compared to Wednesday’s closing level of 1,651.17. The key index opened 1.30 points lower at 1,649.87. Market breadth across the broader market was negative, with decliners outpacing gainers 200 to 142, while 307 counters traded unchanged, 2,124 untraded, and 12 suspended. Early turnover reached 246.59 million shares valued at RM118.14 million. Heavyweights and Active Counters Financial and utility heavyweights dragged on the benchmark index during early trade: - Public Bank fell 3 sen to RM4.67. - Tenaga Nasional lost 2 sen to RM12.94. - CIMB shed 1 sen to RM7.78. - Maybank and IHH Healthcare traded flat at RM9.90 and RM7.83, respectively. In active trading, ACE Market debutant GB Bond fell half a sen to 24.5 sen, while VS Industry traded unchanged at 28 sen. Divfex gained 2 sen to 11 sen, Jaks Resources rose 1 sen to 21.5 sen, and Astro Malaysia added half a sen to 6 sen. Energy and consumer-linked stocks featured among the top gainers: - Keck Seng advanced 11 sen to RM5.14. - Petron Malaysia picked up 7 sen to RM3.47. - Hengyuan Refining and Spritzer each rose 6 sen to RM3.62 and RM3.67, respectively. - Jati Tinggi gained 5 sen to RM1.44. title: 'CIMB Bank wins big at Euromoney Awards
body: 'PETALING JAYA: CIMB Bank Bhd and CIMB Investment Bank have won top accolades at the Euromoney Awards for Excellence 2026, taking home top honours as Malaysia’s Best Retail Bank, Malaysia’s Best Digital Bank for SMEs, and Malaysia’s Best Investment Bank. The bank said in a statement that the awards reflected the ongoing focus on providing customer-centric solutions through innovation, digital capabilities and deep market expertise across its retail, small and medium enterprise (SME), and investment banking businesses. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd group chief executive officer Novan Amirudin commented that the recognitions are a testament to the trust of the group’s customers and the dedication of its teams. “They reaffirm CIMB’s purpose of advancing customers and society by making financial solutions more accessible, relevant and impactful for the people and businesses we serve,” he added. “As their needs continue to evolve, we remain committed to being a trusted partner supporting individuals in realising their aspirations and helping businesses achieve their growth ambitions through meaningful and lasting value creation.” CIMB’s latest wins come amid the bank’s continued efforts to empower customers through accessible, inclusive and purpose-driven financial solutions. In retail banking, it has been working to deepen its franchise through personalisation offerings, digitally enabled journeys, and stronger engagement across segments. The bank said revenue and profitability had advanced during the year, underpinned by market share gains in auto finance, credit cards and retail deposits, on top of progress in digital sales and customer cross-sell. It also continued to strengthen wealth proposition through differentiated investment solutions, broader product diversity, chief investment office-led advisory capabilities and enhanced digital wealth platform, with particular momentum seen in the “Preferred” affluent segment as it expands its advisory-led and relationship-based wealth capabilities. Meanwhile, the bank has continued to advance its SME services, having launched the CIMB OCTO Biz digital banking platform, which has amassed more than 280,000 customers to date. Additionally, it has expanded financing access through embedded merchant financing with TNG eWallet and its flexible financing through its SME FlexiCash. Beyond this, CIMB Investment Bank in 2025 secured the top ranking in Malaysian equity and debt capital markets by deal value and share of wallet, as well as the highest position in Asean equity and debt capital markets by deal value, cementing its position both locally and regionally.

title: 'Maybank upgrades MAE Malware Shielding to detect more security risks
body: 'Maybank is rolling out an enhanced version of its Malware Shielding feature on the MAE app, which can now detect a wider range of potential security risks on users’ devices. As part of the update, MAE users will also be required to review and agree to a new set of Malware Shielding Terms & Conditions before they can continue using the app  The upgraded feature started rolling out progressively on 26 September 2026 with MAE app version 0.9.51, so don’t be surprised if the update hasn’t reached your phone just yet. Once updated, you’ll be prompted to review and agree to the new terms before you can continue using the app. By tapping ‘Agree’, you’re acknowledging that Malware Shielding will check your device for potential malware and risky security settings every time you launch MAE.  So what exactly is it looking out for? According to Maybank, Malware Shielding can detect malicious apps that may intercept authentication codes, remotely control your device or steal banking credentials. It also checks for unsafe device configurations, including Developer Mode, rooted or jailbroken devices, emulators and cloned environments.  The feature can also detect active screen sharing, recording, mirroring and overlay apps, as well as VPN services and untrusted keyboard apps. On top of that, it checks whether the MAE app itself has been modified or tampered with.  As for privacy, Maybank says Malware Shielding does not access, collect, process or store any personal information from the apps installed on your device. The bank also says your banking information and personal data remain confidential and protected.

title: 'MACC Remands Corporate Brothers in RM10m Investment Probe, Seizes 15 Luxury Cars Among Others
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Two corporate figures, who are brothers, are being remanded for five days over an alleged abuse of position involving an investment of about RM10 million. The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) obtained the remand order, effective from Thursday until next Monday (Oct 5), from Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court on Thursday morning. According to a source, the two men, in their 40s and 50s and carrying the titles of Datuk Seri and Datuk Wira respectively, were detained at about 9pm on Wednesday after giving their statements at the MACC headquarters here. Initial investigations found that the duo were suspected of acting in collusion in the alleged offence in late 2020. “They are also believed to have colluded with an officer of an education-based foundation to approve an investment of about RM10 million in an investment company owned by the elder brother,” the source told Bernama. The MACC also seized 15 luxury cars, 12 high-powered motorcycles, five luxury watches, three bracelets and about RM30,000 in cash. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the matter when contacted and said the case is being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009. title: 'Apa yang mesti berubah sebelum pelajar lain dicederakan?/ What must change before another child is hurt?
body: '[ENGLISH VERSION BELOW] Kematian Muhammad ldlan Fareeq Shahril, 14 tahun, meninggalkan sebuah keluarga dalam kesedihan dan ibu bapa di seluruh Malaysia dengan satu pertanyaan yang amat membimbangkan: adakah anak saya selamat di asrama sekolah? Bagi pihak Children’s Protection Society Malaysia (CPSM), saya merakamkan ucapan takziah yang sedalam-dalamnya kepada ibu bapa dan keluarga Muhammad ldlan. Tiada kata-kata yang dapat meringankan kehilangan mereka. Mereka berhak mendapat ruang untuk berduka, dan jawapan yang benar serta keadilan. Kami mengambil maklum bahawa Menteri Pendidikan Fadhlina Sidek telah bertemu dengan keluarga dan warga sekolah serta mengarahkan audit segera. Kami menyambut baik jaminan beliau bahawa tiada sesiapa akan dilindungi sekiranya salah laku terbukti. Polis mesti diberi ruang untuk menentukan fakta, termasuk punca dan keadaan yang membawa kepada kematian Muhammad ldlan. Dakwaan tidak boleh dianggap sebagai dapatan, dan pelajar yang terlibat tidak wajar dihakimi oleh masyarakat sebelum siasatan selesai. Namun, siasatan terhadap satu kejadian tidak boleh menjadi noktah kepada perkara ini. Audit tersebut perlu menjawab soalan yang lebih sukar: adakah terdapat kebimbangan yang timbul sebelum kematian Muhammad ldlan, dan adakah pihak asrama mempunyai cara yang berkesan untuk mengenal pasti serta menanganinya? Soalan ini perlu diteliti tanpa membuat andaian tentang apa yang berlaku dalam kes ini. Apabila seorang pelajar tinggal di asrama, pihak sekolah memikul tanggungjawab menjaganya pada waktu ibu bapanya tidak dapat melihat keadaannya sendiri. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Tanggungjawab itu melangkaui daftar penghuni dan peraturan yang ditampal pada papan kenyataan semata-mata. la memerlukan orang dewasa yang mengenali pelajar, menyedari perubahan tingkah laku, mengambil tindakan apabila kebimbangan dibangkitkan dan bertanggungjawab terhadap keselamatan mereka selepas waktu persekolahan. Tiada pelajar berhak menguatkuasakan disiplin dengan kekerasan. Jika seorang pelajar disyaki melanggar peraturan, sama ada berkaitan dengan vape, barang yang hilang, sikap tidak menghormati orang lain atau apa-apa perkara sekalipun, urusan itu mesti dikendalikan oleh orang dewasa yang bertanggungjawab. Pelajar tidak boleh ditampar, dipukul, ditahan secara paksa, diugut atau dikenakan hukuman yang dikendalikan oleh pelajar lain. Sesiapa yang melihat sesuatu masalah hendaklah melaporkannya kepada warden atau guru disiplin. Tiada tempat bagi pelajar yang melantik diri mereka sendiri sebagai penguat kuasa di dormitori, asrama atau sekolah. Oleh itu, CPSM menyeru Kementerian Pendidikan supaya menggunakan audit semasa sebagai permulaan kepada semakan keselamatan asrama yang jelas dan mempunyai tempoh pelaksanaan yang ditetapkan. Semakan itu perlu merangkumi perkara berikut. Pertama, teliti sama ada tanda amaran terlepas pandang. Penyiasat dan pasukan audit perlu meneliti aduan terdahulu, laporan tidak rasmi, permintaan untuk bertukar bilik, kecederaan yang tidak dapat dijelaskan, ketidakhadiran, perubahan tingkah laku dan kebimbangan yang dibangkitkan oleh ibu bapa, sekiranya maklumat tersebut wujud. Mereka perlu mengenal pasti siapa yang menerima setiap maklumat, tindakan yang diambil dan sama ada keadaan pelajar berkenaan disusuli. Jika tiada aduan direkodkan, hal itu perlu dinilai secara bersama satu lagi persoalan: adakah pelajar mempunyai saluran yang selamat dan boleh dipercayai untuk bersuara? Kedua, pastikan penyeliaan orang dewasa ada pada waktu dan tempat pelajar memerlukannya. Warden sukar menjalankan pengawasan yang rapi jika mereka perlu menjaga terlalu ramai pelajar, beberapa bangunan atau terlalu banyak tugas serentak. Kementerian perlu menyemak jumlah petugas asrama, liputan pada waktu malam, serah tugas dan tatacara mendapatkan bantuan apabila sesuatu kejadian berlaku. Setiap asrama perlu mempunyai petugas yang jelas dikenalpasti sedang bertugas, pengganti apabila petugas tersebut tiada, serta rekod kebimbangan yang dibangkitkan dan tindakan yang diambil yang disimpan dengan selamat. Ketiga, sediakan saluran aduan yang diyakini pelajar. Seorang pelajar perlu boleh bercakap secara sulit dengan lebih daripada seorang petugas yang ditetapkan, termasuk seseorang di luar rantaian pengurusan harian asrama. lbu bapa juga mesti tahu siapa yang boleh dihubungi. Laporan mengenai keganasan atau ugutan perlu mendapat respons segera, penilaian terhadap keselamatan pelajar, perlindungan daripada tindakan balas dan tindakan susulan. Pelajar perlu diberitahu dengan jelas bahawa melaporkan perbuatan yang memudaratkan orang lain ialah tindakan berani, bukannya perbuatan tidak setia kepada rakan. Keempat, fahami keperluan setiap pelajar apabila mereka mula tinggal di asrama. Pihak sekolah perlu berbincang dengan pelajar dan ibu bapa tentang penyesuaian kepada kehidupan berasrama, sebarang kebimbangan keselamatan yang pernah timbul, dan sokongan yang mungkin diperlukan. Jika sesuatu kebimbangan memerlukan penilaian lanjut, profesional yang berkelayakan perlu dilibatkan. Maklumat yang diperoleh mesti dirahsiakan dan digunakan untuk merancang sokongan serta penyeliaan yang sesuai, bukan untuk melabel seorang pelajar atau menafikan aksesnya kepada pendidikan berdasarkan andaian yang belum diuji. Kelima, jadikan larangan terhadap keganasan suatu amalan yang benar-benar dilaksanakan. Pengetua, warden, guru disiplin, kaunselor dan, jika berkaitan, ustaz atau pendidik agama lain perlu menyampaikan mesej yang sama secara konsisten. Perhimpunan mingguan dan pertemuan di asrama boleh digunakan untuk membincangkan batas pergaulan, tekanan rakan sebaya, cara menegur dengan hormat dan cara mendapatkan bantuan. Toleransi sitar terhadap keganasan mesti diterjemahkan melalui tindakan yang konsisten: setiap laporan diambil serius, pelajar yang terlibat dilindungi, fakta ditentukan dan tindakan diambil secara adil. Arahan kepada pelajar mesti jelas: jangan gunakan kekerasan terhadap pelajar lain; laporkan masalah kepada orang dewasa; dan jika melihat kejadian yang membahayakan seseorang, dapatkan bantuan dengan segera tanpa meletakkan diri sendiri dalam bahaya. Keenam, laksanakan langkah keselamatan yang praktikal. Kementerian perlu menyemak peraturan keselamatan di asrama sekolah dan mengenal pasti kawasan bersama yang sesuai untuk pemantauan CCTV, dengan keutamaan kepada tempat yang mungkin mendedahkan pelajar kepada risiko apabila penyeliaan orang dewasa terhad. Penggunaan kamera mesti menghormati privasi pelajar dan tidak boleh menggantikan kehadiran orang dewasa yang peka. Setiap sistem perlu mempunyai petugas yang bertanggungjawab memastikan ia berfungsi, bertindak apabila kejadian dilaporkan dan menyimpan rakaman berkaitan sebelum rakaman itu terpadam secara automatik. Akses kepada rakaman hendaklah dihadkan dan direkodkan, manakala rakaman yang relevan perlu diserahkan segera kepada penyiasat melalui saluran yang betul dengan perlindungan terhadap identiti pelajar yang dirakam. Kebertanggungjawaban mesti melangkaui kes ini. Persoalan yang timbul daripada kematian ini mesti membawa kepada tindakan yang dapat dilihat oleh ibu bapa dan pelajar. Kementerian perlu menerbitkan dapatan utama audit sebaik sahaja hal itu dapat dilakukan tanpa menjejaskan siasatan polis atau privasi pelajar yang terlibat. title: 'Giggs warns Asean nations naturalised players not quick fix
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Manchester United icon Ryan Giggs has urged Southeast Asian nations not to treat naturalised and dual-heritage players as a shortcut to success. Giggs cautioned that strong domestic academy pipelines must anchor sustainable progress in football. Speaking to reporters in the capital, the 13-time Premier League winner addressed the accelerating trend across the region, where nations including Malaysia and Indonesia have increasingly turned to foreign-born and heritage players to fast-track competitiveness on the continental stage. Giggs, himself a celebrated graduate of United's famed "Class of '92" youth system, offered his take on the debate and said that while outside talent can raise immediate standards, it should never come at the expense of grassroots development. "I think everything is always a balance," Giggs said when asked if relying on naturalised players is a sound strategy for lower-ranked nations looking to climb the ladder. "Where it's countries or leagues outside the big leagues, you need the infrastructure of academy players coming through. "And also, the foreign players coming in, they need to be good quality, good professionals." The 53-year-old former Wales manager also pointed out the critical role of coaching in bridging the developmental gap, noting that importing tactical expertise must serve to elevate local coaching standards rather than displace them. "The coaching, if possible, I think should be local," he said. "But obviously, if you bring in experienced coaches from other countries, they can also help show the professionalism and introduce different tactical ideas. "It's always a balance. But I think for any country, it's always good if you have your own players coming through from an early age, though of course, they have to be good enough." Beyond regional football development, Giggs reflected on his long-standing ties with Malaysia, describing the country as an indispensable commercial partner for English football giants. "Oh, it's very important," he said. "If I look at Man United, I've worked with Maybank, I've worked with Malaysia Airlines, and events like this boost the spotlight on the country." Decades after making his senior debut, Giggs admitted he remains touched by the enduring enthusiasm of Malaysian supporters, who still flock to greet him at airport arrivals halls. "If you speak to anyone who's been here, whether during pre-season or after they finish playing, they love it," he said. "They love the people, they love the culture, and they love the food, even if sometimes it can be a bit too spicy for the UK! But no, I love it, and I always love coming back."

"But obviously, if you bring in experienced coaches from other countries, they can also help show the professionalism and introduce different tactical ideas. "It's always a balance. But I think for any country, it's always good if you have your own players coming through from an early age, though of course, they have to be good enough." "Oh, it's very important," he said. "If I look at Man United, I've worked with Maybank, I've worked with Malaysia Airlines, and events like this boost the spotlight on the country." "If you speak to anyone who's been here, whether during pre-season or after they finish playing, they love it," he said. "They love the people, they love the culture, and they love the food, even if sometimes it can be a bit too spicy for the UK! But no, I love it, and I always love coming back."

title: 'Sektor teknologi dan industri jadi tumpuan selepas FBM KLCI diperluas kepada 50 kaunter - CIMB Securities | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 8 Sept — Sektor teknologi dan perindustrian berpotensi meraih banyak perhatian pelabur selepas indeks penanda aras FBM KLCI diperluas daripada 30 kepada 50 kaunter, serta mengurangkan dominasi sektor kewangan dan utiliti dalam indeks utama Bursa Malaysia, menurut CIMB Securities. Firma penyelidikan itu berkata pertambahan tersebut dijangka meningkatkan kepelbagaian sektor dengan memberikan bahagian perwakilan yang lebih besar kepada sektor perindustrian, teknologi, barangan pengguna pilihan, tenaga, hartanah dan barangan pengguna asas. Perubahan tersebut dilihat positif dari sudut struktur pasaran kerana FBM KLCI yang lebih pelbagai berpeluang menjadi penanda aras mencerminkan keseluruhan ekonomi Malaysia, selain meluaskan pilihan pendedahan pelabur institusi di luar kelompok syarikat bermodal besar sedia ada. "Simulasi terdahulu dilaksanakan kami menganggarkan 20 kaunter baharu itu boleh mewakili kira-kira 15.6% daripada FBM KLCI yang diperluaskan apabila penyertaan penuh dicapai," jelas CIMB Securities dalam nota analisisnya. Menurut firma berkenaan lagi, perluasan tersebut dijangka mengurangkan pemberat sektor kewangan dan utiliti, manakala sektor teknologi serta perindustrian antara segmen yang dilihat sebagai berpotensi mendapat perwakilan lebih besar dalam indeks berkenaan. Bagaimanapun ujarnya, impak aliran dana dalam tempoh terdekat dijangka lebih bersifat khusus kepada kaunter tertentu berbanding keseluruhan pasaran, memandangkan saiz aset di bawah pengurusan pasif yang menjejaki FBM KLCI masih relatif kecil. Kesan tersebut juga kata CIMB Securities, tidak akan berlaku secara mendadak kerana kemasukan kaunter baharu bakal dilaksanakan secara berperingkat, iaitu kira-kira 50% pada Disember 2026 sebelum mencapai penyertaan penuh 100% pada Jun 2027. "Pihak pengurusan FTSE sendiri sudah menjelaskan bahawa permodalan pasaran penuh akan digunakan bagi menentukan pemilihan akhir kaunter, manakala kaedah 'free float' atau pengapungan bebas akan menentukan pemberat setiap saham dalam indeks," tambahnya. Dalam perkembangan berkaitan, FBM70 akan dikurangkan kepada 50 kaunter dan dinamakan semula sebagai FBM Mid Cap Index mulai 21 Disember 2026, sementara FBM100 masih lagi dikekalkan tanpa sebarang perubahan jumlah kaunter didagangkan. Spesifikasi derivatif juga jelas CIMB Securities, adalahtidak berubah, manakala FTSE Russell sedang mengkaji kemungkinan untuk melonggarkan ambang kemasukan pantas bagi tawaran awam permulaan (IPO) yang bermodal saiz besar. Justeru, firma penyelidikan tersebut menjangkakan butiran lanjut mengenai perubahan struktur itu akan dimasukkan dalam kemas kini 'FTSE Bursa Malaysia Index Series Ground Rules' selepas dimuktamadkan pada akhir September 2026. Secara keseluruhan, ia kekal positif kerana perluasan itu berpotensi menjadikan FBM KLCI lebih pelbagai, sekali gus memberi ruang lebih besar kepada sektor teknologi dan industri dalam penanda aras utama pasaran saham Malaysia.

title: 'Smoky Singapore gears up to talk money ahead of F1
body:
'

SINGAPORE (Oct 5): Regional, business, cryptocurrency and sports leaders are meeting in Singapore for a slew of finance-focused conferences ahead of this weekend's Grand Prix as haze continues to shroud the city state.

Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, famed investor Ray Dalio and Eric Trump, a co-founder of the family-backed cryptocurrency business, are expected, while hundreds of thousands of Formula One (F1) fans will converge on the island.

The night race through the city streets and some 40 sideline events are typically a global showcase for Singapore and hotel room rates have soared.

The Fullerton Bay Hotel next to the race track is charging S$5,030 (US$3,933 or RM16,054) a night for a room that typically costs US$1,460.

This year, the pall from Indonesia's most intense fires in more than a decade will probably form part of the backdrop. Air quality was forecast at the "high moderate to low unhealthy" range on Monday by Singapore's environment agency. No longer-range forecast was provided for Sunday's Grand Prix.

Singapore's tourism board said F1 and its surrounding events had "strong momentum" reflecting confidence despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty.

Jitters in financial markets where bond prices are slumping and sentiment around artificial intelligence is shifting from euphoric to cautious will occupy investors and business chiefs at the Forbes Global CEO Conference and Milken Asia Summit, which runs from Wednesday.

Trump, a co-founder of crypto venture World Liberty Financial, is due to speak at the TOKEN2049 cryptocurrency event with digital asset markets fragile following a bruising 12 months.

A hoped-for regulatory framework failed last month to clear the US Senate, in part as President Donald Trump's personal crypto dealings ​became a flashpoint for Democrats.

Despite a recent bounce, the total value of the cryptocurrency market is down about a quarter over the last 12 months to US$3 trillion, according to data aggregator CoinGecko.

Still, organisers say their event is nearly sold out with 25,000 attendees expected, the same as last year. The Straits Times reported that about 90,000 "c-suite", or top-ranking, executives will be in town.

F1 generates around S$145 million in incremental tourism receipts for Singapore each year, according to official estimates. Maybank economist Chua Hak Bin expects it to hit S$160 million this year, along with "wider economic benefits" from deals struck at sideline events.

title: 'Maybank Group Sustainability Week 2026 advances net zero ambitions through capacity building and collective action | Maybank
body: 'In its third year, MGSW 2026 recognised over 1000 certified sustainability practitioners & continues to inspire greater net zero action across the Group Maybank recently organised the Maybank Group Sustainability Week (MGSW) 2026, a three-day sustainability-focused programme held from 21 to 23 September 2026 at Menara Merdeka Maybank. Under the theme “Net Zero. From Commitment to Action”, MGSW 2026 focuses on advancing Maybank’s net zero journey through capacity building, deepening sustainability awareness and strengthening capabilities, in line with the Group’s ROAR30 sustainability ambitions. MGSW 2026 saw Maybankers across the Group participate in two key events; ‘Net Zero Week’, which featured a series of learning, engagement and experiential activities, and the ‘Maybank Sustainability Practitioner Certification (MSPC) Open Day’ and ‘Grand Conferment Ceremony’, which celebrated over 1,000 certified sustainability practitioners and inspiring Maybankers to advance in their sustainability journey. The event saw the attendance of Dato' Sri Khairussaleh Ramli, President & Group CEO Maybank, Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Group Chief Sustainability Officer Maybank, Board of Directors and Group EXCO members of Maybank, Dato’ Ir. Ts. (Dr.) Izwan Hasli Mohd Ibrahim, CEO PNB Merdeka Ventures, Muazzam Mohamad, Head of Corporate Sustainability & Stewardship PNB, Leo Pui Yong, Chief Sustainability Officer Tenaga Nasional Berhad and Edey Suresh Kumar Manikam, Board Director at Large UN Global Compact Network Malaysia, Brunei & Cambodia (UNGCMBC). Dato' Sri Khairussaleh Ramli said “As we advance in our sustainability journey, MGSW 2026 reflects our continued focus on enabling our people to support our customers' transition journeys to net zero through stronger knowledge and mindsets. Ultimately, our commitment to capacity building will in turn help our customers transition responsibly and sustainably, strengthen our communities and drive meaningful sustainability impact.” A key highlight of MGSW 2026 was the MSPC Grand Conferment Ceremony, which honoured 36 MSPC Level 3 Red Belt graduates from across the Group for their achievements and continued commitment in sustainability. Developed in partnership with UNGCMBC, the MSPC programme was introduced in 2023 with the vision of building a future-ready sustainability workforce. Through its four-tier certification pathway comprising Level 1 White, Level 2 Green, Level 3 Red and Level 4 Black Belt levels, the programme combines sustainability knowledge with practical application to equip Maybankers with the capabilities needed to drive sustainability initiatives across the organisation. Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli, President & Group CEO Maybank (Center in blue batik), Dato’ Ir. Ts. (Dr.) Izwan Hasli Mohd Ibrahim, CEO PNB Merdeka Ventures (In red tie) and Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Group Chief Sustainability Officer Maybank (In black blazer with glasses) posing with the MSPC Level 1 White Belt recipients at the MSPC Grand Conferment ceremony during the MGSW 2026. As the entry level of the MSPC programme, the certification equips Maybankers with the foundational knowledge and capabilities needed to drive sustainability initiatives across the Group. A key highlight of the MSPC ceremony was the recognition of the 36 MSPC Level 3 Red Belt graduates from across the Group. Since its inception, MSPC has grown into a network of sustainability practitioners across the Group, spanning more than 60 cohorts and expands beyond Malaysia to Singapore, Indonesia, the Philippines and Cambodia. To date, the programme has enrolled more than 2,300 participants and certified 1,755 practitioners. Maybankers came together throughout the three-day MGSW 2026 to learn, engage and take action on sustainability through a diverse range of interactive workshops, experiential activities, sharing sessions and challenges, reflecting the Group’s commitment to advancing its net zero journey under the theme “Net Zero. From Commitment to Action.” As a pioneering initiative and a first of its kind in the industry, MSPC is a sustainability capability programme built on a structured belting system, demonstrating how a financial institution can systematically empower its people with the knowledge, skills and credibility needed to deliver sustainable impact. Maybankers participated in a weaving activity at the Women Eco Weavers booth by Maybank Foundation during the MGSW 2026, transforming used fabric into handcrafted products while promoting how traditional craftsmanship can support waste reduction and sustainable livelihood. “The MSPC ceremony marks another significant milestone in our journey towards becoming the sustainability leader in ASEAN as it is ultimately a celebration of our people. It recognises Maybankers who have committed themselves to developing the knowledge and skills needed to advance our sustainability ambitions. It also reflects how far we have progressed, from building awareness and advocacy to strengthening action and accountability across the Group.” said Dato' Sri Khairussaleh Ramli. MGSW 2026 also saw the launch of the ‘Plastic Bottle Recycling’ initiative between Maybank, PNB and PNB Merdeka Ventures to encourage greater environmental responsibility among occupants of Menara Merdeka Maybank. The initiative was launched by Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli, Dato’ Izwan Hasli and Muazzam Mohamad through a symbolic recycling activity. As part of the initiative, dedicated plastic bottle recycling bins will be deployed across Menara Merdeka Maybank to encourage proper waste segregation and foster a greener, more environmentally conscious community. Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli, President & Group CEO of Maybank, together with Muazzam Mohamad and Dato’ Ir. Ts. (Dr.) Izwan Hasli Mohd Ibrahim, officiates the launch of the Plastic Bottle Recycling initiative through a symbolic recycling activity during MGSW 2026. The programme featured a diverse range of learning, engagement, and experiential activities through initiatives such as Net Zero Zone, MSPC Experience Zone, Sustainability Marketplace, Upcycling Activities, Sustainability Tree, the Relationship Manager’s Net Zero Challenge, and #MaybankCares Points. Maybankers participated in the creation of reusable tote bags made from used clothing at the ‘Upcycling booth’ during the MGSW 2026, highlighting the importance of waste reduction, resource circularity and sustainable everyday practices. A series of expert-led discussions, workshops and sharing sessions covered topics such as “Talk to Traction: Solving the Net Zero Equation Across Sustainability, Business and Law.”, “From Energy Optimisation to Net Zero”, Menara Merdeka Maybank Green Building Sharing Session and Social Impact Partners’ Day. Concurrently, the Etiqa Sustainability Day was also held in conjunction with MGSW 2026, where they hosted workshops, sharing sessions and a Sustainability Bazaar at Dataran Maybank. Maybankers participated in expert-led discussions, workshops and knowledge-sharing sessions during Maybank Group Sustainability Week (MGSW) 2026, which covered topics ranging from net zero transition and energy optimisation to sustainable building practices and social impact, aimed at strengthening sustainability knowledge and action across the Group. Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin said “MGSW demonstrates the growing momentum of sustainability within Maybank. The enthusiasm and participation shown by Maybankers throughout the week reinforces our belief that continued progress is driven by a shared sense of purpose and responsibility. We are encouraged by this momentum and are confident it will continue to shape the way sustainability is embraced across the Group.” Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Group Chief Sustainability Officer Maybank (Center in Black blazer) sharing a light moment with participants of the Sustainable Manager Portfolio Challenge during the MGSW 2026. The interactive competition simulated real-world portfolio management scenarios, challenging participants to balance profitability, business growth and sustainability considerations in their decision-making. As part of its commitment in transitioning towards a low-carbon economy, Maybank has achieved a cumulative 58.9% reduction in operational carbon emissions since 2021, marking significant progress towards its target of a 61% reduction by 2026. The achievement reflects the Group’s continued efforts to reduce its environmental footprint while advancing its long-term ambitions of achieving carbon neutrality by 2030 and net zero emissions by 2050.

title: 'Refugees are not ‘foreign fugitives’
body: 'Charles Santiago The Ministry of Home Affairs should be careful about the language it uses to describe Myanmar nationals in Malaysia. People who have fled genocide, conflict or religious persecution are not “foreign fugitives” simply because they lack regular immigration status. Immigration status and criminality are not interchangeable. The government says the repatriation programme is voluntary, orderly and based on individual consent. But a genuinely voluntary return requires more than a signature. People must be able to make an informed decision, free from coercion, with a proper assessment of the risks they face on return. It is particularly troubling that the UNHCR, the UN’s refugee agency, says it had no role in Malaysia’s repatriation process. It has also warned that Myanmar remains unsafe for refugee returns. Consultation needs to be transparent too. Where is the meaningful engagement with the UNHCR, Suhakam, refugee-led organisations and civil society groups that have worked directly with these communities for years? - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member These groups hold information about individual vulnerabilities, family circumstances, protection concerns and conditions in Myanmar. Government agencies cannot simply assume they know these things. If the government has carried out comprehensive screening and concluded that every person returned can safely go home, it should publish the methodology, safeguards and independent verification mechanisms behind that conclusion. And if the government’s justification is that Myanmar nationals are a ‘financial burden’ or a ‘security threat’, the people of Malaysia deserve evidence. What is the actual public expenditure? Which specific security threats are being referred to? Are they a bigger threat than the two million undocumented migrant workers who have been in the country for the past 20 years or so? title: 'HLB Meezani Account-i Offers Cash, Gold, And Cars In New Prize Draws
body: 'HLB Meezani Account-i holders stand a chance to win cash, gold bars, holiday packages, a Proton e.MAS 5, and a Porsche Cayenne in HLB Islamic’s second year of prize draws, which runs from 30 July 2026 to 29 July 2027. There are daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly draws, with minimum balances ranging from RM100 to RM60,000 depending on the prize. HLB Islamic announced this year’s prizes at a rewards ceremony in Kuala Lumpur on 29 September 2026, held to mark the account’s first year. The bank said 43% of those who opened the account in its first year were new HLB Islamic customers. The Minimum Balance For Each Prize Each prize has its own minimum balance, and you get one entry for every full multiple of that amount. For example, keeping RM1,000 in the account when the day ends gives 10 entries in the daily draw, since the minimum balance is RM100. For the weekly draw, you get one entry for every RM200. Keeping RM2,500 at the end of the week gives 12 entries, and the extra RM100 doesn’t count. For quarterly and yearly prizes, entries are counted from each month-end balance and added up until the draw. Keeping RM2,000 in the account at the end of each month for a three-month quarter, for example, gives three entries for the 10g gold bar draw. Since the monthly, quarterly, and yearly draws all use your month-end balance, withdrawing money on the last day of the month can reduce your entries for that month, even if you put the money back a few days later. Some Payments And Deposits Can Earn Extra Entries The monthly and quarterly prizes also offer extra entries if you’ve already met the minimum balance for the relevant prize. You can earn additional entries by making at least 10 eligible QR or online payments from the account in a month, or by depositing at least RM2,000 in a single transaction. Doing both in the same month earns one more combo entry. Making 10 payments earns extra entries for the RM500 cash and Touch ‘n Go prizes. A deposit of RM2,000 or more earns extra entries for every prize in the table except the Proton e.MAS 5, which only gets the combo entry when you do both in the same month. The daily, weekly, and yearly draws don’t offer extra entries. Win Limits And Claiming Your Prize You can win the daily prize once a week at most, and the weekly prize once every two weeks. If your name is selected for more than one monthly prize in the same month, you’ll only receive the highest-value prize. The same applies to the quarterly and yearly draws. To qualify for the draws, you need to actively use HLB Connect from the start of each draw period until any prize is handed over. Winners are selected within 30 working days after each draw period ends and notified through the HLB Connect app within 14 working days after that. You have 30 working days from the announcement to claim your prize, after which the bank may award it to another winner. Cash prizes are credited directly into the winner’s HLB Meezani Account-i. Winners are responsible for any taxes or fees related to their prizes, and HLB Islamic may publish winners’ names with part of their IC numbers concealed. Non-cash prizes are handed over within 90 working days. Winners will need their winning letter and IC to collect them. Prizes can’t be exchanged for cash or transferred to someone else. Opening An HLB Meezani Account-i The account is Shariah-compliant and open to individuals who live in Malaysia. You need RM100 to open it and RM50 to keep it open. The account currently has an indicative profit rate of 0.05% p.a., calculated daily and paid monthly, as of 30 September 2026. You can deposit or withdraw money through HLB Islamic branches, ATMs, cash deposit machines, and online channels. Because it’s an investment account rather than a savings account or fixed deposit, HLB Islamic states that the money and returns aren’t guaranteed and the account isn’t protected by Perbadanan Insurans Deposit Malaysia (PIDM). The prize draws come on top of the account’s profit rate, so look at both when deciding where to keep your money. You can also compare the latest savings account and fixed deposit rates on RinggitPlus. You can open the account at an HLB Islamic branch or book an appointment through the HLB Islamic website. The full rules are set out in the campaign’s terms and conditions [PDF]. Follow us on our official WhatsApp channel for the latest money tips and updates. title: 'Maybank, Asian Banking School Collaborate to Raise Wealth Advisory Standards in Malaysia | Maybank
body: 'Maybank to serve as Founding Industry Partner in developing an industry-recognised certification for wealth advisory professionals Maybank and the Asian Banking School (ABS) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to explore the development of a professional certification framework for wealth advisory in Malaysia, aimed at introducing an industry-recognised benchmark for advisory capability. The proposed certification framework, to be known as the ABS Wealth Advisory & Management Certification Programme, is intended to establish competency standards specifically for wealth advisory professionals in banking. Upon its launch, it will be Malaysia’s first industry-wide professional certification framework dedicated to wealth advisory. As wealth management needs grow more complex, clients increasingly require advice that connects different aspects of their financial lives. This initiative therefore aims to establish a consistent benchmark for the advisory capabilities required to serve clients holistically. Maybank will serve as the Founding Industry Partner, contributing insights and its experience in developing wealth talent, while ABS will bring its expertise in professional banking development and certification. ABS will retain independence over the standards and how they are assessed and certified. “Maybank has continuously invested in developing our wealth professionals through Maybank Wealth Academy, building advisory capabilities that complement technical expertise and enable a holistic approach that meets the financial needs of clients. This collaboration with the Asian Banking School allows us to contribute that experience beyond our organisation, to raise professional standards for wealth advisory in Malaysia, with the opportunity to extend elements of the programme across the region over time,” said Syed Ahmad Taufik Albar, Group CEO, Community Financial Services, Maybank. “Malaysia has an opportunity to further develop wealth advisory as a profession through independent and industry-relevant standards. By combining ABS’s expertise in professional banking development with Maybank’s practitioner experience as Founding Industry Partner, we aim to create a credible pathway that gives wealth professionals a clearer benchmark as they progress in their careers while raising the quality of wealth advisory across Malaysia,” said Professor Dr. Manivanan Saman, Chief Executive Officer, Asian Banking School. (L-R) Prof. Dr. Manivanan Saman, CEO of Asian Banking School & Syed Ahmad Taufik Albar, Group CEO, Community Financial Services, Maybank The programme’s first intake is expected in the second half of 2027, and Maybank intends to incorporate the programme into Maybank Wealth Academy, connecting it with structured learning and career development through practical workplace application. The parties will also explore opportunities to extend relevant certification pathways to wealth professionals across the region. This initiative builds on the Bank’s established wealth management franchise, which was named Malaysia’s Best Private Bank 2026 by Euromoney, and recognised as the Best Wealth Management Bank in Malaysia by Alpha Southeast Asia for the 10th consecutive year.

title: 'World Bank Supports Malaysia’s Possible Integration of GST Elements Into SST
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): The World Bank has agreed that certain elements of the goods and services tax (GST) should be implemented into Malaysia’s sales and service tax (SST) to address its distortionary features. World Bank lead economist for Malaysia Apurva Sanghi said the government should address the SST’s nature as a cascading tax and, in turn, an embedded tax. The SST is a single-stage tax with no input credit mechanism. In other words, tax can become embedded in prices as goods and services move through the supply chain. “We believe what is required is neutral tax reform that relieves cascading and embedded effects on businesses, for example through input tax credits, while also broadening the tax base to bolster revenues," he said during a briefing on the October 2026 Malaysia Economic Monitor report. There has been much industry and policy discussion on what an integration of GST elements into the SST, or a formulation of a better SST, could look like. Discourse began after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the government is studying improvements to the existing SST, including whether it can incorporate elements of the GST, following a Budget 2027 engagement session in August. Malaysia implemented the GST in 2015 at a 6% rate under the administration of Datuk Seri Najib Razak. The implementation led to soaring inflation and widespread complaints of slow tax refunds that created a cash crunch for small- to medium-sized businesses. The tax was suspended on June 1, 2018, after Pakatan Harapan took over the federal government, and was subsequently abolished and replaced with the current SST on Sept 1, 2018. While Apurva agreed the SST can be improved if the cascading tax aspect is addressed, he did note the World Bank has held the view that the GST is a better solution, should its regressivity be offset with cash transfers to those vulnerable. “Trying to integrate GST elements with SST, I think of it as trying to integrate efficiency with empathy. “And, when you fuse both together, the risk is you may get neither,” he warned. GST, all being equal, is favourable to SST, Apurva noted. He said GST avoids cascading and embedded tax. “One of the stumbling blocks of GST 1.0, the previous GST regime, was the delay in issuing refunds. If that is addressed, then that definitely is yet another argument to think about GST,” he said. World Bank economist Deisigan Shammugam also highlighted that it has been a decade since then and that technology has improved since then. title: 'Top Glove Expects An Even Better FY2027 After Strong FY2026
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Top Glove Corporation Bhd (KL:TOPGLOV) expects an even better FY2027 after its net profit tripled in the financial year ended Aug 31, 2026 (FY2026). Top Glove executive chairman Tan Sri Dr Lim Wee Chai said the group’s performance in FY2027 is expected to track global market demand growth of around 10%. "For FY2027 and ahead, we should be able to sustain and should be able to do better...the profit growth or sales growth should be about 10%, following the market growth," Lim said during the group's financial briefing following the release of its fourth-quarter results. "If we work harder and smarter, we should grow even better than 10% of the market growth rate…very likely that we will do better than FY2026," he added. Despite the optimistic outlook, the group faces operational headwinds from rising raw material costs, driven by persistent volatility in crude oil prices from the prolonged Iran war, and the hike in natural gas tariffs starting Oct 1. Top Glove joint managing director Ng Yong Lin said the 30% gas tariff hike is set to increase the group's cost per 1,000 pieces by 50 to 70 US cents (about RM2 to RM2.86), or 2% or 3%. However, the group was confident it could navigate these material cost pressures in FY2027 through disciplined cost and energy saving efforts. Ng said the group had reduced its energy consumption per 1,000 gloves by 30% to 35% compared to 2019 levels and expects automation and AI technology to cushion margins. To offset the rising raw material and gas expenses, the group is increasing average selling prices (ASPs) by US$2 to US$4 per 1,000 pieces for October and November. Currently, generic nitrile glove prices hover around US$21 to US$22 per 1,000 pieces. "So for the month of October, November, we have adjusted the glove selling price by about two to three dollars or even four dollars and that will be enough to cover other costs that increase," Lim said, adding that order books for October and November remain strong despite the price revisions. On competition from China glove manufacturers, Lim said the cost and pricing gap between Malaysian and Chinese makers has narrowed compared to three to four years ago. "The price difference for gloves sold from Malaysia compared to China used to have a big gap of about three to four dollars. Now, Malaysian manufacturers like us have improved our costing well. So our glove costing and selling prices are very close to theirs…there is not much difference anymore," Lim said. He added that attempts by some Chinese manufacturers to expand production into Southeast Asian nations such as Vietnam and Indonesia face operational challenges, including higher raw material import costs and reliance on Chinese expatriate staff, resulting in production costs increases of 10%. "Competition is there, but not as tough as two, three years ago," Lim said. For FY2026, the group's revenue grew 21% to RM4.23 billion from FY2025, supported by a 28% increase in sales volume. Net profit for the full year stood at RM308 million. Top Glove shares closed nine sen higher or 11.46% at 87.5 sen on Tuesday, giving the group a market capitalisation of RM7.2 billion. It was the second most active stock on Bursa Malaysia with 165.13 million shares changing hands.
