title: 'PETRONAS to Submit First in Sarawak Oil Rights Dispute, But Only Full FC Bench Can Decide on Preliminary Issues Hearing
body: 'PUTRAJAYA (Oct 1): A Federal Court judge has decided that only a full bench can decide on a preliminary issue raised by the Sarawak government in the dispute with PETRONAS over who has control over the oil in the state. Federal Court judge Datuk Rhodzariah Bujang on Thursday declined to make a ruling on the hearing of the preliminary issue, saying that the full Federal Court bench that will hear the separate PETRONAS and Sarawak government petitions should decide on the matter. The full bench hearing is scheduled for Jan 25 next year. Sarawak wants the preliminary issue of the legality of the colonial-era Order In Council 1954 (OIC) law to be heard before PETRONAS' petition about the competence of 10 Sarawak laws. The state government asserts that the OIC extends Sarawak's maritime borders beyond what is set in federal law and includes the continental shelf. The legal wrangle over who has control over oil found in Sarawak was sparked by the founding of state oil company Petros in 2016. Earlier this year, PETRONAS filed its petition to challenge the competency of 10 Sarawak laws on Jan 12, while Sarawak filed its challenge on three federal laws on Feb 23. Rhodzariah on Thursday said it would be improper for her to decide on the preliminary issue as the two cases are not consolidated, and the full bench might rule differently than her. However, Rhodzariah ruled that with regard to the submission of substantive arguments (the main matter of the case), based on the sequence of the filing of the petitions, PETRONAS would orally submit the issues raised in its petition first, and Sarawak after that. “This is based on the normal practice that the first petition filed first would be heard first, and subsequently the other. The fact that PETRONAS obtained leave (permission) from the Federal Court only on March 16 was not a consideration,” she ruled after a short 20-minute recess. The judge also asked parties (PETRONAS, the Sarawak government, and the federal government) to write in their applications to Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh, as they sought a panel of nine to 11 judges at the apex court constitutional hearing scheduled for five days beginning Jan 25 next year. A Federal Court bench usually comprises three or five judges. A full bench is convened for cases of extraordinary weight. Datuk Dr Cyrus Das appearing for PETRONAS, senior federal counsel Ahmad Hanir Hambaly @ Arwi, and Sarawak senior state counsel Mohd Adzrul Azlan indicated they would do so. Mohd Adzrul told the court that Sarawak would possibly indicate one or two judges who should not hear the matter. It is to be noted that besides the top-four judges — the Chief Justice, President of the Court of Appeal Datuk Seri Abu Bakar Jais, Chief Judge of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah, and Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Azizah Nawawi — there are 11 other apex court judges. PETRONAS is challenging the competency of the Sarawak assembly in enacting 10 laws which it says encroaches on federal government powers as set out in the Constitution's the Federal List. Chief among them is the OIC law, which extends Sarawak’s offshore borders beyond what is set by the federal government and international treaties. The OIC sets Sarawak’s offshore border to beyond three nautical miles from its shores and includes its continental shelf. The other state legislations being challenged by PETRONAS include the Environment (Reduction of Greenhouse Gas Emission) Ordinance 2023 and the Sarawak Oil Mining Ordinance 1958. Meanwhile, Sarawak is challenges three federal laws: the Petroleum Development Act 1974, the Continental Shelf Act 1966 and the Petroleum Mining Act 1966. Last week, parties indicated before Rhodzariah that they want their petitions to be heard separately and not be consolidated, but they do not agree on the sequence. The parties indicated that they do not mind the same judges hearing the petitions. On Thursday, parties indicated before Rhodzariah that they still disagree on which petition should be heard first. Cyrus said PETRONAS’ petition should be first because it was filed first. The senior lawyer said that since the Sarawak government had raised the OIC law in its defence, this indicates that it is a pre-emptive move by the state for it to be heard at the outset. “This court should not entertain such pre-emptive moves. Furthermore, the Federal Government is supporting PETRONAS that the company should submit first,” he said. Mohd Adzrul told Rhodzariah that since the OIC is central to PETRONAS’ argument, thus by ease of reference, the Sarawak petition should be heard first. “It is important to note that the OIC was never revoked or amended, and remains a part of the state law. There is a need for the apex court to decide the status of the OIC. Our petition should take precedence, because the dispute is between the state and the federal government as a party. “The court would have to decide whether it has original jurisdiction to touch on the OIC. This is the reason why we say the Sarawak government should be allowed to submit first, so that the submissions could be dealt with in a structured manner,” he said. Ahmad Hanir said the federal government supports PETRONAS’ application to submit first, as this a federal-state dispute and there is no need for the apex court to hear or decide on the preliminary issue. Following Rhodzariah’s decision on not deciding on Sarawak's preliminary issue, Mohd Adzrul said the state would apply for it be heard first. “The application will be filed within 14 days from today (Thursday),” he said, adding that they would file their written submissions in accordance with the agreed directions on Jan 11, and reply on Jan 18. Besides Das, Khoo Guan Huat, Datuk Azian Abd Aziz, Grace Teoh Wei Shan, Ahmad Faiz Razali, Khoo Yuan Ping and Alex Ngu appeared for PETRONAS. For Sarawak, besides Mohd Adzrul, the state is represented by Sarawak counsel Richard Tie Sing Wan and Felicity Sharmela Thomas. In addition to Ahmad Hanir, federal counsel Imtiyaz Wizni Aufa Othman represented the federal government. title: 'Maybank Falls Below RM10 for First Time in Nine Months as Rising Bond Yields Hurt Banking Stocks
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) fell below RM10 for the first time in nearly nine months and banking stocks mostly declined on Thursday amid rising bond yields. Higher yields generally hurt banks as they take larger paper losses from lower prices of the bonds they hold, which eats into capital and forces them to book losses if they sell. Investors may also demand higher returns on corporate bonds, affecting appetite for new issuances. That would weigh on banks’ near term non-interest income as well as their capital ratios, Affin Hwang Investment Bank flagged in a note on Thursday. Maybank, the country’s top bank in terms of assets, fell for the third straight day and closed down 0.4% at RM9.95. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) and Hong Leong Bank Bhd (KL:HLBANK) each declined over 1%. The Bursa Malaysia Financial Services Index, which also tracks non-bank firms such as insurers and stockbrokers, fell to its lowest level in 10 months. The US Federal Reserve raised interest rates earlier this month for the first time in three years, sending the yield on the 10-year benchmark Malaysian Government Securities to as high as 4.18% before moderating. A growing number of economists expect Bank Negara Malaysia to raise the overnight policy rate in November during the final scheduled monetary policy review for the year. Rising yields tend to lead to higher corporate bond yields, which also tie-in to capital raising decisions both for banks and other corporates and, subsequently, fee income to the banks, Affin Hwang said. Maybank and Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (KL:ABMB) have on their books the longest bond duration — the length of time for a bond to repay its cost in cash flows while also being a measure of sensitivity to changes in interest rates — according to the research house’s analysis. Public Bank Bhd (KL:PBBANK) and Hong Leong Bank, meanwhile, have the shortest duration. In terms of capital ratios, Maybank, RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK) and CIMB could see the largest drops, while Public Bank and Hong Leong Bank would see the least due to their portfolios’ shorter duration, the house added. title: '‘Ibu Janji Ambil Kami Di Sekolah, Tapi Dia Pergi Buat Selamanya’ | Medialahmy
body: 'GUA MUSANG – Hancur hati dua beradik apabila ibu yang dinanti untuk menjemput mereka pulang dari sekolah tidak kunjung tiba, sebaliknya mereka menerima berita duka apabila insan tersayang itu meninggal dunia akibat kemalangan. Nur Arissa Najla Mohd Shazuam, 13, dan Nur Amani Nuwairah Mohd Shazuam, 15, menanti penuh sabar selepas ibunya, Nor Hasyikim Daud, 34, berjanji mengambil mereka pulang dari Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Bandar Chiku. Nur Arissa Najla berkata, dia menerima berita kemalangan itu daripada seorang rakan ketika menunggu pada 1.40 tengah hari. “Ibu ada maklumkan akan ke Gua Musang dengan rakannya dan berjanji mengambil saya serta kakak dari sekolah. “Pada hari kejadian, saya menduduki tiga kertas peperiksaan dan sangat teruja untuk memberitahu ibu yang saya boleh jawab semua soalan subjek Sejarah. “Lebih setengah jam menanti ibu, namun tidak kunjung tiba, sebaliknya saya terima berita ibu kemalangan. “Saya nampak bapa saudara datang menjemput kami,” katanya ketika ditemui di Felda Chiku 5 di sini. Dalam kejadian Ahad lalu, Nor Hasyikim maut di lokasi kejadian apabila kenderaan dipandunya bertembung dengan lori 10 tan di Kilometer 40 Jalan Gua Musang-Kuala Krai. Mangsa meninggal dunia akibat tersepit, manakala rakannya di tempat duduk penumpang hadapan cedera parah. Allahyarham turut meninggalkan seorang bayi Nur Aireen Nisrina berusia 11 bulan. Sementara itu, kakak kepada Nor Hasyikim, Siti Noraeshah Daud, 39, berkata, tiga beradik itu akan dijaga ibunya dengan bantuan adik-beradik lain. “Sejak setahun lalu arwah membesarkan tiga anaknya dengan bekerja di kantin asrama SMK Bandar Chiku. “Selepas ini kami akan bersama-sama menjaga dan membesarkan tiga anak perempuan arwah,” katanya. Orang ramai yang ingin memberi sumbangan boleh menyalurkan ke akaun Bank CIMB milik Siti Noraeshah Daud bernombor 7601845122. Sumber – Berita Harian

title: 'Maybank falls below RM10 for first time in nine months, rising bond yields hurt banking stocks
body: 'Maybank falls below RM10 for first time in nine months, rising bond yields hurt banking stocks KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) fell below RM10 for the first time in nearly nine months and banking stocks mostly declined on Thursday amid rising bond yields. Higher yields generally hurt banks as they take larger paper losses from lower prices of the bonds they hold, which eats into capital and forces them to book losses if they sell. Banks will also have to increase their rates to attract depositors, leading to higher funding costs. That would weigh on banks’ near term non-interest income as well as their capital ratios, Affin Hwang Investment Bank flagged in a note on Thursday. Maybank, the country’s top bank in terms of assets, fell for the third straight day and closed down 0.4% at RM9.95. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) and Hong Leong Bank Bhd (KL:HLBANK) each declined over 1%. The Bursa Malaysia Financial Services Index, which also tracks non-bank firms such as insurers and stockbrokers, fell to its lowest level in 10 months. The US Federal Reserve raised interest rates earlier this month for the first time in three years, sending the yield on the 10-year benchmark Malaysian Government Securities to as high as 4.18% before moderating. A growing number of economists expect Bank Negara Malaysia to raise the overnight policy rate in November during the final scheduled monetary policy review for the year. Rising yields tend to lead to higher corporate bond yields, which also tie-in to capital raising decisions both for banks and other corporates and, subsequently, fee income to the banks, Affin Hwang said. Maybank and Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (KL:ABMB) have on their books the longest bond duration — the length of time for a bond to repay its cost in cash flows while also being a measure of sensitivity to changes in interest rates — according to the research house’s analysis. Public Bank Bhd (KL:PBBANK) and Hong Leong Bank, meanwhile, have the shortest duration. In terms of capital ratios, Maybank, RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK) and CIMB could see the largest drops, while Public Bank and Hong Leong Bank would see the least due to their portfolios’ shorter duration, the house added. title: 'CIMB Securities: Consumer, construction stocks seen as key beneficiaries of Budget 2027
body: 'CIMB Securities: Consumer, construction stocks seen as key beneficiaries of Budget 2027 KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 22): Consumer and construction stocks could be among the key beneficiaries of the upcoming Budget 2027, as higher cash aid, potential tax relief and increased development spending are expected to support domestic demand and infrastructure activity, CIMB Securities said on Tuesday. In a note, the research house expects allocations for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) to rise by about RM2 billion to RM17 billion. It believes the higher allocation “could provide a modest boost to mass-market consumption, particularly benefitting companies exposed to lower- and middle-income households”. Among the counters poised to benefit are 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd (KL:99SMART), Eco-Shop Marketing Bhd (KL:ECOSHOP) and MR DIY Group (M) Bhd (KL:MRDIY), as well as food and beverage manufacturers Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd (KL:NESTLE), Life Water Bhd (KL:LWSABAH) and QL Resources Bhd (KL:QL). CIMB Securities also expects gross development expenditure to rise to RM83 billion in 2027, with higher spending on water infrastructure among the potential areas of focus. Among the counters it sees as well positioned to benefit are Gamuda Bhd (KL:GAMUDA), IJM Corp Bhd (KL:IJM), Malayan Cement Bhd (KL:MCEMENT) and Insight Analytics Bhd (KL:IAB). Healthcare sector seen supported Separately, Maybank Investment Bank expects Budget 2027 to remain supportive of the healthcare sector. Potential measures include tax relief for healthcare and medical insurance, support for the nationwide MediAsas rollout, continued medical-tourism incentives and greater public-private collaboration to ease congestion at public hospitals, it said. Local pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical manufacturers may also benefit from continued government support for manufacturing, procurement, research and development, Maybank IB said. title: 'Tengku Ampuan Pahang rasmi Kejohanan Golf Wanita, The Ladies 2026
body: 'PETALING JAYA: Kejohanan golf wanita, The Ladies 2026 rasmi membuka tirai kelmarin menerusi acara Pro-Am Diraja yang dirasmikan oleh Tengku Ampuan Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah Almarhum Sultan Iskandar Al-Haj di The Mines Resort and Golf Club. Kejohanan yang berlangsung selama tiga hari itu menyaksikan penyertaan seramai 50 pemain merangkumi kelompok profesional dan amatur termasuklah kemunculan semula juara bertahan, Liyana Durisic serta atlet Olimpik negara, Kelly Tan. Menurut The Mines Resort & Golf Club, matlamat utama kejohanan itu adalah untuk melahirkan lebih ramai pemain berwibawa tempatan selain bertindak sebagai batu loncatan penting sebelum saingan bertaraf antarabangsa menjelang kejohanan Maybank Championship tidak lama lagi. Katanya, penganjuran itu membawa mesej yang jelas kepada generasi muda bahawa kerjaya dalam bidang sukan golf profesional bukan mustahil untuk dicapai oleh wanita Malaysia. “Ia adalah satu jemputan kepada generasi baharu untuk melihat golf profesional bukan sekadar sesuatu yang dimainkan di tempat lain di dunia tetapi sebagai laluan kerjaya yang boleh diceburi oleh wanita Malaysia,” katanya dalam kenyataan. Dalam pada itu, saingan Pro-Am Diraja hari ini menyaksikan pasukan yang dibarisi Dianna Lee, Ang Bee Ee, Jojo Goh dan digandingkan bersama pemain profesional Kelly Tan dinobatkan sebagai juara keseluruhan. Tempat kedua diraih oleh pasukan Miran Shin, Raina Azene Ramli, Nur Azreen dan pemain profesional Tan Ying Ying manakala kedudukan ketiga disandang oleh Yang Amat Mulia Che Puan Besar Kedah, Che Puan Hajah Hamimah Haji Hamidun, Datuk Norfaizah Zainal, June Yap bersama pemain profesional, Zulaikah Nasser. Menurutnya lagi, selain memperkukuh pembangunan bakat tempatan, penganjuran edisi kali ini turut mendapat sokongan padu pelbagai syarikat korporat terkemuka seperti Prudential, 100PLUS, Power Root dan Delon. Jelasnya, pihak penganjur turut mempunyai perancangan jangka panjang untuk meningkatkan kualiti kejohanan itu dengan sasaran hadiah terkumpul mencecah kira-kira RM12.5 juta pada masa hadapan. “Objektifnya bukan sekadar meningkatkan wang kemenangan tetapi untuk mewujudkan acara yang mempunyai status kukuh bagi menarik perhatian antarabangsa, di samping memberikan pemain Malaysia platform yang lebih berkesan ke pentas global,” katanya. – UTUSAN

title: 'FBM KLCI Slips At Open As Budget 2027 Looms
body: 'The FBM KLCI opened slightly lower on Wednesday as investors remained cautious ahead of the tabling of Budget 2027, with the market continuing to search for fresh catalysts.  At 9.05am, the benchmark index fell 3.22 points to 1,630.13, remaining rangebound amid continued uncertainty.  Apex Securities said easing crude oil prices and expectations surrounding Budget 2027 could provide some support to the local market, although a stronger recovery would likely require fresh foreign fund inflows and clearer direction on bond yields and geopolitical developments.  “We stay cautious on the local bourse this week, as easing crude oil prices and Budget 2027 expectations may offer some support, but a stronger recovery will likely require fresh catalysts such as foreign fund inflows and clearer direction on bond yields and geopolitical developments,” it said in a note.  The research firm also remained cautious on near-term global risk appetite, noting that the current rally was narrowly led by technology stocks while bond yields remained near multi-decade highs.  It said equities could remain vulnerable if the US Federal Reserve adopts a more hawkish tone.  Banking counters were among the early decliners, with CIMB falling seven sen to RM7.63 and Hong Leong Bank losing eight sen to RM22.  Press Metal shed six sen to RM7.13.  Among actively traded stocks, Metronic was unchanged at 0.5 sen and Zetrix AI remained at nine sen, while Top Glove jumped five sen to 92.5 sen.  Glove makers also gained amid renewed optimism in the sector, with Supermax rising two sen to 48 sen, Hartalega adding five sen to RM1.17 and Kossan gaining two sen to RM1.27.

title: 'RHB, The Makeover Guys Offer Flexi Loan for Home Purchase and Renovation
body: 'RHB Bank has partnered with renovation firm The Makeover Guys to offer financing that covers both a property purchase and renovation costs. The Makeover Flexi Loan provides eligible customers with financing of up to 120% of the property’s value. This comprises up to 90% for the home purchase and an additional 30% for renovation work, mortgage insurance or takaful, legal costs and documentation fees. Borrowers can repay the loan over a maximum of 35 years or until they reach the age of 70, whichever comes first. Its Full Flexi features allow them to make additional repayments and redraw funds when needed. Renovation funds will be released progressively as contractors reach project milestones. The facility is designed for homeowners and property investors. Customers can access consultation, interior design, project management and construction services through The Makeover Guys. “We have seen customers delay moving in, renovate room by room over several years or compromise on what they originally wanted because the renovation budget was not available upfront. The Makeover Flexi Loan changes that by allowing homeowners to plan both their property purchase and renovation together from day one,” said Gavin Liew, Founder & CEO of The Makeover Guys. “As homeownership needs evolve, financing solutions must evolve as well. Traditionally, property financing and renovation financing have been treated as separate decisions, even though both are fundamental to creating a home. We saw an opportunity to bridge that gap by bringing these financing needs together under a single solution,” said Sien Vee Loc, Head of Consumer Finance, Group Community Banking, RHB Bank Berhad. title: 'CIMB sees rising odds of BNM rate hike in 1H27
body: 'BANK Negara Malaysia (BNM) is expected to keep the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) unchanged at 2.75% in November, although the probability of a rate hike in the first half of 2027 is increasing if economic growth remains firm and inflation pressures broaden, according to CIMB Treasury and Markets Research.   “We expect a hold in November, but see rising odds of a 25bps rate hike in 1H27 if growth stays firm and inflation broadens,” CIMB said in a report released today. title: 'PTT Synergy beli 4 kilang dalam pembinaan bernilai RM32 juta di Klang jana hasil sewa berulang - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt — PTT Synergy Group Berhad bakal memperluas portfolio hartanah dengan pemerolehan empat unit kilang bernilai hampir RM32 juta di Klang, Selangor, yang disasarkan menjana pendapatan sewa berulang daripada penyewa industri. Menerusi makluman tambahan kepada Bursa Malaysia, ia berkata anak syarikat tidak langsung milik penuhnya, PTT Assets Sdn Bhd, akan memperoleh empat bidang tanah bersama unit kilang yang sedang atau akan dibina dengan jumlah pertimbangan tunai RM31.997 juta. Menurut kumpulan tersebut, pemerolehan itu bertujuan mengembangkan portfolio pelaburan hartanah kumpulan dan mewujudkan aliran pendapatan sewa berulang menerusi penyewaan keempat-empat unit kilang kepada penyewa industri. "PTT merancang memulakan proses mencari penyewa serta rundingan pajakan sepanjang tempoh pembinaan, dengan operasi sewaan disasarkan bermula selepas projek siap dan milikan kosong diserahkan, tertakluk kepada kerja pengubahsuaian yang diperlukan," katanya. Keempat-empat hartanah dijangka disiapkan dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh perjanjian jual beli (SPA) masing-masing, dengan kerja pembinaan telah bermula pada 7 Januari 2026 dan kini mencapai sehingga peringkat rangka struktur bangunan, atau kira-kira 55% siap. Dari segi pembiayaan, risiko pembelian itu disokong kelulusan pinjaman daripada CIMB Bank Berhad dengan margin pembiayaan 90%, selain rebat Bumiputera 10% yang diberikan penjual. Berdasarkan terma pembayaran, 10% daripada harga pembelian perlu dibayar sebaik sahaja setiap SPA ditandatangani, manakala baki bayaran dibuat secara berperingkat mengikut kemajuan pembinaan sehingga notis milikan kosong dikeluarkan. "Pembelian itu turut mengambil kira transaksi hartanah perindustrian berdekatan, termasuk sebuah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja Prime Industrial Park seluas 1,854.99 meter persegi yang didagangkan pada RM8.5 juta pada Jun 2026," jelas PTT. Satu lagi perbandingan ialah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja 3 Industrial Park berkeluasan 2,024.99 meter persegi yang direkodkan pada harga RM7.689 juta pada Mac 2026. Sekiranya penjual gagal menyerahkan milikan kosong dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh SPA, penjual perlu membayar ganti rugi dipersetujui pada kadar 5% setahun berdasarkan jumlah bayaran yang telah dibuat PTT sehingga tarikh penyerahan sebenar. Dari segi kedudukan kewangan, nisbah penggearan proforma PTT dijangka meningkat kepada 2.01 kali selepas pemerolehan berbanding 1.91 kali setakat 30 Jun 2025, berdasarkan kedudukan kewangan proforma yang dinyatakan syarikat.

title: 'Bursa opens lower on higher US yields, Middle East tensions
body: 'At 9.10am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 3.74 points, or 0.22%, to 1,647.43 from Wednesday’s close of 1,651.17. The index opened 1.30 points lower at 1,649.87. On the broader market, decliners outpaced gainers 200 to 142, with 307 counters unchanged, 2,124 untraded and 12 suspended. Turnover stood at 246.59 million shares worth RM118.14 million. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said Wall Street closed mixed as softer inflation eased expectations of another US Federal Reserve rate hike, although elevated bond yields continued to weigh on sentiment. On the domestic front, he said the market benchmark may trade cautiously, with weak market breadth and recent foreign selling indicating continued caution among investors. “Thus, for today, we expect the index to remain in consolidation mode within the 1,640-1,660 range, with bargain hunting providing some downside support,” he told Bernama. Among the heavyweights, Maybank and IHH Healthcare were unchanged at RM9.90 and RM7.83 respectively. Public Bank fell three sen to RM4.67, CIMB shed one sen to RM7.78 and Tenaga Nasional lost two sen to RM12.94. In active trade, ACE Market debutant GB Bond fell half a sen to 24.5 sen, while VS Industry was unchanged at 28 sen. Astro Malaysia added half a sen to six sen, Jaks Resources gained one sen to 21.5 sen and Divfex advanced two sen to 11 sen. Among the top gainers, Keck Seng advanced 11 sen to RM5.14 and Petron Malaysia rose seven sen to RM3.47. Hengyuan Refining and Spritzer each gained six sen to RM3.62 and RM3.67 respectively, while Jati Tinggi strengthened five sen to RM1.44. Kuala Lumpur Kepong led the decliners, falling 18 sen to RM22.02. UWC shed 15 sen to RM6.92, while Insights Analytics and MISC each fell nine sen to RM1.20 and RM7.55 respectively. Petronas Dagangan lost eight sen to RM19.20. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index fell 42.26 points to 17,532.41, the FBM Emas Index declined 26.32 points to 12,265.69, and the FBM Top 100 Index shed 27.82 points to 12,056.62. The FBM Emas Shariah Index weakened 22.09 points to 12,154.26, while the FBM ACE Index trimmed 6.31 points to 5,527.97. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index slipped 0.10 point to 180.31, while the Energy Index gained 1.41 points to 847.11. The Financial Services Index fell 27.47 points to 19,189.02, while the Plantation Index retreated 33.34 points to 9,163.33.

title: 'Haze keeps air quality unhealthy across most of S'pore as smoke drifts from Indonesia; Will haze affect the S'pore F1 Grand Prix? No race-day forecast yet from weatherman: Singapore live news
body: 'Haze keeps air quality unhealthy across most of S'pore as smoke drifts from Indonesia; Will haze affect the S'pore F1 Grand Prix? No race-day forecast yet from weatherman: Singapore live news A curated selection of some of the biggest, most important, and fascinating news that's making waves online, featured by Yahoo Singapore Air quality in four of Singapore's five regions remained unhealthy early on Tuesday (6 Oct), with the 24-hour PSI at 6am reaching 130 in the central region, 117 in the west, 112 in the east and 107 in the north, while only the south stayed moderate at 95, according to reports. One-hour PM2.5 levels were elevated in the central, west and east regions but normal in the north and south, following a worsening on Monday evening when the east joined the west and central regions in the unhealthy band. The National Environment Agency (NEA) forecast a 24-hour PSI in the "high moderate to mid unhealthy" range as south-easterly winds carry moderate to dense smoke from Kalimantan and southern Sumatra towards Singapore. NEA advises healthy people to reduce prolonged or strenuous outdoor exertion while the PSI is unhealthy, with the elderly, pregnant women and children told to minimise it and people with chronic heart or lung disease told to avoid it. The PSI first breached the unhealthy threshold on 4 Sept, the first haze-driven breach since October 2023, and peaked at a 2026 high of 164 in central Singapore on 29 Sept. The Meteorological Service Singapore (MSS) said a strong El Niño could delay the end of the dry season, with the monsoon transition expected only in late October or early November. Political, business and cryptocurrency leaders, including Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, investor Ray Dalio and Eric Trump, are gathering in hazy Singapore for finance conferences ahead of this weekend's Formula One Grand Prix. Hotel rates have soared, with the Fullerton Bay Hotel beside the track charging S$5,030 a night for a room that usually costs US$1,460, as hundreds of thousands of fans and about 90,000 top executives arrive, according to reports. Maybank economist Chua Hak Bin expects F1 to generate S$160 million in tourism receipts this year, up from the usual S$145 million, while the Singapore Tourism Board (STB) said the events showed strong momentum despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty, Reuters reported. Slumping bond prices and cooling sentiment on artificial intelligence are expected to dominate the Forbes CEO Conference and the Milken Asia Summit, while a crypto event is nearly sold out even after the market's value fell about a quarter in a year. Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) forecast "high moderate to mid unhealthy" air for Tuesday (6 Oct) but gave no forecast for Sunday's race, and weather analyst Fergus Keatinge said there was no clear sign the haze would end quickly. Indonesia recorded 15,461 hotspots in September, second only to 2015, as a strong El Niño fuelled fires that left Singapore the world's third-most polluted city on 30 Sept. Read more in our live blog below, including the latest local and international news and updates. - Joel Balbin Smoky Singapore gears up to talk money ahead of F1 as haze shrouds city Political, business, cryptocurrency and sports leaders are gathering in Singapore for a series of finance-focused conferences ahead of this weekend's Formula One Grand Prix, as haze from Indonesian fires continues to cover the city-state. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, investor Ray Dalio and Eric Trump, co-founder of his family's cryptocurrency business, are expected to attend, along with hundreds of thousands of F1 fans, according to Reuters. The Fullerton Bay Hotel beside the race track is charging S$5,030 (US$3,933) a night for a room that usually costs US$1,460, as the night race and about 40 sideline events draw visitors. F1 generates about S$145 million a year in incremental tourism receipts, according to official estimates, and Maybank economist Chua Hak Bin expects that to reach S$160 million this year, plus broader gains from deals struck at sideline events, Reuters reported. The Singapore Tourism Board (STB) said F1 and its related events had strong momentum, reflecting confidence despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty. About 90,000 top-ranking executives are expected in town. Slumping bond prices and a shift in sentiment on artificial intelligence, from euphoric to cautious, are expected to occupy investors at the Forbes CEO Conference and the Milken Asia Summit, which begins on Wednesday (7 Oct). The total value of the cryptocurrency market has fallen about a quarter over 12 months to US$3 trillion, yet organisers of a crypto event said it was nearly sold out, with 25,000 attendees expected, matching last year, according to Reuters. Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) forecast air quality in the "high moderate to mid unhealthy" range for Tuesday but gave no longer-range forecast for Sunday's race. Fergus Keatinge, director of WeatherMapping.com, said air quality would vary daily with wind and showers, but there was "no clear sign of a sustained pattern change" to end the haze quickly, according to Bloomberg. Kuala Lumpur topped IQAir's global pollution rankings on 30 Sept, with Singapore third, and poor air quality had forced organisers to shorten a Singapore half marathon at the last minute the previous weekend. Indonesia's forestry ministry recorded 15,461 hotspots in September, above 2019 levels and second only to 2015, as a strong El Niño brought abnormally hot and dry conditions. - Joel Balbin Air quality unhealthy as smoke drifts from Indonesia into Singapore amid haze Air quality in four of Singapore's five regions stayed in the unhealthy range early on Tuesday (6 Oct), with the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) at 6am reading 130 in the central region, 117 in the west, 112 in the east and 107 in the north. Only the south, at 95, remained in the moderate band, where a reading of 101 to 200 is classed as unhealthy, Straits Times reported. One-hour PM2.5 readings, which guide immediate activities, were elevated in the central (60), west (59) and east (56) regions, while the north (48) and south (35) stayed at normal levels, according to Straits Times. The morning readings followed a deterioration on Monday evening, when the east reached a PSI of 101 at 6pm to join the west at 120 and the central region at 122 in the unhealthy band, with PM2.5 elevated in all five regions. The National Environment Agency (NEA) said in its 5 Oct advisory that with winds expected from the south-east or east-south-east, the 24-hour PSI was forecast to be in the "high moderate to mid unhealthy" range. Dry conditions are expected to persist over Kalimantan and southern Sumatra, where moderate to dense smoke plumes were seen drifting towards Singapore. Under NEA guidance, healthy people should reduce prolonged or strenuous outdoor exertion when the 24-hour PSI is unhealthy, while the elderly, pregnant women and children should minimise it and people with chronic heart or lung disease should avoid it. When PM2.5 is elevated, healthy people are advised to cut strenuous outdoor activity for the next hour, and vulnerable groups should avoid it. The PSI first crossed into the unhealthy range on 4 Sept, the first haze-driven breach since October 2023, and the year's highest reading of 164 was recorded in central Singapore on 29 Sept. The Meteorological Service Singapore (MSS) told the media that strong El Niño events tend to delay the end of the dry season, and that it expects Singapore's monsoon transition only in late October or early November, later than in the previous two years. Under NEA guidance, healthy people should reduce prolonged or strenuous outdoor exertion when the 24-hour PSI is unhealthy, while the elderly, pregnant women and children should minimise it and people with chronic heart or lung disease should avoid it. When PM2.5 is elevated, healthy people are advised to cut strenuous outdoor activity for the next hour, and vulnerable groups should avoid it. The PSI first crossed into the unhealthy range on 4 Sept, the first haze-driven breach since October 2023, and the year's highest reading of 164 was recorded in central Singapore on 29 Sept. title: 'VS Surprise 4Q Return to Core Profit Prompts Three Brokers to Upgrade
body: 'V.S Industry returned to core profitability in 4QFY26, posting a RM19.5 million core net profit after a RM38.0 million core loss in the previous quarter and a RM31.5 million core loss a year earlier. This narrowed its FY26 core net loss to RM21.5 million, a better-than-expected result. Stronger orders from key brand owners lifted sales and improved operating leverage. title: 'Awards offer SMEs a benchmark for growth
body: 'GEORGE TOWN: Business awards can serve as more than recognition, giving small and medium enterprises (SMEs) a benchmark to measure their progress, identify areas for improvement and set targets for the year ahead, said fourth-generation entrepreneur Jonathan Chan Heng Liang. Chan, 34, the fourth-generation successor of Sin Boon Kee Coffee, said the guidelines under the Star Outstanding Business Awards (SOBA) categories provided companies with an indication of where they stood and what they could work towards next. “Joining SOBA is actually kind of one indicator for us, whether we improved since last year, what we are doing in the future and what we are aiming to hit next year. “Winning awards could also generate publicity and give customers greater confidence in a brand,” he said during SOBA Connect Penang at The Ship Campus in Batu Kawan on Sept 29. Organised by Star Media Group (SMG) and themed “Connections That Matter, Strategies That Scale”, the event attracted over 100 business owners, entrepreneurs and industry representatives for discussions on business growth, financing, technology and cybersecurity. Chan’s company, SBK Concept Store Sdn Bhd, received five recognitions at SOBA 2025, including Platinum awards for Best Employer, Best in CSR and Best in Halal Product/Service, Gold for Best Use of Technology and a Meritorious Achievement for Young Entrepreneur of the Year. He was among three speakers in the “Funding Growth: Unlocking Capital” panel, together with RHB Bank Bhd (RHB) SME Product and Programme Lending Management (PLM) development head Ian Chua and National Association of Women Entrepreneurs of Malaysia (Nawem) Penang chairman Bharati Suresh Chand. “Businesses should maintain cash reserves equivalent to three to six months of operating expenses. “This provides an important buffer to help them navigate periods of cash-flow pressure and manage their day-to-day obligations with greater confidence,” said Chua. He added that RHB views itself as a partner to SMEs, offering financing solutions tailored to their evolving business needs, whether to support short-term working capital requirements or longer-term expansion plans. “We see ourselves not just as a financier, but as a partner to SMEs. Whether businesses require short-term working capital to bridge temporary cash-flow gaps or financing to support expansion and asset acquisition, we are committed to providing solutions that meet their specific needs,” he said. The event also covered cybersecurity and data protection, an area increasingly tied to business growth. Titled “Cybersecurity & Data Protection for Business Growth”, the panel featured BitRanger Sdn Bhd chief executive officer and founder as well as Universiti Sains Malaysia Cybersecurity Research Centre (Cyres) deputy director Assoc Prof Dr Shankar Karuppayah, EY Consulting association partner Jerry Ng and Crest Asia Council chairman BK Soon and examined cybersecurity and data protection from a business perspective, as companies increasingly relied on digital systems for operations, customer engagement and growth. The programme subsequently moved to an Alumni Spotlight featuring business growth stories, with speakers sharing practical examples from their own companies. Berry Group founder and managing director Victor Tan presented his session on “Tech-Driven Growth: Turning Digital Tools into Business Advantage”, highlighting how the education group expanded from 200 students in 2020 to 10,500 in 2026. The 50-fold growth was achieved with a lean core team of 30 full-time staff while the group managed 147 tutors. He explained how the company connected six systems covering operations and culture, workforce accountability, virtual classrooms, customer engagement, enrolment automation and AI-supported teaching. Solar House business development director Ong Yong Qiang, who presented Cash Flow Mastery: Strengthening Business Stability & Growth, highlighted three factors putting pressure on business margins – the impact of the Sales and Service Tax (SST), rising material costs and changes in industry policies. He cited the July 2025 electricity tariff restructuring for medium-voltage users as an example, with lower charges per kilowatt-hour but higher charges based on maximum demand. Collaborative Excellence Sdn Bhd founder and managing partner Chong Li Ken, who presented “Future-Ready Workforce: Building Agile & Adaptive Teams”, highlighted the importance of turning individual expertise into organisational capability by capturing knowledge, processes and data, enabling businesses to build more adaptive teams and retain critical know-how as people and technology evolve. The event also saw services business pitches by the four main SOBA sponsors: Credit Guarantee Corporation Malaysia Bhd (CGC) Prai branch manager Nori Harni Juhari, U Mobile Sdn Bhd (U Mobile) head of SME Caroline Chin, RHB regional sales head SME Darren Lau and The Ship Campus chief executive officer Jasmon Lim, representing PKT Logistics Group Sdn Bhd (PKT). Lim said The Ship Campus’ role in Batu Kawan went beyond providing space for events, with the campus focused on developing an ecosystem linking businesses, education and entrepreneurship. “Our core and primary role being located in Batu Kawan was to ensure that we could build an effective ecosystem. The campus, established in 2020, engaged businesses and potential clients to understand their needs and connect them with potential suppliers, customers and other business opportunities. “The ecosystem also included Peninsula College, which offers certificates, diplomas and degrees, and Penn Skills, an accredited training centre focused on skilling, upskilling and reskilling. “Having the campus in Batu Kawan’s industrial area also placed it close to manufacturers and other companies, allowing it to understand their talent requirements and connect industry with education and skills training,” he said. SOBA 2026 is organised by SMG with CGC, PKT, RHB and U Mobile as main sponsors, while Great Wall Motor is co-sponsor, with the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) being the official trade promotion partner. It is audited by BDO while radio stations 988 and Suria are official media partners. For more information, call the SOBA Hotline at 017-231 1789or visit www.soba.com.my

title: 'Senior Citizens’ Bill: Give older people a fairer deal
body: 'V Thomas The women, family and community development minister has said the Senior Citizens’ Bill will be tabled in Parliament in early 2027. The public is still being asked for input and feedback. Here are my suggestions for the bill. Dedicated hospital wings Major government hospitals should have a separate wing for older adults. It would focus on treatment, surgery and medication. At present, older people wait with everyone else until their name or number is called. Many are frail, in wheelchairs or ill. They should not have to wait so long for treatment. A separate wing would help the government judge whether it needs bigger budgets and more geriatricians. It would also be easier to manage well, as it would handle fewer patients. Better EPF returns Major banks in India offer older adults deposit interest rates of up to about 7-8%, depending on the bank and tenure. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Likewise, the Employees Provident Fund in Malaysia could pay older people a higher dividend on their savings. A rate of 10% on up to RM200,000 in savings would help. (The current rate is about 6.15%, declared for 2025.) A separate EPF scheme for older people could achieve this. At 10%, RM200,000 would earn about RM20,000 a year, or roughly RM1,666 a month. At present, members can deposit up to RM100,000 a year in aggregate across EPF’s voluntary contribution schemes. But the EPF voluntary contribution scheme now stops at age 75. That age limit could be extended to 80. More older people could then cope with the cost of living, medical bills and other expenses. Many older people would no longer have to seek help from the Social Welfare Department. Harnessing experience The government should use older people’s experience through incentives in residents’ associations and other local groups. Local authorities could help in these programmes. Town hall sessions would benefit from older people’s knowledge, particularly of local government. Local authorities should register older people’s associations freely and tell older people about programmes in their areas. Some light duties could be reserved for older people who can work. Older people are a vital asset, and the government should make full use of what they can contribute in their later years. Many capable older people could serve as local councillors and village development and security committee (JKKK) members because they know local needs well. A quota for older people among councillors could be considered. Older people should also have their own associations at state and national level. This would let them voice their needs, especially when the yearly budget is drawn up. The government would then understand their needs better and allocate the right funds for their wellbeing. The number of older people is rising fast. It is time for the government to plan soundly and strategically for this growing issue. V Thomas follows the Aliran website. The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. title: 'Bursa Malaysia Experiences Downturn at Mid-Afternoon
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia saw a decline at mid-afternoon, with selling pressure noted in selected heavyweight stocks. According to BERNAMA News Agency, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) dropped 19 points to 1,632.17 at 3 pm, down from Wednesday's close of 1,651.17. The index had initially opened 1.30 points lower at 1,649.87. Market breadth was negative, with 614 decliners compared to 322 gainers. Additionally, 488 counters remained unchanged, 1,349 were untraded, and 12 were suspended. The turnover was recorded at 1.98 billion units valued at RM1.50 billion. Among the prominent stocks, Maybank decreased by three sen to RM9.96, Public Bank fell five sen to RM4.65, CIMB was down seven sen to RM7.72, Tenaga Nasional declined four sen to RM12.92, and IHH Healthcare dropped 16 sen to RM7.67. In active trading, Zetrix AI rose half a sen to 16.5 sen, VS Industry fell half a sen to 27.5 sen, Jaks Resources lost one sen to 19.5 sen, GB Bond retreated 2.5 sen to 22.5 sen, and Dagang Nexchange increased by 1.5 sen to 50 sen. Top gainers included Malaysian Pacific Industries, which surged RM1.34 to RM41.74, Ayer Holdings, up 20 sen to RM7.70, MI Technovation, rising 16 sen to RM5.36, Riverview Rubber Estates, strengthening 13 sen to RM3.03, and Vitrox, improving 11 sen to RM10.02. Among the top losers, Kuala Lumpur Kepong fell 72 sen to RM21.48, Allianz Malaysia dropped 62 sen to RM21.00, and United Plantations decreased 46 sen to RM31.10. Hong Leong Bank and Batu Kawan both fell 42 sen to RM22.72 and RM20.10, respectively. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index fell 103.44 points to 17,471.22, the FBM Emas Index decreased 117.43 points to 12,174.59, and the FBM Top 100 Index reduced by 121.55 points to 11,962.89. The FBM Emas Shariah Index weakened by 112.81 points to 12,063.54, while the FBM ACE Index decreased by 27.38 points to 5,506.90. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index fell 2.02 points to 178.39, the Energy Index eased 8.88 points to 836.82, the Financial Services Index dropped 168.21 points to 19,048.82, and the Plantation Index retreated 150.10 points to 9,046.57.

title: 'From F1 to the World Cup: How Anwar is using sport as diplomacy to put Malaysia on the world stage
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s approach of leveraging sports as a platform for diplomacy, economic activity and nation branding is helping position Malaysia back on the global sporting stage, according to an analyst. Global Peace Institute, London senior fellow Prof Dr Mohd Mizan Mohammad Aslam said Malaysia had, in recent months, demonstrated how global sporting events could be used not only to entertain the public but also to strengthen international relationships, generate economic activity and create a sense of shared national excitement. “Sport is often treated as entertainment, but for governments it can also be diplomacy, economic policy and nation branding rolled into one,” he said in a statement today. Formula 1’s return to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after nine years and Malaysia’s efforts to ensure access to the 2026 Fifa World Cup broadcasts demonstrated how sports could be used to strengthen the country’s international engagement. Mohd Mizan said Malaysia’s hosting of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2–4 demonstrated the international dimension of sports diplomacy, after the Bahrain Grand Prix could not proceed at its original venue due to geopolitical conditions in West Asia. He said the arrangement went beyond a commercial transaction involving a racetrack, as it was facilitated within the wider relationship between Malaysia and Bahrain, with the support of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa. Bahrain’s Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa also travelled to Malaysia and met Anwar during the race weekend. Mohd Mizan said Anwar’s attendance at the qualifying session at Sepang, visit to the Mercedes-AMG Petronas pit and participation in a reception hosted by Prince Salman further demonstrated how the sporting event created a platform for diplomatic engagement. “Sport had therefore created a diplomatic platform. Leaders met, bilateral relations were reinforced and Malaysia was placed before a global audience not through a formal summit but through one of the world’s most recognisable sporting spectacles,” he said. Mohd Mizan said the public response to F1’s return was equally significant, with around 95,000 three-day tickets sold by late September and SIC expecting sales to reach about 100,000, which would be the highest ticket sales recorded for races held at the circuit. He said the event also generated significant economic spillovers, with the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture estimating that it could draw around 300,000 tourists, including about 50,000 international visitors, while Hong Leong Bank Research projected an economic impact of approximately RM1.3 billion through sports tourism and foreign visitor spending. “Formula 1 does not benefit only the circuit. Visitors spend on hotels, restaurants, transport, retail and tourism. Television coverage carries images of Malaysia around the world. International teams, sponsors, journalists and corporate leaders arrive in the country,” he said. Turning to football, Mohd Mizan said the government’s decision to ensure Malaysians had access to the 2026 Fifa World Cup represented the domestic dimension of sports diplomacy, with football remaining one of the country’s most widely followed sports. RTM and Unifi TV were appointed official broadcasters, with all 104 matches made available through the participating platforms, while the government allocated RM26.2 million to secure the broadcasting rights and strategic cooperation with the private sector helped widen access and distribution, he said. title: 'Bursa opens marginally higher on easing US Treasury yields, Fed tone
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia rebounded to open marginally higher on Friday, as easing US Treasury yields and a measured tone from the Federal Reserve provided some relief to market sentiment.  At 9.10am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 1.49 points, or 0.09%, to 1,631.85 from Thursday’s close of 1,630.36.  The index opened 3.51 points higher at 1,633.87.  On the broader market, gainers outpaced losers 239 to 137, with 270 counters unchanged, 2,127 untraded and 24 suspended.  Turnover stood at 173.94 million shares worth RM95.98 million.  Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the latest decline had pushed the index back into oversold territory, which could have encouraged bargain hunting following the sharp correction.  “Against the reported foreign-selling backdrop, however, we believe any initial rebound may remain modest.  “Nonetheless, the weakness presents opportunities to selectively accumulate fundamentally sound stocks, particularly among established banks, utilities and semiconductor counters,” he noted.  Thong said a more sustainable recovery would require stronger participation from heavyweight counters and an improvement in market breadth.  Thus, he expects cautious trading today within the 1,625-1,640 range.  Among the heavyweights, Maybank was flat at RM9.95, while Public Bank and CIMB fell one sen to RM4.66 and RM7.68, respectively. Tenaga Nasional added four sen to RM12.94 and IHH Healthcare rose one sen to RM7.71.  In active trade, Zetrix AI, Jaks Resources and Genetec all remained unchanged at 16.5 sen, 18 sen and 32.5 sen, respectively. V.S Industry gained one sen to 28 sen, but Kinergy Advancement lost half a sen to 39.5 sen.  Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries advanced 58 sen to RM41.70, Hengyuan Refining inched up 19 sen to RM3.83, Petronas Chemicals perked up 15 sen to RM4.28, while UWC and MI Technovation both firmed 10 sen to RM7.20 and RM5.36, respectively.  MISC led the decliners, falling 14 sen to RM7.54, while LPI Capital, Hong Leong Industries, MNRB and RHB Bank shed four sen each to RM12.80, RM16.10, RM2.78 and RM7.43, respectively.  On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index ticked up 75.93 points to 17,434.91, the FBM Emas Index appreciated 17.18 points to 12,160.71, and the FBM Top 100 Index widened 21.58 points to 11,954.73.  The FBM Emas Shariah Index accumulated 34.76 points to 12,047.77, while the FBM ACE Index improved 18.61 points to 5,501.58.  Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index grew 1.10 points to 178.83, while the Energy Index gained 9.45 points to 844.46. The Financial Services Index fell 26.33 points to 19,034.58, while the Plantation Index ticked up 2.75 points to 9,029.32.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia dibuka tinggi
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia dibuka lebih tinggi pada Isnin, menjejaki kenaikan Wall Street berikutan pertumbuhan gaji Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang lebih perlahan, meredakan jangkaan kenaikan kadar faedah serta-merta oleh Rizab Persekutuan (Fed) AS. Pada 9.10 pagi, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 5.01 mata atau 0.31 peratus kepada 1,635.88 berbanding paras 1,630.87 ketika ditutup pada Jumaat. Indeks utama itu dibuka 2.55 mata lebih tinggi kepada 1,633.42. Sentimen pasaran secara keseluruhan positif dengan kaunter untung mengatasi kaunter rugi sebanyak 224 berbanding 158, sebanyak 337 kaunter tidak berubah, 2,054 tidak diniagakan dan 24 digantung dagangan. Jumlah dagangan berjumlah 206.30 juta saham bernilai RM98.78 juta. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, Thong Pak Leng, berkata hasil bon 10 tahun AS kekal tinggi pada paras 5.28 peratus manakala harga minyak mentah Brent ditutup pada AS$102.25 setong, menjadikan sentimen pasaran sensitif terhadap kadar faedah dan perkembangan di Asia Barat. "Di Hong Kong, Indeks Hang Seng susut di bawah paras 24,000 berikutan penyusutan saham sektor kewangan dan teknologi. "Di pasaran tempatan, susulan penutupan lebih tinggi FBM KLCI pada Jumaat lepas, kami menjangkakan kestabilan sementara dalam julat 1,625-1,635 hari ini, dengan aktiviti pembelian saham pada harga rendah memberikan sedikit sokongan di sebalik sentimen pasaran yang berhati-hati," katanya kepada Bernama. Saham wajaran tinggi menyaksikan Maybank, Public Bank, CIMB dan Tenaga Nasional menambah empat sen masing-masing kepada RM10.06, RN4.70, RM7.69, dan RM13.00, manakala IHH Healthcare berkurangan enam sen kepada RM7.74. Bagi saham aktif, VS Industry menambah tiga sen kepada 32 sen, Notion VTec naik empat sen kepada 74.5 sen, GB Bond meningkat setengah sen kepada 23.5 sen, SFP Tech menokok satu sen kepada 28.5 sen, manakala Dagang NeXchange tidak berubah pada 51.5 sen. Antara saham paling untung, Samaiden naik 19 sen kepada RM3.03, UWC meningkat 16 sen kepada RM7.73, Critical Holdings menokok 15 sen kepada RM2.61, Mi Technovation melonjak sembilan sen kepada RM5.30, dan Solarvest mengukuh lapan sen kepada RM4.25. Nestle mendahului saham paling rugi, susut 32 sen to RM89.20, manakala Vitrox merosot 14 sen kepada RM10.32, Kobay Technology berkurangan 12 sen kepada RM2.18, Kelington menguncup lima sen kepada RM8.58, dan YTL Power International turun empat sen kepada RM5.64. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 menambah 28.14 mata kepada 17,510.07, Indeks FBM Emas meningkat 33.81 mata kepada 12,204.38, Indeks FBM Top 100 naik 32.24 mata kepada 11,989.92, Indeks FBM Emas Syariah bertambah 22.28 mata kepada 12,082.60, manakala Indeks FBM ACE meningkat 31.41 mata kepada 5,560.87. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian naik 0.59 mata kepada 179.11, Indeks Tenaga naik 2.57 mata kepada 835.60, Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan meningkat 97.59 mata kepada 19,138.10, manakala Indeks Perladangan melonjak 2.23 mata kepada 9,058.78. - BERNAMA

title: 'Former UiTM Holdings CEO Charged With CBT of Misappropriating RM37 Mil
body: 'SHAH ALAM (Oct 1): A former chief executive officer of UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd (UHSB) has been charged with criminal breach of trust (CBT) for misappropriating RM37.4 million earmarked for solar power development. Azlizan Fadzil, who was in court in a wheelchair due to his stroke, pleaded not guilty and claimed trial before Sessions Court judge Datuk Mohd Nasir Nordin. The 52-year-old is accused of misappropriating RM37.4 million by making payments other than for the specified purpose of investment in a large-scale 50MW solar photovoltaic power generation development in Gambang, Pahang. The alleged offence took place between February and October 2017. The single charge is framed under Section 409 of the Penal Code and carries a penalty of imprisonment for a term between two to 20 years, whipping and a fine. UHSB is the wholly owned investment holding company of Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), generating wealth and creating commercial investment opportunities for the institute of higher learning. The court set bail at RM50,000 with two sureties, with additional conditions for the accused to report to authorities once every three months and not to disturb potential prosecution witnesses. Earlier, deputy public prosecutor Law Chin How proposed RM100,000 bail, citing the large sum involved, UiTM's reputation at stake and its high-profile nature which involves leakages of public funds. Defence counsel Hasshahari Johari Mawi asked for a lower bail of RM20,000 as his client has no independent income and is fully dependent on his wife and family. The lawyer added that the wife has to also care for seven children aged between 14 and 21 years old, who are all still schooling. Hasshahari also added that his client suffers from cognitive impairment and is not a flight risk. He added that his client has also been cooperative with authorities in their investigations. The case comes up for mention on Nov 3. title: 'MARC Ratings Affirms PNB Merdeka Ventures’ Sukuk Rating - MARC
body: 'MARC Ratings has affirmed the rating of AAAIS on PNB Merdeka Ventures Sdn Berhad’s (PNBMV) Merdeka Sukuk Wakalah Programme of up to RM6.0 billion with a stable outlook. The affirmed rating is equalised with the AAA/Stable corporate credit rating of Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB) which is based on publicly available information. The rating equalisation is premised on the unconditional and irrevocable rolling guarantee from PNB to cover any shortfall in principal repayments and profit payments on the Merdeka Sukuk Wakalah. PNBMV is wholly owned by PNB and was set up to undertake the 40-acre Merdeka 118 development in the vicinity of Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara in Kuala Lumpur. The development comprises several components, chiefly the 118-storey Menara Merdeka Maybank (formerly known as Menara Merdeka 118), a single tower with 84 floors of office space, a 17-floor luxury hotel and a three-floor observation deck. Adjacent to the tower are a seven-floor retail mall which is expected to open in November 2026, and sites earmarked for the future construction of two residential towers and a serviced apartment building. PNBMV is also the landowner and custodian of Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara, both of which are listed as National Heritage sites. PNBMV has leased the entire 84 floors of office space in the tower to PNB under a triple net master lease agreement. PNB undertakes all property-related expenses, including quit rent, insurance and repair costs, in addition to the monthly net rental and service charge. PNBMV is therefore not exposed to the occupancy risks or other risks associated with the office component of the tower. As at date, about 70% of the 1.6 million sq ft of net lettable area (NLA) of the office tower has been sub-leased: 40% or 33 floors to Maybank, 20% to PNB, and about 10% to other tenants. Occupancy is expected to increase to approximately 90% over the next five years. The office tower is expected to generate an annual net property income of around RM137.0 million. Lease agreements for 81% of the 750,324 sq ft of NLA in the retail mall have either been signed or are under negotiation to be signed with tenants at an indicative average rental rate of RM11.92/sq ft. 'MARC Ratings has affirmed the rating of AAAIS on PNB Merdeka Ventures Sdn Berhad’s (PNBMV) Merdeka Sukuk Wakalah Programme of up to RM6.0 billion with a stable outlook. The affirmed rating is equalised with the AAA/Stable corporate credit rating of Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB) which is based on publicly available information. The rating equalisation is premised on the unconditional and irrevocable rolling guarantee from PNB to cover any shortfall in principal repayments and profit payments on the Merdeka Sukuk Wakalah. PNBMV is wholly owned by PNB and was set up to undertake the 40-acre Merdeka 118 development in the vicinity of Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara in Kuala Lumpur. The development comprises several components, chiefly the 118-storey Menara Merdeka Maybank (formerly known as Menara Merdeka 118), a single tower with 84 floors of office space, a 17-floor luxury hotel and a three-floor observation deck. Adjacent to the tower are a seven-floor retail mall which is expected to open in November 2026, and sites earmarked for the future construction of two residential towers and a serviced apartment building. PNBMV is also the landowner and custodian of Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara, both of which are listed as National Heritage sites. PNBMV has leased the entire 84 floors of office space in the tower to PNB under a triple net master lease agreement. PNB undertakes all property-related expenses, including quit rent, insurance and repair costs, in addition to the monthly net rental and service charge. PNBMV is therefore not exposed to the occupancy risks or other risks associated with the office component of the tower. As at date, about 70% of the 1.6 million sq ft of net lettable area (NLA) of the office tower has been sub-leased: 40% or 33 floors to Maybank, 20% to PNB, and about 10% to other tenants. Occupancy is expected to increase to approximately 90% over the next five years. The office tower is expected to generate an annual net property income of around RM137.0 million. title: 'Doktor diperdaya bekas penyanyi, polis siasat penipuan pelaburan projek Kad Prihatin Siswa
body: 'Ampang Jaya: Polis sudah membuka kertas siasatan membabitkan penipuan pelaburan projek Kad Prihatin Siswa yang dikaitkan dengan sebuah syarikat milik seorang lelaki yang juga bapa kepada bekas penyanyi. Ketua Polis Daerah Ampang Jaya, Asisten Komisioner Khairul Anuar Khalid berkata, mangsa, doktor swasta berusia 38 tahun pada awal 2023 bersama suaminya berurusan dengan suspek berkaitan projek Kad Prihatin Siswa yang dikaitkan dengan sebuah syarikat secara bersemuka dan melalui WhatsApp. Menurutnya, suspek memperkenalkan projek terbabit sebagai pelaburan yang membabitkan 20 buah universiti dan kira-kira 620,000 pelajar serta menjanjikan pulangan keuntungan kepada pelabur. "Mangsa membuat lima kali transaksi pembayaran dengan jumlah keseluruhan sebanyak RM300,000 ke atas nombor akaun Maybank milik suspek sepanjang 2023. "Selepas daripada itu, satu perjanjian pelaburan ditandatangani yang menyatakan pelaburan sebanyak RM300,000 dengan keuntungan sebanyak 10 peratus sebulan selama 12 bulan dan modal akan dipulangkan pada tamat tempoh perjanjian," katanya dalam kenyataan hari ini. Beliau berkata, mangsa kemudiannya didaftarkan sebagai pemegang 10 peratus saham syarikat terbabit. "Bagaimanapun, keuntungan dan dividen yang dijanjikan tidak pernah diterima. Mangsa dan suami beberapa kali meminta penjelasan, pembayaran dividen serta salinan perjanjian yang dimatikan setem, namun suspek memberikan pelbagai alasan dan gagal memberikan penyelesaian. "Siasatan dijalankan mengikut Seksyen 420 Kanun Keseksaan dan tiada tangkapan setakat ini," katanya. Harian Metro hari ini melaporkan lelaki itu meyakinkan pelabur bahawa projek Kad Prihatin Siswa membabitkan 20 universiti mampu menjana pulangan lumayan dan kononnya ingin membantu lebih ramai orang Melayu kaya sepertinya. Itu taktik seorang lelaki bergelar Datuk yang juga bapa kepada bekas penyanyi memperdayakan pasangan doktor sehingga menyebabkan kerugian RM300,000 selepas melabur sejak 2023. Malah, dia turut mendakwa berkawan dengan pegawai tertinggi kerajaan dan kononnya minit mesyuarat projek ini juga sudah dihantar ke kerajaan dengan 620,000 pelajar akan menikmati kad terbabit hasil kerjasama dengan syarikat telekomunikasi terkenal.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Retreats After Opening Higher On Selling Pressure
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 – Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, but retreated shortly after as selling pressure in key financial and industrial heavyweights dragged down the benchmark index. At 9:11 AM, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 3.68 points to 1,629.67 compared to Tuesday’s close of 1,633.35. The benchmark index had initially opened 0.19 points higher at 1,633.54. Despite the drop in the main index, market breadth remained positive, with gainers outpacing decliners 221 to 180, while 306 counters were unchanged, 2,083 untraded, and 13 suspended. Total trading volume stood at 327.37 million units valued at RM150.56 million. Heavyweight Pressure and Active Stock Movements Selective profit-taking in banking and industrial counters pulled the composite index down by a combined 7.23 points: - Heavyweight Decliners: Hong Leong Bank slipped 10 sen to RM21.98, CIMB lost 15 sen to RM7.55, and Press Metal Aluminium dropped six sen to RM7.13. Additionally, AMMB fell five sen to RM6.42, Petronas Gas erased eight sen to RM17.20, and Mr D.I.Y. edged down one sen to RM1.24. - Heavyweight Gainers: IHH Healthcare gained three sen to RM7.94, while Maybank rose two sen to RM9.99. - Active Counters: Glovemakers saw buying momentum, with Top Glove advancing 5.5 sen to 93 sen and Supermax adding 2.5 sen to 48.5 sen. Zetrix AI and Ni Hsin both shed half a sen to 8.5 sen and 37 sen, respectively, while Metronic Global traded flat at half a sen. Top Market Movers and Sectoral Performance Technology and industrial stocks featured prominently among the morning’s top gainers and decliners: - Top Gainers: Malaysian Pacific Industries led gains, surging 62 sen to RM45.58, followed by Nestle (up 32 sen to RM91.58), Mi Technovation (up 19 sen to RM6.19), Critical Holdings (up 12 sen to RM2.81), and Hengyuan Refining Company (up nine sen to RM3.55). - Top Decliners: TMK Chemical fell eight sen to RM2.61, Pekat dropped five sen to RM2.91, while Stratus Global and Solarvest each lost four sen to RM3.09 and RM4.33, respectively. Malaysia Smelting declined three sen to RM1.65. On the broader index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index added 61.25 points to 17,795.36, the FBM Emas Shariah Index gained 26.12 points to 12,185.10, and the FBM ACE Index edged up 0.94 points to 5,659.86. Conversely, the FBM Emas Index shed 5.46 points to 12,227.41 and the FBM Top 100 Index dropped 9.15 points to 12,006.63. Across sectors, the Financial Services Index declined 134.06 points to 18,933.94, and the Industrial Products and Services Index dropped 0.09 points to 180.32. On the positive side, the Energy Index climbed 6.79 points to 847.51 and the Plantation Index gained 9.57 points to 9,051.74. –NMT

title: 'OPR berpotensi naik 25 mata asas tahun depan -MBSB Research
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR - Kadar Dasar Semalaman (OPR) Malaysia berpotensi meningkat sebanyak 25 mata asas pada 2027 didorong oleh jangkaan bahawa kadar faedah global terus meningkat, menurut MBSB Research.  Firma penyelidikan itu memaklumkan pasaran menjangka peningkatan 25 mata asas lagi untuk Kadar Dana Persekutuan (FFR) Amerika Syarikat (AS) menjelang akhir 2026, dengan negara lain berpotensi mengambil langkah yang sama.  “Terdapat kemungkinan kenaikan OPR sebanyak 25 mata asas — kenaikan sebanyak 50 mata asas dilihat sukar berikutan OPR tidak bergerak seiring dengan FFR dan inflasi tempatan adalah terkawal.  “Bagaimanapun, tiada keperluan mendesak untuk menaikkan OPR berikutan ekonomi domestik yang kukuh,” menurutnya dalam nota penyelidikan hari ini, sambil menambah sebarang kenaikan OPR dijangka pada 2027.  Kenaikan OPR secara amnya akan memberi manfaat kepada margin faedah bersih (NIM) bank berikutan hasil pinjaman yang lebih tinggi boleh menjadikan pendanaan borong lebih berdaya maju dan memberikan kelegaan daripada persaingan deposit.  Berdasarkan analisis senarionya, MBSB Research memaklumkan AmBank, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd, Public Bank Bhd dan RHB Bank Bhd berpotensi memperoleh manfaat NIM yang lebih besar daripada kenaikan kadar faedah manakala CIMB Group Holdings Bhd dan Malayan Banking Bhd dapat menghadapi impak daripada pendedahan terhadap pasaran Indonesia.  Secara keseluruhan, MBSB Research mengekalkan saranan positifnya terhadap sektor perbankan, disokong oleh prospek dividen, pertumbuhan pinjaman perniagaan, pendapatan fi dan kawalan perbelanjaan operasi walaupun terdapat beberapa faktor berkaitan pertumbuhan, terutamanya pinjaman perniagaan dan pendapatan pengurusan kekayaan, dijangka tidak berpanjangan.  — BERNAMA

title: 'Mateen perlu RM8,000 beli ‘stroller’ khas
body: 'PETALING JAYA – Bayi hidrosefalus, Muhammad Mateen Aryan Muhammad Hanif, 15 bulan, dari Sungai Petani, Kedah, kini semakin aktif namun pergerakannya terbatas disebabkan kepalanya yang berat. Bapanya, Muhammad Hanif Zakaria, 32, berkata, Mateen kini cuba menggerakkan badan dan memusingkan badan, tetapi sukar berbuat demikian dengan kepala yang mencecah ukuran 90 sentimeter (cm). “Perkembangan dia okey. Dia pun cuba bergerak, nak pusing badannya, tetapi tak boleh sebab kepala dia berat,” katanya ketika dihubungi Kosmo!. Menurut Muhammad Hanif, keadaan Mateen kini semakin baik apabila sawan yang dialaminya semakin berkurang, namun apabila serangan berlaku, saiz kepala anaknya boleh kembali membesar. “Sejak kami mendapatkan rawatan alternatif, Mateen semakin kurang diserang sawan dan saiz kepala dia turun sedikit ke 89cm. Tapi apabila kena sawan, automatik saiz tu boleh naik balik,” ujarnya. Muhammad Hanif berkata, keperluan asas Matten kini mencukupi dan berterima kasih kepada pihak yang pernah membantu, namun dia dan isteri kini merancang untuk mendapatkan kereta sorong (stroller) khas bagi memudahkan pergerakan Mateen. Bagaimanapun dia menjelaskan, ia perlu ditempah khas mengikut keperluan Mateen, dengan anggaran kos sebanyak RM8,000 dan akan berbuat demikian apabila jumlah itu mencukupi. Orang ramai yang ingin membantu keluarga itu mendapatkan kereta sorong berkenaan, boleh menyalurkan sumbangan ke akaun bank CIMB bernombor 7632966954 di atas nama Muhammad Hanif. Terdahulu Kosmo! melaporkan, Muhammad Hanif yang bekerja sebagai pemandu lori bersyukur kerana anak bongsu daripada tiga beradik itu tidak pernah menangis kesakitan sejak lahir. Dia dan isteri, Habidah Nasruddin, 31, bagaimanapun berdepan kesukaran mengangkat Mateen disebabkan kepalanya yang makin membesar. The post Mateen perlu RM8,000 beli ‘stroller’ khas appeared first on Kosmo Online.
