title: '13th PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia with iProperty honours real estate excellence - Newswav
body: 'Top developers celebrated the 13th PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia in partnership with iProperty, presented by Lim Soh & Goonting Advocates & Solicitors, at The St. Regis Kuala Lumpur. Guided by the theme “Defined by Excellence,” the 2026 PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia with iProperty recognised the country’s best in real estate across 62 categories. From township developers to breakthrough companies, this year’s awards were comprehensive, honouring the best in different real estate segments and regions. Timber Land Group won the evening’s top honour, Best Developer, marking its first-ever win in the category, in addition to Best Developer (East Malaysia). CPI Land was named Best Developer (Central Malaysia) alongside award-winning project Tuan Straits. Tanah Sutera took both Best Developer (Southern Malaysia) and Best Landed Homes Developer, buoyed by winning project The Seed. JLand Group, named Best Township Developer, collected the most awards of any company, covering Developer, Development, and Design categories for projects including Arena Larkin; Bandar Tiram; Ibrahim Technopolis (IBTEC) – Aspiration Park; Ibrahim Technopolis (IBTEC) – STeP West; and Medora One. JRK Holdings Berhad won both Best Breakthrough Developer and Best Boutique Developer. Keck Seng (Malaysia) Berhad was named Best Mixed Use Developer, also winning for the project Daya 1 Residences, Taman Daya. Penang developers also made their mark at this year’s awards, with PTL Properties, Aspen and Pinnacle Group among the winners. PTL Properties was named Best Lifestyle Developer, with The Rimbun also winning Best Mass Market Landed Development (Northern) and Best Townhouse Development. Aspen’s Aspen Vision City received the Best Township Development (Northern) award, while Pinnacle Group won Best Premium High-Rise Development (Northern) for Pinnacle Bukit Gambier. Other companies with winning projects include Amalan Setar (M) Sdn Bhd, which won for Ixora Garden – Sari Alamanda 4 Phase 2; Armani Group (Armani Hallson Bukit Bintang); Astaka Kimlun Sdn Bhd (Amora Serviced Residence); BCB Land Sdn. Bhd. (Straya Heights); Coronade Properties Sdn Bhd (Coronation Square; Coronade Twins – Serviced Residences); CTC Development Malaysia Sdn Bhd (CTC Skyone @ Bukit Chagar); Faire Development (bée); Gunung Impian Development Sdn Bhd (Taman Impian Emas); Infra Park Sdn Bhd (MLIMA Kiara); KEB Berhad (Residensi Cove @ Kota Syahbandar); Matrix Concepts (Levia Residence Puchong); OCR Templer Sdn Bhd (D’Templer Hilltop Residences); Peter’s Group (Cherita Residences); Puncak Concept Sdn Bhd (Puncak LakePark City @ Cyberjaya); R&F Development Sdn Bhd (R&F Princess Cove); Steadfast Properties (Laguna Residences); Tiram Industrial Park Sdn Bhd (Akasia Business Park); Tropicana Corporation Berhad (Clarissa Serviced Suites, Tropicana Cenang); UEM Sunrise Berhad (Intrika, Serene Heightshase s); and Worldwide Holdings Berhad (Pavonia Worldwide, Bukit Bandaraya Shah Alam). Outstanding real estate figures The 13th PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia with iProperty celebrated some of the impactful figures in Malaysian real estate. Tan Sri Dato’ Seri Dr. Jeffrey Cheah KBE AO, founder and chairman of Sunway Group, received the Life Achievement Award. Dato’ Seri Azmir Merican, group managing director and chief executive officer of Sime Darby Property, was named Real Estate Personality of the Year. Dato’ Sri Edwin Tan Pei Seng, executive chairman of Paragon Globe Berhad, was honoured as Rising Star, while Ms. Maggie Ng Mui Kit, chief executive officer of Kuok Group Property Division (Southern), received the Woman Changemaker Award. Consumers, catalysts, and consistency The Consumer Demand Award continued this year, recognising the property that captured the strongest genuine interest from Malaysian property seekers. Determined by consumer views and leads across PropertyGuru.com.my and iProperty.com.my, Leisure Farm Resort by Mulpha International was named Most In-Demand Bungalow/Villa, in addition to winning Best Resort-Style Township Development. The People’s Choice Awards also continued the tradition of tapping consumer opinion to identify the nation’s 10 favourite developers. This year, 15,383 votes were cast for developers that consumers in Malaysia admire and trust. The winners of the People’s Choice Awards in 2026 are: Berinda Group; Coronade Properties Sdn Bhd; CPI Land; Gunung Impian Development Sdn Bhd; JLand Group; KEB Berhad; Matrix Concepts; Pinnacle Group; Tropicana Corporation Berhad; and UEM Sunrise Berhad. In addition, PropertyGuru.com.my and iProperty.com.my presented several titles for the first time this year. IIB Experience Centre (IIBEX) by Iskandar Investment Berhad received the inaugural Real Estate Ecosystem Catalyst Award. The Consistency Excellence Awards also made their debut, recognising companies with consecutive years of wins at the awards. Gunung Impian Development Sdn Bhd won the 4-Year Consistency Excellence Award. Meanwhile, the 3-Year Consistency Excellence Awards were presented to Armani Group; Astaka Padu Sdn Bhd; Berinda Group; Coronade Properties Sdn Bhd; Iskandar Investment Berhad; JLand Group; R&F Development Sdn Bhd; and Tropicana Corporation Berhad. Live selection process Winners of the competitive categories were selected during the Live Judging Days from 30 June to 2 July 2026 at the Amari Hotel Kuala Lumpur. The evaluation process, independently supervised by HLB Ler Lum Chew, saw a multi-disciplinary panel from Malaysia’s leading professional bodies assess an expanded lineup of categories. This year’s panel was chaired by Datuk Ar. Ezumi Harzani Ismail, president of the Malaysian Institute of Architects (PAM) from 2020 to 2022, and included Ir. Ashwin Thurairajah, executive director, GreenRE Sdn Bhd; YBrs. Sr. Haji Ishak Ismail, president, Malaysian Institute of Property & Facility Managers (MIPFM) 2023–2027; Ms. Janice Chin, senior director, Capital Markets, JLL Appraisal & Property Services Sdn Bhd; Prof. Dr. Ir. Jeffrey Chiang Choong Luin, president, The Institution of Engineers Malaysia (IEM) 2024–2026; Dato’ Sr. Lau Wai Seang, president, Royal Institution of Surveyors Malaysia (RISM) 2017–2018; TPr. Mazrina Dato’ Abdul Khalid, president, Malaysian Institute of Planners (MIP) 2025–2027; Assoc. Prof. LAr. Dr. Nor Atiah Ismail, president, Institute of Landscape Architects Malaysia (ILAM) 2024–2026; Adj. Prof. IDr. Norshafina Ibrahim, president, Malaysian Institute of Interior Designers (MIID) 2024–2026; Mr. Oliver Wee, president, Master Builders Association Malaysia (MBAM) 2024–2026; Ar. Sarly Adre Sarkum, chief executive officer, Green Building Index (GBI); Ar. Dr. Serina Hijjas, president, Malaysia Green Building Council (MGBC) 2023–2027; and Ms. Tan Hui Yin, partner, Tan Chap & Associates. Datuk Ar. Ezumi Harzani Ismail said: “Good design is the product of discipline, clarity of intent, and an understanding of how people inhabit space. What struck me most among this year’s winners was a shared design intelligence: sensitivity to context and climate, thoughtful handling of landscape and light, and a commitment to sustainability that goes beyond token gestures. From the elegant restraint of landed homes to the confident lines of high-rise towers, these projects show that Malaysian design has matured into something both internationally credible and distinctly our own. And with quality consistent across every tier, good design is not a privilege of the few but a standard we can deliver for all. On behalf of the judging panel, I congratulate every winner for raising the bar for Malaysian real estate.” Jules Kay, managing director of PropertyGuru Asia Property Awards and Events, said: “This year’s awardees share a commitment to thoughtful placemaking, sustainable design, and creating developments that enhance the way people live, work, and connect. From transformative township masterplans to beautifully crafted landed homes, this year’s winners show that excellence equals lasting value for communities. We are proud to celebrate developers that deliver value and quality to homebuyers. We also celebrate the individual leaders whose passion and foresight continue to inspire the industry. Together, these achievements set a benchmark for Malaysian real estate.” Winners may advance to the PropertyGuru Asia Property Awards Grand Final, recognising the Best in Asia on 11 December 2026 at The Athenee Hotel, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Bangkok. title: 'Maybank completes Maybank Ageas buyout
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has completed the acquisition of the remaining 30.95 per cent stake in Maybank Ageas Holdings Bhd. This gives the banking group full ownership of the holding company for its Etiqa insurance and takaful business in Malaysia and Singapore. The transaction follows Maybank's share purchase agreement with Ageas Insurance International NV on Sept 8 and regulatory approval from Bank Negara Malaysia received on Sept 1. With the completion, Maybank Ageas becomes a wholly owned subsidiary of Maybank. Maybank president and group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Khairussaleh Ramli said the acquisition marks a significant milestone as the group seeks to strengthen Etiqa's position as a national insurance and takaful champion, while expanding its footprint across Southeast Asia. He said the move also supports Maybank's ROAR30 strategy to build a stronger regional franchise and establish a global takaful powerhouse. "With Maybank Ageas being a wholly owned subsidiary of Maybank, it strengthens Etiqa's position as a national insurance and takaful champion, driving deeper penetration of Maybank's customer base," said Khairussaleh. Full ownership is expected to give Maybank greater flexibility to integrate its banking, wealth and protection offerings, particularly across its regional customer base. Khairussaleh said Maybank intends to unlock further value through cross-selling and more integrated, personalised financial solutions. The acquisition should also support more effective capital management within Maybank Ageas and at the wider Maybank group level, potentially improving the insurance business's efficiency and resilience. Etiqa will continue to operate as one of Maybank's key brands, offering life and general conventional insurance alongside family and general takaful products through multiple distribution channels. "The Etiqa brand remains a strong and well-established insurance and takaful franchise, and it will continue to be positioned as one of Maybank's flagship brands," said Khairussaleh. With Maybank's extensive customer base and distribution network behind it, Etiqa is expected to pursue growth opportunities as demand rises for more integrated and personalised protection solutions. Maybank also acknowledged Ageas' contribution to the development of the Etiqa franchise over the past 25 years.

title: 'Maybank IB upgrades SD Guthrie to ‘buy’ post sell-off, cites market overreaction to PNB's exchangeable sukuk
body:
'

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 15): Shares of SD Guthrie Bhd (KL:SDG) have been upgraded to "buy" from "hold" in the near term by Maybank Investment Bank after an "unwarranted" sell-off following Permodalan Nasional Bhd’s (PNB) latest exchangeable sukuk issuance. 

The research house said despite recent share price weakness, the plantation group's fundamentals remain intact. 

It added that the selldown was largely driven by market overreaction to PNB’s US$300 million (RM1.22 billion) exchangeable sukuk (ES), which has no earnings per share (EPS) impact on SD Guthrie.

SD Guthrie shares increased from RM6.14 on Sept 9, the day PNB announced the exchangeable sukuk, to RM6.34 at time of writing on Tuesday. The latest price values the group at RM43.85 billion.

"With the ES issued last week, we believe concerns over ES potential overhang are over and largely misunderstood," Maybank IB said in a note on Tuesday.

Because the sukuk was issued by PNB rather than SD Guthrie, there will be no new share issuance if investors exercise their options. 

Furthermore, there must be a significant price appreciation before conversion rights can be exercised.

Maybank IB estimates SD Guthrie's share price would need to hit at least RM8.66, which is well above current trading levels, before sukuk investors can exchange them for the stock.

"We believe the recent selldown has been unwarranted as nothing has fundamentally changed the past month except for an US$300 million exchangeable sukuk (ES) issued by PNB," Maybank IB added.

The stock upgrade comes as Maybank IB projects SD Guthrie's core net profit to be RM2.9 billion for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY2026), which is 5% above the broader market consensus of RM2.76 billion. 

However, long-term consensus expectations lean higher than the research house's forecasts.

According to Bloomberg data, the broader market sentiment on SD Guthrie remains positive, with 14 out of 18 research houses rating the stock as a "buy", two recommending "hold" and two "outperform" calls. 

The Bloomberg consensus 12-month target price stands at RM7.65, a potential upside of 20.9% from current trading levels.

Maybank IB said SD Guthrie's growth would be centred on new business verticals, including industrial park joint developments spanning over 20,000 acres to sustain RM500 million to RM700 million annual income, alongside its goal of developing one gigawatt in large-scale solar projects.

Maybank IB maintained its target price of RM7.10 based on 0.55 times revised net asset value (RNAV).

An interim dividend per share of 11.18 sen declared in its 1HFY2026 results will go ex-date on Oct 20.

PNB issues second US$300 mil exchangeable sukuk

title: 'Maybank emerges as top winner at inaugural Bursa Malaysia IR Awards 2026
body:
'

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 7): Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) emerged as the biggest winner at the inaugural Bursa Malaysia IR Awards 2026 that was held last Friday, sweeping home three awards including Best Financial Reporting and the flagship Best Company in IR.

Capping the hattrick win for the company was its sectoral win as Best Large-Cap company in IR for Financial Services while its president and group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Khairussaleh Ramli was named Best CEO in IR.

The awards honoured a total of 32 winners across eight main categories, celebrating public listed companies (PLCs) and investor relations professionals who have demonstrated a strong commitment to investor engagement, market communication and corporate transparency, Bursa said in a statement on Monday.

The eight categories are:

  1. Best Company in IR (overall)
  2. Best Financial Reporting
  3. Best Sustainability Communications
  4. Best IPO Company in IR
  5. Best CEO in IR
  6. Best CFO in IR
  7. Best Large-cap Company in IR by Sector (across 13 sectors)
  8. Best Mid/Small-cap Company in IR by Sector (across 13 sectors)

Other notable winners include Tenaga Nasional Bhd (KL:TENAGA), which took home twin awards for Best Sustainability Communications and Best Large-cap Company in IR for Utilities, and Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd (KL:KOPI), which was named Best IPO Company in IR. 

The other individual award — the Best CFO in IR — went to Malkit Singh Maan of Hong Leong Bank Bhd (KL:HLBANK).

Effective investor relations is important in strengthening the quality and competitiveness of Malaysia's listed companies, said Treasury secretary general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican when delivering the keynote address at the awards celebrations.

“By communicating openly and consistently with investors, public listed companies enable better-informed investment decisions and demonstrate their commitment to transparency and accountability. As we continue enhancing the competitiveness and quality of Malaysia’s listed companies, effective investor engagement will remain an enabler of long-term value creation and sustainable market growth,” Johan said.

The inaugural awards aimed to recognise companies and professionals who are setting a high standard for transparency, engagement and market communication, said Bursa CEO Datuk Fad'l Mohamed.

"By spotlighting these practices, we hope to encourage more listed companies to strengthen their investor relations capabilities and help raise standards of investor engagement across the market," he said.

He also noted that there is considerable opportunity to strengthen IR capabilities across the market and enhance issuer-investor engagement across the market.

Based on Bursa's research, only 32% of listed companies have a dedicated internal IR function while 17% outsource the function and 51% operate without any formal IR structure.

The exchange operator and regulator said it has been building IR capabilities in the capital market through IR4U by providing practical guidance and learning opportunities for PLCs, which saw the participation of about 690 listed companies throughout 2024 and 2025.

These efforts are complemented by MY Value Up, the national capital market initiative jointly launched by the Securities Commission Malaysia and Bursa to encourage companies to strengthen fundamentals while articulating their strategies and priorities more clearly to the market.

The complete list of award winners will be featured in a special pullout in The Edge Malaysia weekly.

title: 'Optimistic outlook for equities in fourth quarter
body: 'PETALING JAYA: Malaysia’s resilient domestic economy, alongside Budget 2027, should support the local stock market in the fourth quarter of 2026 (4Q26), although geopolitical uncertainty and elevated global yields could keep a lid on valuations, says MBSB Research. In a strategy report, the research house said it remained “optimistic but cautious” on Malaysian equities, favouring defensive sectors while selectively taking on growth exposure. The research house said market direction in 4Q26 would depend on whether the Strait of Hormuz begins to reopen, oil and freight costs moderate, and the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) September rate hike proves to be an adjustment rather than the start of a prolonged tightening cycle. It said Malaysia’s resilient economic growth, corporate earnings and domestic liquidity should provide downside support, while Budget 2027 could bring renewed attention to domestic catalysts. However, sustained oil prices above US$100 a barrel, further Fed rate hikes and persistently elevated bond yields could continue to weigh on valuations and foreign fund flows. Despite heightened external uncertainties, MBSB Research said growth should remain well anchored, with the strong first-half (1H26) performance providing a solid base for the rest of the year, “which we expect to remain reassuring in 3Q26”. Even under more adverse scenarios, the research house said full-year growth should remain above 4%, given the strong 1H26 performance. “Into 2027, we favour sectors combining near-term catalysts with recurring demand, pricing power and resilience against prolonged external disruption,” it said. “Preference should remain with companies offering visible earnings, recurring demand, balance-sheet strength, dividend support and direct exposure to Malaysia’s domestic investment cycle.” Against this backdrop, the research house favours utilities, telecommunications, consumer staples and healthcare for their resilient earnings, while construction and technology offer exposure to growth. MBSB Research also recommended retaining exposure to plantations and energy-related stocks as protection against external uncertainty in 4Q26. Plantations could benefit from firm crude palm oil prices, biodiesel demand and ringgit weakness, while energy infrastructure and shipping should remain relevant amid normalising trade and potential supply disruptions, it said. MBSB Research expects Malaysia’s economic growth to moderate to 4.6% in 2027 from a forecast 5.1% this year, having expanded 5.7% year-on-year in 1H26. It said the moderation largely reflected normalisation from a relatively high base rather than a material weakening in underlying economic conditions. The research firm said domestic demand should remain supportive, underpinned by healthy labour market conditions, positive wage growth and continued investment activity, while external trade should continue to benefit from resilient electrical and electronics (E&E) demand. Still, MBSB Research said the outlook for 2027 remained clouded by geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainties, including the US midterm elections, conflicts involving the United States, Iran and Israel, risks around the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, inflation and the path of monetary policy. “A change in any one of these variables could materially alter the direction of energy prices, interest rates, global growth and financial markets, making a single-point forecast inadequate,” it noted. The research house said the next major political event to watch was the US midterm elections on Nov 3, which will determine control of the US House of Representatives and Senate. The research house said the election would not directly determine the actions of Iran, Israel or the Houthis, but could affect areas including war funding, sanctions, congressional oversight, the legal basis for military operations and the political cost of sustaining the blockade. Under its baseline scenario, where Malaysia’s economy grows 4.6% in 2027, MBSB Research expects corporate earnings to expand 6.6% and has set a preliminary FBM KLCI target of 1,850 points. The target is based on a forecast 2027 price-to-earnings ratio (PER) of 15.4 times, compared with the FBM KLCI’s current 2026 PER of 14.8 times. “Underpinned by our baseline expectations of resilient macro performance along with healthy earnings growth next year, we expect equity valuations to improve going forward,” it said. It expects the local equity market to benefit from an anticipated easing of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, with Brent crude oil prices expected to decline towards US$75 to US$85 per barrel. Under a more adverse scenario, MBSB Research sees GDP growth slowing to 3.2%, with earnings growth moderating to 4.5%. In this scenario, it has set a lower FBM KLCI target of 1,730 points based on a PER of 14.7 times. Separately, CIMB Research said changes to the rules governing the expanded FBM KLCI should give the 50-stock index a wider buffer against frequent changes in its constituents. The FBM KLCI is set to expand to 50 constituents from 30, with the new structure taking effect from the December 2026 semi-annual index review. FTSE Russell, which manages the index, has revised the entry and exit thresholds to reduce the frequency of stocks moving in and out of the index. Under the new rules, a stock must rank among the top 40 by full market capitalisation to qualify for inclusion, compared with the top 25 previously, while existing constituents will only be removed if they fall to 61st or below, compared with 36th previously. CIMB Research said the wider gap between the inclusion and deletion thresholds should reduce index churn. FTSE Russell has also lowered the fast- entry threshold to 1% of FBM Emas market capitalisation from 2%. Based on Aug 28 data, CIMB Research said this translates into an estimated market capitalisation threshold of RM18.1bil, compared with RM36.3bil previously. The research house said the lower threshold should allow large newly listed companies to enter the KLCI more quickly if they meet the other eligibility requirements.

title: 'Jamin peruntukan awam universiti, hentikan korporatisasi UiTM – Suara Siswa UiTM
body: 'Suara Siswa UiTM menggesa Kementerian Pendidikan Tinggi (KPT) dan Kementerian Kewangan menjamin peruntukan awam yang mencukupi dan berterusan kepada universiti awam, susulan perkembangan terbaharu berkaitan UiTM Holdings yang, menurut kumpulan itu, mencerminkan masalah lebih besar dalam model pembiayaan pendidikan tinggi. Kumpulan mahasiswa itu berkata pengakuan Menteri Pendidikan Tinggi Zambry Kadir pada 27 September bahawa kerajaan tidak lagi menanggung sepenuhnya keperluan kewangan universiti sejak 2017 menunjukkan universiti awam semakin didorong mencari sumber pendapatan sendiri, termasuk melalui syarikat pegangan, pelaburan dan kegiatan komersial. KPT pada masa sama mengakui sebahagian syarikat pegangan universiti tidak berfungsi dengan baik, dan proses meneliti serta menyusun semula syarikat berkenaan telah dimulakan sejak tahun lalu. Menurut Suara Siswa UiTM, UiTM Holdings tidak wajar dilihat semata-mata sebagai sebuah syarikat yang mengalami masalah kewangan. KPT sebelum ini mengesahkan kerugian sebelum cukai terkumpul UiTM Holdings sekitar RM157j bagi 2017, 2018, 2019 dan 2021, manakala Jawatankuasa Kira-Kira Wang Negara (PAC) pernah merekodkan suntikan modal UiTM berjumlah RM260j juta kepada syarikat itu antara 2007 hingga 2018 serta membangkitkan isu pematuhan dan tadbir urus. Kumpulan itu berkata perkembangan berkenaan perlu dibaca bersama dasar kewangan pendidikan tinggi negara. Menurut Pelan Pembangunan Pendidikan Tinggi Malaysia 2015-25 (PPPM) merekodkan sumbangan kerajaan kepada universiti awam bukan universiti penyelidikan turun daripada 85% perbelanjaan operasi pada 2015 kepada 76% pada 2022, sementara pendapatan dijana sendiri meningkat daripada 21% kepada 22%. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Dokumen itu mengenal pasti kemampanan kewangan sebagai cabaran utama institut pengajian tinggi. Suara Siswa UiTM berkata keadaan itu menunjukkan universiti awam semakin diletakkan di bawah tekanan untuk mencapai kelestarian kewangan melalui penjanaan pendapatan, termasuk pelaburan, kegiatan komersial, konsultansi dan model perniagaan baharu. PPPM secara jelas meletakkan penjanaan pendapatan, pendanaan berasaskan prestasi dan model perniagaan inovatif sebagai sebahagian daripada agenda kelestarian kewangan institusi. [Hala tuju ini diteruskan dan diperkukuh dalam Rancangan Pendidikan Tinggi Malaysia 2026-35.] “Kami melihat persoalan UiTM Holdings sebagai sebahagian daripada masalah korporatisasi pendidikan tinggi,” kata kumpulan itu. “Apabila pembiayaan awam dikurangkan, risiko kewangan tidak hilang, tetapi dipindahkan kepada universiti untuk ditanggung melalui pasaran dan akhirnya kepada mahasiswa melalui pelbagai bentuk kos pendidikan dan sara hidup.” Suara Siswa UiTM menggesa kerajaan mengembalikan pembiayaan awam sebagai asas utama kewangan universiti, dengan peruntukan KPT dan Kementerian Kewangan yang mencukupi untuk menanggung fungsi teras seperti pengajaran, penyelidikan, penyelenggaraan kampus dan kebajikan mahasiswa tanpa memaksa universiti bergantung kepada keuntungan aktiviti komersial. Kumpulan itu turut menyeru supaya yuran dan kos wajib pendidikan dikurangkan secara berperingkat sehingga pendidikan tinggi awam dapat dinyahkomodifikasikan. Kumpulan mahasiswa itu turut menuntut supaya sebarang penyusunan semula UiTM Holdings tidak berakhir dengan sekadar mencari model perniagaan baharu atau menutup kerugian melalui suntikan dana awam tanpa perubahan struktur. Ia mahu kerajaan menilai semula aktiviti komersial universiti berdasarkan kepentingan pendidikan dan masyarakat, di samping memastikan pekerja universiti tidak menjadi pihak yang menanggung kesan penstrukturan. Dalam perkembangan berasingan, Suruhanjaya Pencegah Rasuah Malaysia mengesahkan siasatan terhadap UiTM Holdings masih berjalan dan melibatkan isu teknikal serta kelemahan tadbir urus, termasuk dakwaan pembayaran RM42j berkaitan projek solar 50MW di Gambang, yang dikatakan dibuat tanpa kelulusan lembaga pengarah dan bagi tujuan yang tidak berkaitan dengan projek. Suara Siswa UiTM berkata sebarang pertuduhan jenayah hendaklah tertakluk kepada hasil siasatan dan proses undang-undang, namun isu tadbir urus dan model pembiayaan universiti boleh dipersoalkan secara berasingan. “Universiti awam tidak sepatutnya dipaksa menjadi perusahaan yang mencari keuntungan untuk membiayai fungsi awamnya,” kata kumpulan itu. “Peruntukan pendidikan ialah tanggungjawab negara, manakala kekayaan dan aset universiti harus diprioritikan untuk mahasiswa, pekerja, pengajaran, penyelidikan dan kepentingan masyarakat.” – Suara Siswa UiTM The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. 'Suara Siswa UiTM menggesa Kementerian Pendidikan Tinggi (KPT) dan Kementerian Kewangan menjamin peruntukan awam yang mencukupi dan berterusan kepada universiti awam, susulan perkembangan terbaharu berkaitan UiTM Holdings yang, menurut kumpulan itu, mencerminkan masalah lebih besar dalam model pembiayaan pendidikan tinggi. Kumpulan mahasiswa itu berkata pengakuan Menteri Pendidikan Tinggi Zambry Kadir pada 27 September bahawa kerajaan tidak lagi menanggung sepenuhnya keperluan kewangan universiti sejak 2017 menunjukkan universiti awam semakin didorong mencari sumber pendapatan sendiri, termasuk melalui syarikat pegangan, pelaburan dan kegiatan komersial. KPT pada masa sama mengakui sebahagian syarikat pegangan universiti tidak berfungsi dengan baik, dan proses meneliti serta menyusun semula syarikat berkenaan telah dimulakan sejak tahun lalu. Menurut Suara Siswa UiTM, UiTM Holdings tidak wajar dilihat semata-mata sebagai sebuah syarikat yang mengalami masalah kewangan. KPT sebelum ini mengesahkan kerugian sebelum cukai terkumpul UiTM Holdings sekitar RM157j bagi 2017, 2018, 2019 dan 2021, manakala Jawatankuasa Kira-Kira Wang Negara (PAC) pernah merekodkan suntikan modal UiTM berjumlah RM260j juta kepada syarikat itu antara 2007 hingga 2018 serta membangkitkan isu pematuhan dan tadbir urus. Kumpulan itu turut menyeru supaya yuran dan kos wajib pendidikan dikurangkan secara berperingkat sehingga pendidikan tinggi awam dapat dinyahkomodifikasikan. Kumpulan mahasiswa itu turut menuntut supaya sebarang penyusunan semula UiTM Holdings tidak berakhir dengan sekadar mencari model perniagaan baharu atau menutup kerugian melalui suntikan dana awam tanpa perubahan struktur. Ia mahu kerajaan menilai semula aktiviti komersial universiti berdasarkan kepentingan pendidikan dan masyarakat, di samping memastikan pekerja universiti tidak menjadi pihak yang menanggung kesan penstrukturan. title: 'Stock Today: Maybank Gains 0.5% After ASB Disposal
body: 'Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) rose 0.5% in late morning trade on Friday, despite Amanah Saham Bumiputera (ASB) having disposed of 13 million shares in the bank earlier this week.  As of 10.56am, Maybank gained five sen to RM10.00, after opening at RM9.95. The stock traded between RM9.93 and RM10.02 during the session.  Some 1.33 million shares had changed hands, with the last done price above the previous adjusted close of RM9.95.  At the time, 598,000 shares were queued to buy at RM9.99 while 1.52 million shares were queued to sell at RM10.00.  Maybank disclosed on Oct 1 that AmanahRaya Trustees Bhd, as trustee for ASB, had disposed of 13 million shares on Sept 29 through a sale of shares.  Following the disposal, ASB’s direct stake in Maybank stood at 3.418 billion shares, representing 28.261% of the bank’s issued shares.  The notice of change in substantial shareholding was dated Sept 29 and received by Maybank on Oct 1.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia dibuka tinggi, jejaki peningkatan di Wall Street
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, 5 Oktober: Bursa Malaysia dibuka lebih tinggi pada Isnin, menjejaki kenaikan Wall Street berikutan pertumbuhan gaji Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang lebih perlahan, meredakan jangkaan kenaikan kadar faedah serta-merta oleh Rizab Persekutuan (Fed) AS. Pada 9.10 pagi, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 5.01 mata atau 0.31 peratus kepada 1,635.88 berbanding paras 1,630.87 ketika ditutup pada Jumaat. Indeks utama itu dibuka 2.55 mata lebih tinggi kepada 1,633.42. Sentimen pasaran secara keseluruhan positif dengan kaunter untung mengatasi kaunter rugi sebanyak 224 berbanding 158, sebanyak 337 kaunter tidak berubah, 2,054 tidak diniagakan dan 24 digantung dagangan. Jumlah dagangan berjumlah 206.30 juta saham bernilai RM98.78 juta. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, Thong Pak Leng berkata hasil bon 10 tahun AS kekal tinggi pada paras 5.28 peratus manakala harga minyak mentah Brent ditutup pada US$102.25 setong, menjadikan sentimen pasaran sensitif terhadap kadar faedah dan perkembangan di Asia Barat. “Di Hong Kong, Indeks Hang Seng susut di bawah paras 24,000 berikutan penyusutan saham sektor kewangan dan teknologi. “Di pasaran tempatan, susulan penutupan lebih tinggi FBM KLCI pada Jumaat lepas, kami menjangkakan kestabilan sementara dalam julat 1,625-1,635 hari ini, dengan aktiviti pembelian saham pada harga rendah memberikan sedikit sokongan di sebalik sentimen pasaran yang berhati-hati,” katanya kepada Bernama. Saham wajaran tinggi menyaksikan Maybank, Public Bank, CIMB dan Tenaga Nasional menambah empat sen masing-masing kepada RM10.06, RN4.70, RM7.69, dan RM13.00, manakala IHH Healthcare berkurangan enam sen kepada RM7.74. Bagi saham aktif, VS Industry menambah tiga sen kepada 32 sen, Notion VTec naik empat sen kepada 74.5 sen, GB Bond meningkat setengah sen kepada 23.5 sen, SFP Tech menokok satu sen kepada 28.5 sen, manakala Dagang NeXchange tidak berubah pada 51.5 sen. Antara saham paling untung, Samaiden naik 19 sen kepada RM3.03, UWC meningkat 16 sen kepada RM7.73, Critical Holdings menokok 15 sen kepada RM2.61, Mi Technovation melonjak sembilan sen kepada RM5.30, dan Solarvest mengukuh lapan sen kepada RM4.25. Nestle mendahului saham paling rugi, susut 32 sen to RM89.20, manakala Vitrox merosot 14 sen kepada RM10.32, Kobay Technology berkurangan 12 sen kepada RM2.18, Kelington menguncup lima sen kepada RM8.58, dan YTL Power International turun empat sen kepada RM5.64. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 menambah 28.14 mata kepada 17,510.07, Indeks FBM Emas meningkat 33.81 mata kepada 12,204.38, Indeks FBM Top 100 naik 32.24 mata kepada 11,989.92, Indeks FBM Emas Syariah bertambah 22.28 mata kepada 12,082.60, manakala Indeks FBM ACE meningkat 31.41 mata kepada 5,560.87. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian naik 0.59 mata kepada 179.11, Indeks Tenaga naik 2.57 mata kepada 835.60, Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan meningkat 97.59 mata kepada 19,138.10, manakala Indeks Perladangan melonjak 2.23 mata kepada 9,058.78. – Bernama

title: 'CIMB Says Lindung 24 Can Narrow Malaysia’s Protection Gap
body: 'Evidently, the SOCSO’s Lindung 24 social insurance scheme is expected to significantly broaden accident protection for workers without materially disrupting the private insurance and takaful industry.  In a sector report, CIMB Securities said Lindung 24, which was implemented by the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) on June 1, extends protection beyond work-related accidents to provide eligible workers with 24-hour coverage for non-employment accidents, alongside income replacement, rehabilitation and dependants’ benefits.  The research house maintained its Neutral stance on Malaysia’s insurance sector, saying the scheme is primarily aimed at underinsured workers and complements rather than replaces private medical, life and disability coverage.  CIMB said the protection gap remains substantial. Citing Perkeso, it noted that only about 48% of Malaysians have insurance protection beyond motor insurance, while coverage among the bottom 40% income group is estimated at just 4%.  About 38,000 claims were rejected between 2015 and 2025 because employees did not meet traditional eligibility requirements for employment-related accidents. With Lindung 24, Perkeso estimates that roughly 250,000 employees a year could benefit from protection for accidents previously outside the conventional workplace definition.  Take-up has also remained high. As at Sept 9, 8.5 million workers, or 87.6% of the estimated workforce, remained enrolled after the opt-out period for local workers ended on Aug 31. Around 1.2 million workers opted out, with 52% of them earning below RM3,500 per month.  Lindung 24 covers non-work accidents occurring at home, during personal travel, recreational activities, religious activities and other off-duty situations, complementing Perkeso’s existing Employment Injury Scheme, which applies to work-related accidents.  The contribution rate is currently 0.75% of monthly salary until May 2028. It will increase to 1.0% from June 2028 and 1.25% from June 2031, with both contributions and benefits capped at a monthly wage of RM6,000.  Benefits include temporary and permanent disablement payments, medical treatment, rehabilitation, dependants’ benefits, funeral assistance and education support. CIMB noted that fully disabled contributors could receive up to 90% of covered income for life, subject to Perkeso’s assessment and applicable rules.  For insurers, CIMB sees the greatest potential overlap in standalone and employer-sponsored personal accident policies. Employers could eventually rationalise duplicated accident benefits and redirect spending towards medical coverage and other employee benefits.  However, private insurance remains relevant for higher-income workers because Lindung 24 benefits are capped at the RM6,000 salary ceiling, while private products provide broader medical, life, critical illness and income protection.  CIMB said the longer-term effect could be positive by raising awareness of underinsurance and encouraging insurers to focus on higher-value protection and health products. It maintained its Neutral sector view, while remaining more constructive on LPI Capital than Syarikat Takaful Malaysia Keluarga.

title: 'Sebungkus nasi bahagi dua, duit poket hanya RM300
body: 'TUMPAT: “Setiap hari saya beli sebungkus nasi pada waktu tengah hari. Separuh saya simpan untuk makan malam sepanjang tiga minggu di Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM).” Demikian cerita Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah Sudin, 20, apabila ibu bapanya hanya mampu memberikan wang saku RM300 ketika menghantarnya ke USM di Pulau Pinang. Katanya, itu sahaja simpanan yang ada kerana telah membayar yuran pendaftaran sebanyak RM850 bagi mengikuti pengajian Sarjana Muda Pendidikan Khas. Katanya, yuran pengajian sebanyak RM1,232 belum dijelaskan meskipun sudah tiga minggu belajar di USM. “Jika ibu dapat pinjam dengan saudara-mara, dia akan kirim wang dalam masa terdekat untuk jelaskan yuran pengajian tersebut,” katanya menerusi panggilan video semasa kunjungan Ahli Majlis Presiden Gabungan Pelajar Melayu Semenanjung (GPMS), Che Muhammad Redzuan Jihad di rumahnya di Kampung Bunohan di sini. Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah berkata, dia rela mengikat perut kerana tidak mahu menyusahkan ibunya, Ramlah Abdul Rahman, 52, yang tidak dapat berjalan sejak empat tahun lalu selepas menjalani pembedahan kaki kiri akibat penyakit kencing manis. Katanya, demi membiayai pengajiannya, ibunya yang berkerusi roda gigih membuat kuih bersama bapanya, Sudin Matsan, 63. Bagi Ramlah, doanya sentiasa mengiringi Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah yang bercita-cita mahu menjadi seorang pendidik meskipun berdepan masalah kewangan. “Wang simpanan sudah habis digunakan untuk rawatan perubatan saya. “Walaupun menghadapi kekangan kewangan, saya tahu anak saya kuat semangat untuk menempuhnya,” katanya. Sementara itu, Che Muhammad Redzuan berkata, GPMS akan menyalurkan maklumat kepada Bahagian Hal Ehwal Pelajar (HEP) USM untuk membantu Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah termasuk wang saku, baki yuran dan sumbangan komputer riba. Sumbangan boleh disalurkan ke akaun CIMB 7657421192, Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah. – UTUSAN

title: 'HLB Islamic Berjaya Lonjak Pendapatan Usahawan Berpendapatan Rendah Langkawi Sebanyak 94%
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, 23 SEPTEMBER 2026 – Selaras dengan komitmen untuk memperkasakan ekosistem perantaraan berasaskan nilai (“Value-based Intermediation” atau “VBI”), HLB Islamic (atau “Bank”) telah menyalurkan pembiayaan sebanyak RM138,600 kepada perusahaan sosial SURI Inspirasi ("SURI") di bawah kerangka iTEKAD Bank Negara Malaysia (“BNM”). Inisiatif ini secara langsung menyumbang kepada peningkatan purata pendapatan bulanan sebanyak 94% serta menjana jumlah pendapatan baharu melebihi RM14,000 bagi usahawan yang menyertai program “Sustainable Reliable Income” (“SRI”) anjuran SURI.  HLB Islamic Tingkatkan Pendapatan Usahawan Sebanyak 94% Melalui Program SRI  Program SRI memperkasakan komuniti berpendapatan rendah untuk mengitar semula sisa fabrik menjadi barangan fesyen yang unik, yang secara langsung mewujudkan peluang pekerjaan dan memupuk semangat keusahawanan di samping mempromosikan fesyen sifar sisa serta pemerkasaan komuniti. Usahawan yang terlibat, yang majoriti ibu tunggal berpendapatan rendah, telah menghasilkan 1,000 pasang pakaian seragam sekolah untuk pelajar bagi lima buah sekolah di Langkawi, sekali gus menjana penjimatan sebanyak RM30,000 bagi keluarga tempatan. title: 'MKH bakal dinyahsenarai selepas Batu Kawan kuasai 95.16% saham
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 1 Okt – MKH Bhd bakal dinyahsenarai daripada Bursa Malaysia selepas Batu Kawan Bhd bersama anak syarikatnya, Whitmore Holdings Sdn Bhd serta pihak yang bertindak bersama mereka menguasai 95.16% saham syarikat pemaju hartanah itu. Jumlah pegangan tersebut bersamaan 548.85 juta saham MKH setakat penutupan dagangan pada 30 Sept 2026, menurut kenyataan yang dikeluarkan oleh Maybank Investment Bank Bhd bagi pihak Batu Kawan dan Whitmore. Dengan pegangan yang sudah melepasi 90%, Batu Kawan dan Whitmore kini boleh mengambil alih baki saham MKH yang masih dipegang pemegang saham yang tidak menerima tawaran pengambilalihan tersebut. Baki saham MKH akan diambil alih secara wajib Langkah itu akan dibuat di bawah Seksyen 222(1) Akta Pasaran Modal dan Perkhidmatan 2007 yang membolehkan baki saham diperoleh secara wajib. Tawaran pengambilalihan pada harga RM2 sesaham itu masih dibuka sehingga 8 Oktober 2026 selepas tarikh tutup asal pada 17 September lalu dilanjutkan. Selepas tempoh tawaran tamat, Bursa Malaysia Securities akan menggantung dagangan saham MKH selepas lima hari pasaran, sebelum Batu Kawan dan Whitmore meneruskan proses untuk menarik balik status penyenaraian MKH. Pengambilalihan MKH bernilai RM1.15 bilion Langkah Batu Kawan mengambil alih MKH bermula pada Mei lalu apabila Whitmore bersetuju membeli kepentingan 47.7% dalam MKH daripada anggota keluarga Chen pada harga RM2 sesaham, membabitkan nilai RM549.8 juta. Pembelian itu kemudiannya disusuli tawaran kepada pemegang saham MKH yang lain pada harga sama bagi membolehkan Batu Kawan meningkatkan pegangannya dalam syarikat tersebut. Secara keseluruhan, pengambilalihan MKH untuk menjadikannya syarikat persendirian bernilai sehingga RM1.15 bilion, termasuk kos pembelian kepentingan awal daripada keluarga Chen. Tawaran RM2 sesaham terima pandangan berbeza Bagaimanapun, tawaran tersebut sebelum ini mendapat pandangan berbeza daripada penasihat bebas MKH dan MKH Oil Palm (East Kalimantan) Bhd, iaitu cabang perladangan MKH yang disenaraikan secara berasingan. Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd, yang bertindak sebagai penasihat bebas MKH, menilai tawaran RM2 sesaham itu sebagai “tidak adil tetapi munasabah”, dengan mengambil kira harga tawaran yang lebih rendah daripada nilai aset wajar MKH. Bagi MKH Oil Palm pula, Mainstreet Advisers Sdn Bhd menggesa pemegang saham menolak tawaran 66.26 sen sesaham daripada Batu Kawan, yang disifatkannya sebagai “tidak adil dan tidak munasabah”. Menurut Mainstreet, harga tawaran itu mewakili diskaun 47% kepada nilai aset bersih (NAV) MKH Oil Palm. Pada masa sama, Batu Kawan bercadang mengekalkan MKH Oil Palm sebagai syarikat yang disenaraikan di Bursa Malaysia.- DagangNews.com

title: 'Asteel names ex-IGP Razarudin chairman, Clifford Hii executive deputy chairman in board revamp
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Asteel Group Bhd (KL:ASTEEL) has appointed former Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Razarudin Husain @ Abd Rasid as independent non-executive chairman and new controlling shareholder Datuk Clifford Hii Toh Leong as executive deputy chairman. The boardroom reshuffle follows Clifford securing a 53.08% stake in Asteel at the closing of a mandatory offer on Monday via investment vehicle Hii Capital Holdings Sdn Bhd. Clifford emerged as Asteel’s controlling shareholder in August with the acquisition of an initial 52.94% stake in the company via a RM20.75 million cash deal at 7.5 sen apiece. This triggered a mandatory offer for the remaining 47.06% stake in Asteel, also at 7.5 sen apiece. Clifford, 43, the son of the journalist-turned-businessman Tan Sri Clement Hii Chii Kok, who is the founder and executive chairman of property developer HCK Capital Group Bhd (KL:HCK) and group managing director and major shareholder of private education group SEG International. Clement is also the founder of Gambit Group Sdn Bhd, whose subsidiaries are involved in information technology services, investment, business management consultancy and is a registered digital asset custodian under the Securities Commission Malaysia. Clifford, a former non-independent, non-executive director at HCK Capital, has more than 20 years of experience in the education, property and financial technology sectors. He had held senior management and board positions covering corporate strategy, business development, corporate deals and investments, corporate governance and project management. Razarudin, 63, who is also independent non-executive chairman of Advancecon Holdings Bhd (KL:ADVCON), brings more than four decades of experience in national security and law enforcement. He was Malaysia’s 14th police chief until his retirement in June 2025. In separate filings, the steel manufacturer announced the appointment of Esther Teh Oun Pheng and Datuk Dr Lor Chee Leng as independent non-executive directors, while former executive chairman Tan Sri (Dr) Soh Thian Lai has been redesignated as executive director cum chairman emeritus. At the same time, non-independent non-executive director Christopher Hii Lu Ming, and independent non-executive directors Yan Ying Chieh, Khor Hun Nee and Wee Hiang Chyn have resigned, all citing personal reasons. Teh, 47, is head of internal audit and risk management at Usaha Tegas Sdn Bhd and an independent director of Nasdaq-listed OMS Energy Technologies Inc. She has more than 20 years of experience in internal and external audit, risk management, management consulting, shared-services implementation and operations and controllership. Her previous roles include group head of internal audit and compliance at Singapore-listed fintech company Silverlake Axis Ltd, head of risk management and assurance for group digital at Petroliam Nasional Bhd, and senior manager of management consulting at Accenture. Lor, 62, meanwhile, currently serves as an adviser to the Global ESG Leadership Organization and to Cambodia’s Ministry of Economy and Finance. He brings more than 35 years of experience in financial services, including banking transformation and strategy, corporate governance, risk management, credit oversight and consumer banking. His previous positions include independent director of Mizuho Bank (Malaysia) Bhd, chief executive officer and executive director of Canadia Bank PLC in Cambodia, group CEO of EON Bank Bhd, director of banking solutions at Hewlett Packard Enterprise, group head of consumer banking at RHB Bank Bhd and managing director of consumer banking at DBS Bank Ltd. At Tuesday's market close, Asteel shares rose a sen or 10.5% to 10.5 sen, valuing the group at RM50.9 million.

title: 'Felda’s road ahead in the spotlight
body: 'Felda’s road ahead in the spotlight KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Seven years after Malaysians were made aware of the problems confronting the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda), the institution is once again at a crossroads. Felda, which has the largest plantation footprint in the country and has helped improve the livelihoods of more than 100,000 original settlers and their families, is undergoing another strategic review amid concerns over its long-term sustainability. An interim report on the Felda Group Strategic Roadmap 2025-2030 (HTF 30) was submitted last month by the Special Committee on the Strategic Plan for Felda Group to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Among the proposals under consideration is a redefinition of Felda’s mandate, including a review of the Land Development Act that governs the agency, as the committee monitors actions taken following the 2019 Felda White Paper, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The review comes as the highly indebted entity grapples with crucial replanting costs that could reach RM900 million annually, on top of more than RM900 million in financing costs currently borne by the government. Felda oversees some 870,000 hectares (ha) of land, of which 490,000ha was allocated to settlers, 330,000ha to Felda’s commercial plantations — later placed under FGV Holdings Bhd — and another 50,000ha for village development. Fragmented and ineffective management of the land and operations, together with questionable transactions and investments, resulted in heavy losses despite Felda receiving billions of ringgit from the listing of its commercial arm, then known as Felda Global Ventures Holdings Bhd. By 2017, Felda’s borrowings had ballooned to RM12.1 billion from just RM100 million in 2007. In 2023, the government guaranteed and agreed to service Felda’s RM9.9 billion sukuk, issued to fund the RM3.7 billion privatisation of FGV to consolidate its estate operations, as well as Felda and settlers’ debt. But more needs to be done before those efforts bear fruit. Huge capital needed to become sustainable In 2012, Felda raised RM6 billion through the offer for sale of FGV shares during the latter’s initial public offering, while FGV itself raised RM4.5 billion from investors. In total, the exercise raised RM10.5 billion. Instead of directing more of those proceeds towards critical needs such as replanting, the 2019 Felda White Paper found that RM4.6 billion, or 76% of Felda’s IPO proceeds, went towards what it described as “unproductive spending”, while another RM1.4 billion was channelled into investments that failed to generate returns. The spending included RM1.69 billion in special payments to settlers, RM550 million in one-off contributions to state governments, RM400 million in loans for settlers’ house extensions, RM406 million to redeem FGV shares and RM177 million in listing expenses. FGV, meanwhile, spent RM3.3 billion, or 73% of its RM4.5 billion in IPO proceeds, on investments and developments that did not generate satisfactory returns. FGV, which leased Felda’s plantation land, also failed to achieve the yields Felda had projected, leaving the agency with an earnings shortfall. Following FGV’s privatisation, Felda is looking at consolidating the management of its commercial estates and settlers’ land. But that alone will not resolve the underlying balance-sheet problem, particularly the heavy capital requirements needed to keep the estates productive. The role of Felda Beyond its plantation operations, Felda bears significant social obligations to settlers, including spending on housing, infrastructure and income support for up to five years during the replanting cycle. Today, the families of Felda settlers span as many as six generations and number about 2.8 million people. In many respects, Felda has fulfilled its original mandate of opening up rural land and developing communities alongside settlers, about 95% of whom have received titles to their land. Without a clear framework for its future model, the institution’s role and the financial obligations that come with it risk continuing to be shaped by factors beyond its core mandate, particularly when political considerations intersect with policy during periods of adjustment. Any new roadmap will therefore have to define more clearly where Felda’s commercial responsibilities end and its social obligations begin, and how each should be funded. Felda’s troubled investments Felda was in better shape before the mismanagement that followed the windfall from FGV’s listing, when the institution was earning around RM3 billion a year. There are also arguments that greater provisions should have been made for replanting, which is central to sustaining its core operations. Poor investment decisions, however, turned Felda’s fortunes upside down in less than a decade. A forensic audit found RM2.2 billion in asset impairments from eight transactions undertaken by Felda and Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC) between 2010 and 2018 — equivalent to half of their initial RM4.4 billion investment value. Among them were PT Eagle High Plantations Tbk, the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project, and several London properties. One of the largest was Felda’s US$505.4 million acquisition of a 37% non-controlling stake in Eagle High Plantations in 2016 at a premium, resulting in an impairment loss of RM1.576 billion in 2017. Its London property purchases also came under scrutiny over discrepancies between reported acquisition prices and amounts received by vendors, while some properties saw their values fall sharply soon after acquisition. KLVC, meanwhile, remains the subject of a legal dispute between Felda and developer Synergy Promenade Sdn Bhd (SPSB) over the development of Felda land along Jalan Semarak. Former FIC chief executive officer Mohd Zaid Abdul Jalil has also been charged with two counts of cheating the company’s board, which allegedly resulted in the ownership of 16 land parcels being transferred from Felda to SPSB. Huge capital needed to become sustainable In 2012, Felda raised RM6 billion through the offer for sale of FGV shares during the latter’s initial public offering, while FGV itself raised RM4.5 billion from investors. In total, the exercise raised RM10.5 billion. Instead of directing more of those proceeds towards critical needs such as replanting, the 2019 Felda White Paper found that RM4.6 billion, or 76% of Felda’s IPO proceeds, went towards what it described as “unproductive spending”, while another RM1.4 billion was channelled into investments that failed to generate returns. The spending included RM1.69 billion in special payments to settlers, RM550 million in one-off contributions to state governments, RM400 million in loans for settlers’ house extensions, RM406 million to redeem FGV shares and RM177 million in listing expenses. FGV, meanwhile, spent RM3.3 billion, or 73% of its RM4.5 billion in IPO proceeds, on investments and developments that did not generate satisfactory returns. FGV, which leased Felda’s plantation land, also failed to achieve the yields Felda had projected, leaving the agency with an earnings shortfall. Following FGV’s privatisation, Felda is looking at consolidating the management of its commercial estates and settlers’ land. But that alone will not resolve the underlying balance-sheet problem, particularly the heavy capital requirements needed to keep the estates productive. The role of Felda Beyond its plantation operations, Felda bears significant social obligations to settlers, including spending on housing, infrastructure and income support for up to five years during the replanting cycle. Today, the families of Felda settlers span as many as six generations and number about 2.8 million people. In many respects, Felda has fulfilled its original mandate of opening up rural land and developing communities alongside settlers, about 95% of whom have received titles to their land. Without a clear framework for its future model, the institution’s role and the financial obligations that come with it risk continuing to be shaped by factors beyond its core mandate, particularly when political considerations intersect with policy during periods of adjustment. Any new roadmap will therefore have to define more clearly where Felda’s commercial responsibilities end and its social obligations begin, and how each should be funded. Felda’s troubled investments Felda was in better shape before the mismanagement that followed the windfall from FGV’s listing, when the institution was earning around RM3 billion a year. There are also arguments that greater provisions should have been made for replanting, which is central to sustaining its core operations. Poor investment decisions, however, turned Felda’s fortunes upside down in less than a decade. A forensic audit found RM2.2 billion in asset impairments from eight transactions undertaken by Felda and Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC) between 2010 and 2018 — equivalent to half of their initial RM4.4 billion investment value. Among them were PT Eagle High Plantations Tbk, the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project, and several London properties. One of the largest was Felda’s US$505.4 million acquisition of a 37% non-controlling stake in Eagle High Plantations in 2016 at a premium, resulting in an impairment loss of RM1.576 billion in 2017. Its London property purchases also came under scrutiny over discrepancies between reported acquisition prices and amounts received by vendors, while some properties saw their values fall sharply soon after acquisition. KLVC, meanwhile, remains the subject of a legal dispute between Felda and developer Synergy Promenade Sdn Bhd (SPSB) over the development of Felda land along Jalan Semarak. Former FIC chief executive officer Mohd Zaid Abdul Jalil has also been charged with two counts of cheating the company’s board, which allegedly resulted in the ownership of 16 land parcels being transferred from Felda to SPSB. title: 'TIPAK Marks Path to Leadership in Packaging Solutions Following Listing on SET
body:
'

BANGKOK, Oct 5, 2026 – ACN Newswire via SeaPRwire.com – Thai Packaging Industry PCL (TIPAK), one of Thailand’s leading developers, manufacturers, and distributors of packaging solutions, made its trading debut on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET), establishing itself as a leader in providing complete packaging services across Thailand. As a stock in the Industrial Goods/Packaging sector, TIPAK has demonstrated strong potential for sustainable growth. The company announced a planned investment of approximately THB 100 million in modern technology to upgrade its production processes, aiming to optimize cost management and create innovative, high-value products with distinctive and differentiated solutions. TIPAK highlights its strength in developing specialty packaging and sustainable packaging to align with the global growth of the sustainable economy, and is actively expanding its customer base among industries and factories nationwide.

Mr Veerachai Monsintorn, TIPAK’s Chief Executive Officer, stated that the Company successfully listed its shares today on the SET’s Industrial Goods/Packaging sector, symbol “TIPAK”. He expressed confidence that with the Company’s strong foundational capabilities, including the upgrade of modern technology to improve production efficiency, the development of distinctive and differentiated high-value products, and the delivery of comprehensive end-to-end solutions that meet specific customer needs, TIPAK was well-positioned to respond rapidly to evolving market demands and support the sustainable growth of all industrial sectors. Guided by the vision “Solutions Unfold – Meeting Customer Needs Perfectly”, TIPAK is committed to becoming Thailand’s leading provider of complete packaging solutions.

The Company expects to allocate approximately THB 100 million in 2027 across its Samut Sakhon and Prachin Buri factories through three key projects:

1. Project to Upgrade Production Efficiency and Automation Systems — Transitioning the production lines for corrugated paperboard and corrugated boxes to fully automated systems to reduce waste and increase speed (reduce Speed Losses).
2. Project for Smart Manufacturing Innovation and Digital Infrastructure — Investing in data-driven factory management systems to enable real-time monitoring and analysis of production performance.
3. Project for Quality Control and Production Stability Enhancement — Improving the consistency and reliability of the Quality Rate by upgrading quality assurance systems.

As of June 30, 2026, the Company’s total production capacity exceeds 140,000 tons of corrugated paperboard and more than 170 million corrugated boxes per year.

The Company has formulated a strategy to leverage its experience and expertise in the paper packaging business to develop high-value products and improve production efficiency, aiming for zero defects with new manufacturing technologies. Under a well-balanced pricing strategy, TIPAK designs and produces corrugated paperboard and boxes that are distinctive, differentiated, and precisely tailored to customer requirements, with customized features including packaging solutions for long-distance delivery and e-commerce logistics. The Company also develops sustainable paper packaging made from recycled materials to support the global shift toward environmentally responsible trade under ESG frameworks. Additionally, TIPAK provides consulting services for packaging design and improvement, and continues to expand its customer base among high-potential industries and factories nationwide.

Ms Nalyne Viriyasathien, Managing Director of Investment Banking, Maybank Securities (Thailand) PCL, in her role as financial advisor and joint lead underwriter, said that TIPAK has a clear and comprehensive business plan focused on sustainable growth across all dimensions – from its large-scale manufacturing facilities and internationally recognized production standards, to its relentless pursuit of innovation in high-value products and continuous expansion into diverse industrial sectors. This reflects a diversified revenue base, and she is confident that TIPAK will become a value-driven stock with strong potential for sustainable growth.

Ms. Nuntarut Sangsuwannukul, Executive Vice President, Investment Banking, Land and Houses Securities PCL, in her role as joint lead underwriter, said that TIPAK plays a critical role in driving Thailand’s industrial supply chain. Its commitment to upgrading factories with modern technology enhances efficiency, reduces costs, and strengthens competitiveness. Furthermore, TIPAK benefits from the projected 2.9% growth of the paper packaging industry in 2027, combined with the global momentum toward a sustainable economy. With these solid fundamentals, TIPAK is fully prepared to achieve its goal of becoming Thailand’s leading provider of complete packaging solutions with stable and confident growth.

title: 'Un Singapur envuelto en humo se prepara para hablar de dinero antes de la F1
body: 'SINGAPUR, 5 oct (Reuters) - Líderes regionales, empresariales, del mundo de las criptomonedas y del deporte se reúnen en Singapur para asistir a una serie de conferencias centradas en las finanzas antes del Gran Premio de este fin de semana, mientras la niebla sigue envolviendo la ciudad-estado.  Se espera la presencia del presidente filipino Ferdinand Marcos Jr., del famoso inversor  Ray Dalio y de Eric Trump, cofundador de la empresa de criptomonedas respaldada por su familia, mientras que cientos de miles de aficionados a la Fórmula Uno se darán cita en la isla.  La carrera nocturna por las calles de la ciudad y los cerca de 40 eventos paralelos suelen ser un escaparate mundial para Singapur, y las tarifas de las habitaciones de hotel se han disparado.  El Fullerton Bay Hotel, situado junto al circuito, cobra 5.030 dólares singapurenses (3.933 dólares) por noche por una habitación que suele costar 1.460 dólares.  Este año es probable que la nube de humo procedente de los incendios más intensos que ha sufrido Indonesia en más de una década formen parte del telón de fondo. La agencia medioambiental de Singapur pronosticó para el lunes que la calidad del aire se situaría en el rango de "moderada alta a insalubre baja". No se facilitó ningún pronóstico a más largo plazo para el Gran Premio del domingo.  La oficina de turismo de Singapur afirmó que la F1 y los eventos que la rodean tienen un "fuerte impulso" que refleja confianza pese a la incertidumbre económica y geopolítica.  El nerviosismo en los mercados financieros —donde el precio de los bonos está cayendo en picado y la percepción en torno a la inteligencia artificial está pasando de la euforia a la cautela— ocupará a los inversores y a los directivos en la Conferencia Global de Directores Ejecutivos de Forbes y en la Cumbre Milken Asia, que comienza el miércoles.  Trump, cofundador de la empresa de criptomonedas World Liberty Financial, tiene previsto intervenir en el evento sobre criptomonedas TOKEN2049, en un momento en que los mercados de activos digitales se muestran frágiles tras doce meses muy duros.  El mes pasado, el marco regulatorio que se esperaba no logró ser aprobado en el Senado estadounidense, en parte porque las operaciones personales del presidente Donald Trump con criptomonedas se convirtieron en un punto de fricción para los demócratas.  A pesar de un reciente repunte, el valor total del mercado de las criptomonedas ha caído cerca de una cuarta parte en los últimos 12 meses, a 3 billones de dólares, según el agregador de datos CoinGecko.  Aun así, los organizadores afirman que las entradas para su evento están prácticamente agotadas y se esperan 25 000 asistentes, la misma cifra que el año pasado. El Straits Times informó de que unos 90.000 ejecutivos de alto nivel, o "c-suite", estarán en la ciudad.  La F1 genera unos 145 millones de dólares singapurenses en ingresos turísticos adicionales para Singapur cada año, según estimaciones oficiales. Chua Hak Bin, economista de Maybank, prevé que esta cifra alcance los 160 millones de dólares singapurenses este año, además de "beneficios económicos más amplios" derivados de los acuerdos alcanzados en los eventos paralelos.  (1 dólar = 1,2794 dólares de Singapur)  (Reportaje de Xinghui Kok y Tom Westbrook; edición de Kim Coghill)

title: 'Bursa once said no to crypto. LIDAC26 showed how far Malaysia has come since
body: 'Back in 2024, I wrote a column lamenting Bursa Malaysia’s decision to keep bitcoin and other crypto assets off its new multi-asset exchange, asking whether it might go down as Bursa’s biggest blunder. Two Thursday’s ago, I spent the better part of a day at M Resort & Hotel in Kuala Lumpur listening to regulators, bankers and fund managers talk about digital assets not as a fringe curiosity, but as the plumbing for the next generation of our capital market. What a difference two years makes. The event was LIDAC26, the Luno Institutional Digital Asset Conference, now in its second edition. Luno, one of the digital asset exchanges registered with the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC), pitched it squarely at institutions rather than retail punters, and the room reflected that. The main hall kept the headline sessions flowing from 9.30am, four breakout sessions ran in smaller rooms alongside it through the day, and the session screens I saw all carried a QR code for live audience questions. Attendees could even earn seven continuing professional development (CPD) points, the credits licensed finance professionals collect to keep their qualifications current, which tells you exactly who the organisers were courting. So what were the big takeaways? Three stood out. 1. Stablecoins are the real story Luno chief executive James Lanigan opened proceedings with a slide that cut through a lot of the noise. By Luno’s count, about RM1.43 trillion worth of assets had been tokenised, or recorded as digital tokens on a blockchain, by the first quarter of 2026, and roughly RM1.26 trillion of that was stablecoins, tokens pegged to a currency such as the US dollar. That’s right. Around 90% of all tokenised assets are, in effect, digital cash, the overwhelming majority of which is tokenised USD, cementing it as not only the world’s reserve currency but the currency of choice in the budding crypto economy. Lanigan’s framing was that the industry had moved from speculation, through building infrastructure, and was now firmly in its institutional era, with one of his final slides declaring that Malaysia was not a late market, but an early one. 2. The regulator wants substance, not buzzwords The most anticipated session was that by Wong Huei Ching, the SC’s executive director of digital strategy and innovation, who laid out where Malaysia’s rules are heading. Her message, stripped to its core, was that putting an asset on a blockchain is not innovation in itself, and that pilots need to prove their worth before the rules are rewritten. The SC is practising what it preaches. In April, it teamed up with Khazanah Nasional, our sovereign wealth fund, to price Malaysia’s first tokenised sukuk (an Islamic bond recorded on a blockchain), a RM100 million pilot that SC chairman Mohammad Faiz Azmi said would test tokenisation’s potential “in a controlled and credible manner”. The market she regulates is growing fast, too. Trading value on Malaysia’s licensed digital asset exchanges hit RM17.14 billion in 2025, a 23% jump from RM13.93 billion the year before, according to the SC. 3. The ringgit is going on-chain John Ho, head of legal and financial markets at Standard Chartered, walked participants in the main hall through Bank Negara Malaysia’s growing list of experiments. These include Project Mawar, which explores a wholesale digital ringgit for banks, and the central bank’s Digital Asset Innovation Hub, where Standard Chartered and Capital A are testing a ringgit stablecoin, while Maybank trials tokenised deposits. The prize is not small. One industry estimate cited on stage, and widely reported, puts Malaysia’s tokenisation opportunity at around RM175 billion by 2030. The tidbits Many other speakers added flair and colour to the proceedings. Former deputy international trade and industry minister Ong Kian Ming spoke on navigating digital assets in a fragmenting global order, while Harjit Singh of HSS Advisory and Anil Puri of EY tackled a question plenty of Malaysian crypto investors have been asking for years: how exactly will all this be taxed? My favourite, though, was a breakout billed as Malaysian builders shaping the global digital asset landscape. On one stage sat TM Lee, co-founder of CoinGecko, Matthew Tan, founder of Etherscan, and Siong Ong, co-founder of Jupiter, products used by crypto traders the world over. CoinGecko and Etherscan were both born right here in Kuala Lumpur, and I can’t help but feel proud that some of the most widely used tools in the industry were built by Malaysians. Siong Ong’s speaker photo on the big screen? A Pudgy Penguin, an uber popular non-fungible token (NFT) collection. In a day full of suits, it was a welcome reminder of where this industry came from. The one glaring miss I was, however, surprised that bitcoin, the 800-pound gorilla in the room, barely got a look-in. Bitcoin alone is worth around RM6.9 trillion today, according to CoinGecko, and together with ether, the Ethereum network’s native token, the pair make up about two-thirds of the entire crypto market. Stablecoins, for all the stage time they got, account for a mere 10%. Despite more than a decade of relentless innovation in the industry, bitcoin still commands over half of all crypto value, and not telling that story was a missed opportunity. So where does that leave us? The SC revised its guidelines on Mar 2 to permit digital currency exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and Bursa, the very exchange that shut crypto out of its multi-asset platform in 2024, said in March that it welcomed the listing of digital currency ETFs, and told reporters in July that it planned to add them to its line-up. The regulator has built the framework, Khazanah has shown the plumbing can work and Bank Negara is already testing the ringgit on-chain. All that’s left is for the first digital currency ETF to actually start trading on Bursa. After all, it’s about time the exchange that once said no had something to show for its yes. Siong Ong’s speaker photo on the big screen? A Pudgy Penguin, an uber popular non-fungible token (NFT) collection. In a day full of suits, it was a welcome reminder of where this industry came from. The one glaring miss I was, however, surprised that bitcoin, the 800-pound gorilla in the room, barely got a look-in. Bitcoin alone is worth around RM6.9 trillion today, according to CoinGecko, and together with ether, the Ethereum network’s native token, the pair make up about two-thirds of the entire crypto market. Stablecoins, for all the stage time they got, account for a mere 10%. Despite more than a decade of relentless innovation in the industry, bitcoin still commands over half of all crypto value, and not telling that story was a missed opportunity. So where does that leave us? The SC revised its guidelines on Mar 2 to permit digital currency exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and Bursa, the very exchange that shut crypto out of its multi-asset platform in 2024, said in March that it welcomed the listing of digital currency ETFs, and told reporters in July that it planned to add them to its line-up. The regulator has built the framework, Khazanah has shown the plumbing can work and Bank Negara is already testing the ringgit on-chain. All that’s left is for the first digital currency ETF to actually start trading on Bursa. After all, it’s about time the exchange that once said no had something to show for its yes. title: 'Budget 2027 may bring SST exemptions, income tax relief for middle-income earners — CIMB Securities
body:
'

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 18): Budget 2027 could see further sales and service tax (SST) exemptions to reduce costs embedded in businesses, alongside possible personal income tax relief for middle-income taxpayers, according to CIMB Securities.

CIMB Securities said there is scope for the government to broaden SST exemptions for production-related inputs, as businesses continue to face elevated energy, logistics and other operating costs.

It expects further SST relief to reduce government collections by about RM1 billion, although underlying growth should still lift SST revenue by 5.5% to RM72 billion in 2027.

Unlike the goods and services tax (GST), the SST does not have a general input tax credit mechanism, meaning businesses may pay tax on inputs without being able to deduct it against tax charged on their own sales. This can result in tax costs being embedded through the supply chain, CIMB noted.

CIMB said in a note extending selected exemptions is likely to be the more immediate option in Budget 2027, while a broader input tax credit mechanism could be introduced from 2028 or later because of the additional administrative and refund framework required.

At the same time, CIMB sees room for targeted personal income tax relief for middle-income taxpayers, particularly households facing higher living costs but receiving less direct cash assistance.

As an illustration, the research house said tax rates for chargeable income of RM50,001 to RM70,000 and RM70,001 to RM100,000 could each be reduced by one percentage point to 10% and 18% respectively.

The current 25% tax bracket could also be split, with a 24% rate applied to chargeable income between RM100,001 and RM150,000.

Such a package could provide annual tax savings of RM200 for those with RM70,000 in chargeable income, RM500 at RM100,000 and as much as RM1,000 for those earning RM150,000 and above, CIMB estimated.

It said the illustrative package would cost the government about RM800 million annually.

More broadly, CIMB expects Budget 2027 to continue providing household support while maintaining fiscal consolidation, forecasting the fiscal deficit to narrow slightly to 3.4% of gross domestic product in 2027 from an estimated 3.5% in 2026.

The research house also expects cash assistance under Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah to increase by RM2 billion to RM17 billion, supported partly by lower fuel subsidy spending.

CIMB forecasts petrol and diesel subsidies to fall to RM32 billion in 2027 from RM41 billion, creating room for higher household assistance and development spending while keeping the government on its fiscal consolidation path.

Budget 2027, the fifth Madani Budget and the second under the 13th Malaysia Plan, is scheduled to be tabled in Parliament on Oct 9. The Ministry of Finance has said the budget will focus on areas including cost-of-living pressures, business competitiveness and productivity, while maintaining fiscal discipline.

title: 'ALTO perkuat QRIS, gandeng BNI, BNC, Maybank dan blu BCA Digital
body: 'KONTAN.CO.ID - JAKARTA. PT ALTO Network memperluas konektivitas layanan pembayaran digital bersama sejumlah bank. Langkah tersebut dilakukan melalui ajang FEKDI x IFSE 2026.  CEO PT ALTO Network Gretel Griselda mengatakan, ALTO menandatangani kerja sama dengan tujuh mitra, termasuk Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI), blu by BCA Digital, Bank Neo Commerce (BNC) dan Maybank Indonesia.  "Saya rasa hampir semua masyarakat Indonesia yang melakukan transaksi finansial, pernah melakukan transaksi menggunakan QRIS. Dan tentunya ALTO sebagai salah satu Penyedia Infrastruktur Pembayaran (PIP) mendukung penuh inisiatif-inisiatif yang Bank Indonesia (BI) miliki," ujar Gretel di Jakarta International Convention Center (JICC), Jumat (25/9/2026).  Dengan BNI, ALTO memperkuat layanan QRIS Cross Border. Sementara dengan blu by BCA Digital, BNC dan Maybank, kolaborasi diarahkan pada konektivitas QRIS.  Rangkaian penandatanganan tersebut menjadi momentum bagi ALTO untuk memperkuat hubungan dengan mitra yang sudah ada sekaligus mengembangkan layanan pembayaran digital. Kolaborasi yang dilakukan mencakup QRIS dan disbursement, dengan fokus pada perluasan konektivitas dan penguatan infrastruktur pembayaran.  Di sisi transaksi, total transaksi melalui jaringan ALTO tumbuh 96% secara tahunan pada semester I 2026. Transaksi QRIS tumbuh 118% YoY, sedangkan volume transaksi QRIS meningkat 112% yoy.
