title: 'Brokers Digest: Local Equities - Banking, Solarvest Holdings Bhd, Gamuda Bhd, QL Resources Bhd
body: 'Brokers Digest: Local Equities - Banking, Solarvest Holdings Bhd, Gamuda Bhd, QL Resources Bhd This article first appeared in Capital, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 28, 2026 - October 4, 2026 Banking POSITIVE BIMB SECURITIES RESEARCH (Sept 22): Global bond markets experienced higher yields amid tighter US monetary policy and higher-for-longer interest rates. On Sept 16, the Federal Open Market Committee raised the federal funds rate target by 25 basis points (bps) to 3.75%-4.00%. The 10-year Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yield stands at 4.15% as at Sept 21, and remains elevated by historical standards but is still below the peak of 4.57% recorded in October 2022. According to our economist’s assessment, the 10-year MGS yield is expected to hover around the 4.0% level in the near term before gradually moderating towards the 3.75%-3.90% range by year end. Current yield levels appear to reflect market expectations of close to two policy rate hikes in Malaysia. However, given our view that the Overnight Policy Rate will remain unchanged at 2.75% throughout 2026 and 2027, coupled with a contained domestic inflation outlook, the 10-year MGS yield is expected to ease from its current elevated level over time. Banks typically maintain an average securities portfolio duration of around five to six years, which is considered moderate rather than long term. As a result, their investment portfolios are generally less sensitive to interest rate movements and face lower interest rate risk compared with portfolios concentrated on longer-dated securities. The impact on fair value through other comprehensive income securities is expected to result in lower FVOCI reserves due to revaluation losses in 3Q26, as the 10-year MGS yield is likely to remain elevated in the near term. Nevertheless, the effect on ROE could be favourable, as the decline in shareholders’ funds reduces the equity base used in the ROE calculation. Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) (fair value: RM11.40), CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) (FV: RM8.75) and RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK) (FV:RM8.50), which have exposure to the Singapore market, are likely to see improved net interest margins as the rise in three-month Singapore overnight rate change (SORA), in tandem with Fed rate hikes, lifts asset yields and helps mitigate fair value through profit and loss (FVTPL) mark-to-market losses in 3Q26. Banks’ funding profiles remain largely anchored by longer-tenor liabilities, including Medium Term Notes with maturities of at least two to three years, which help maintain robust Net Stable Funding Ratio positions and reduce near-term refinancing pressures. As such, banks are unlikely to rush into refinancing and are more likely to adopt a wait-and-see approach when considering the rollover of maturing papers. We do not expect deposit competition to become more aggressive from here, given that 1Q26 and 2Q26 had already witnessed intense competition, with banks offering promotional fixed deposit rates of up to 3.7%-3.8% for 10- to 12-month placements. Solarvest Holdings Bhd Target price: RM4.50 BUY AMINVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (Sept 21): We believe that Solarvest Holdings Bhd (KL:SLVEST) would benefit from the government’s CRESS Acceleration Package. Under the package, a System Access Charge (SAC) of 14 sen/kWh will be introduced. We think that the lower SAC would spur the rollout of CRESS projects, as under the previous CRESS scheme, the SAC were perceived as too high. The SAC under the previous CRESS were 20 sen/kWh for projects with battery systems and 40 sen/kWh for projects without battery systems. We reckon that battery and solar systems contracts are worth about RM3.5million/mw to RM4million/mw based on recently announced projects. There is incentive for data centres to do solar under the new CRESS. This is because the tariffs under the new CRESS package would come up to about 45 to 50 sen/kWh compared with their present electricity tariffs of 50 to 60 sen/kWh. Solarvest is bidding for 11,800mw worth of projects. Out of these, about 1,200mw are expected to come from battery projects. We have raised Solarvest’s FY2028F net profit by 13.5% and FY29F net earnings by 40.4% to account for a higher EPCC (engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning) order book due to the new CRESS projects. Gamuda Bhd Target price: RM5.42 BUY TA SECURITIES (Sept 22): Gamuda Bhd (KL:GAMUDA), via the Gamuda-BMD joint venture, has clinched the A$624 million (RM1.8 billion) Elizabeth Drive Upgrade — Mamre Road Upgrade Stage 2 Package from government agency Transport for New South Wales. Based on its 50% effective interest in the JV, Gamuda is entitled to roughly RM908 million in contract value. Given that the award also comes with cost-pass-through clauses, we believe this should limit Gamuda’s execution risk and exposure to volatile material prices. Based on the management-guided PBT margin of 5%, we estimate the project could generate approximately RM45.4 million in PBT over the contract period. Looking ahead, we expect Western Sydney’s rapid development to support sustained infrastructure spending, particularly across the road network. This should provide a healthy pipeline of replenishment opportunities for Gamuda. Gamuda’s FY2027 year-to-date new job wins have reached RM10.2 billion, lifting its unbilled construction order book to RM62.5 billion. We believe Gamuda’s near-term order book replenishment prospects remain healthy, with potential wins likely to come from data centre projects from new and repeat clients in Malaysia, renewable energy projects in Australia, particularly solar EPCCs (engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning) works, and railway infrastructure projects in Taiwan. QL Resources Bhd Target price: RM5.10 BUY HONG LEONG INVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (Sept 23): QL Resources Bhd’s (KL:QL)’s 1QFY2027 marine products manufacturing (MPM) revenue rose 18.2% year on year while PBT jumped 51.5%, with management attributing the bulk of the circa RM30 million y-o-y earnings uplift to fishmeal driven by Peru’s lower catch quota and a temporary El Niño fishing ban. Peru, which supplies roughly a fifth of the world’s fishmeal, in August called off its main anchovy season having landed only 25% of an already reduced quota. That keeps global supply tight, and fishmeal prices in July were still running about 11% above where they averaged through QL’s 1QFY27. Grade C egg prices recovered from the low RM0.20s in April to May to RM0.33 by end-June and >RM0.40 at the farm gate by August We remain constructive on QL, given that MPM is delivering into a supply shock with further runway into FY27, and did so in a seasonally soft quarter with the stronger quarters still ahead. Clean energy under BM Greentech Bhd (KL:BMGREEN] now has a working commercial proof point inside QL’s own plant while Innofood will begin contributing from 2HFY28. Integrated livestock farming and convenience store chain segments have, in our view, both passed their respective troughs, with egg prices recovering off the April low and FamilyMart's top line turning after three quarters of decline. title: 'Bursa Malaysia Index Falls Amid Heavyweight Declines
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia continued to experience a downturn at mid-morning, largely driven by selling pressures in leading sectors such as healthcare, industrial products, and utilities. According to BERNAMA News Agency, at 11 am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) dropped by 11.73 points to 1,639.44, compared to the previous day's close of 1,651.17, after opening slightly lower at 1,649.87. In the healthcare sector, IHH Healthcare saw a decrease of 13 sen to RM7.70. Within industrial products, Petronas Chemicals fell 11 sen to RM4.07, Press Metal Aluminium went down nine sen to RM7.36, and Sunway dipped two sen to RM4.40. Utilities counters also took a hit, with YTL Power dropping six sen to RM5.81, YTL Corporation declining by one sen to RM2.27, and Tenaga Nasional decreasing by two sen to RM12.94. The overall market saw 484 decliners surpassing 273 gainers, with 460 counters unchanged. Additionally, 1,556 counters remained untraded, and 12 were suspended. The market turnover was recorded at 1.18 billion shares valued at RM769.76 million. Hong Leong Investment Bank noted that the ongoing US-Iran tensions and the Federal Reserve's hawkish stance could prolong the benchmark index's risk-off consolidation, influenced by high oil prices, bond yields, and continued foreign outflows. Among major stocks, Maybank and CIMB each dropped by two sen to RM9.97 and RM7.77, respectively, while Public Bank declined three sen to RM4.67. In active trades, Zetrix AI increased by half a sen to 16.5 sen, V.S Industry rose one sen to 29 sen, Jaks Resources fell half a sen to 20 sen, ACE Market newcomer GB Bond decreased by 2.5 sen to 22.5 sen, and Dagang Nexchange rose two sen to 50.5 sen. Top gainers included Malaysian Pacific Industries, which increased by 62 sen to RM41.02, Malayan Cement rising by 12 sen to RM5.57, and both MI Technovation and Hengyuan Refining gaining 10 sen to RM5.30 and RM3.66, respectively. Vitrox saw an increase of eight sen to RM9.99. Conversely, Kuala Lumpur Kepong led the decliners, falling 74 sen to RM21.46, followed by Allianz Malaysia, which shed 68 sen to RM20.94. Nestle fell 40 sen to RM89.60, United Plantations dropped 30 sen to RM31.26, and Hong Leong Bank lost 28 sen to RM22.86. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index decreased by 71.17 points to 17,503.50, the FBM Emas Index fell 72.18 points to 12,219.83, and the FBM Top 100 Index declined by 76.32 points to 12,008.12. The FBM Emas Shariah Index weakened by 71.61 points to 12,104.73, and the FBM ACE Index decreased by 22.64 points to 5,511.64. full_text: 'Bursa Malaysia Index Falls Amid Heavyweight Declines. 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia continued to experience a downturn at mid-morning, largely driven by selling pressures in leading sectors such as healthcare, industrial products, and utilities. Within industrial products, Petronas Chemicals fell 11 sen to RM4.07, Press Metal Aluminium went down nine sen to RM7.36, and Sunway dipped two sen to RM4.40. Utilities counters also took a hit, with YTL Power dropping six sen to RM5.81, YTL Corporation declining by one sen to RM2.27, and Tenaga Nasional decreasing by two sen to RM12.94. The market turnover was recorded at 1.18 billion shares valued at RM769.76 million. Hong Leong Investment Bank noted that the ongoing US-Iran tensions and the Federal Reserve's hawkish stance could prolong the benchmark index's risk-off consolidation, influenced by high oil prices, bond yields, and continued foreign outflows. Among major stocks, Maybank and CIMB each dropped by two sen to RM9.97 and RM7.77, respectively, while Public Bank declined three sen to RM4.67. In active trades, Zetrix AI increased by half a sen to 16.5 sen, V.S Industry rose one sen to 29 sen, Jaks Resources fell half a sen to 20 sen, ACE Market newcomer GB Bond decreased by 2.5 sen to 22.5 sen, and Dagang Nexchange rose two sen to 50.5 sen. Top gainers included Malaysian Pacific Industries, which increased by 62 sen to RM41.02, Malayan Cement rising by 12 sen to RM5.57, and both MI Technovation and Hengyuan Refining gaining 10 sen to RM5.30 and RM3.66, respectively. Vitrox saw an increase of eight sen to RM9.99. Conversely, Kuala Lumpur Kepong led the decliners, falling 74 sen to RM21.46, followed by Allianz Malaysia, which shed 68 sen to RM20.94. Nestle fell 40 sen to RM89.60, United Plantations dropped 30 sen to RM31.26, and Hong Leong Bank lost 28 sen to RM22.86. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index decreased by 71.17 points to 17,503.50, the FBM Emas Index fell 72.18 points to 12,219.83, and the FBM Top 100 Index declined by 76.32 points to 12,008.12. The FBM Emas Shariah Index weakened by 71.61 points to 12,104.73, and the FBM ACE Index decreased by 22.64 points to 5,511.64. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index dropped by 1.24 points to 179.17, the Energy Index eased by 5.43 points to 840.27, the Financial Services Index fell 87.09 points to 19,129.40, and the Plantation Index retreated by 104.26 points to 9,092.41.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia jatuh 20 mata diasak tekanan jualan berterusan
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ditutup rendah pada Khamis dalam keadaan tekanan jualan yang berterusan, sejajar dengan prestasi Wall Street semalaman yang bercampur-campur dan berhati-hati. Pada 5 petang, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) menurun 20.81 mata atau 1.26 peratus kepada 1,630.36 daripada 1,651.17 semasa ditutup pada Rabu. Indeks petunjuk pasaran yang dibuka rendah 1.30 mata kepada 1,649.87 bergerak antara 1,630.10 dan 1,649.87 sepanjang sesi dagangan. Pasaran secara menyeluruh negatif, dengan kaunter rugi mengatasi kaunter untung sebanyak 750 berbanding 342 manakala 495 kaunter tidak berubah, 1,186 tidak diniagakan dan 12 yang lain digantung. Jumlah dagangan merosot kepada 3.1 bilion unit bernilai RM2.7 bilion daripada 3.63 bilion unit bernilai RM3.62 bilion pada Rabu. Pengarah Strategi Pelaburan dan Ahli Ekonomi IPPFA Sdn Bhd, Mohd Sedek Jantan, berkata sentimen pasaran berhati-hati, didorong oleh aktiviti pembuatan domestik yang lembap dan jualan berterusan oleh pelabur asing. Beliau berkata, momentum sektor pembuatan yang lembap dan peralihan portfolio dalam pasaran global terus memberi tekanan kepada indeks petunjuk pasaran, dengan permintaan institusi domestik kekal sebagai pengimbang penting terhadap aliran keluar asing yang berterusan. Terdahulu, Indeks Pengurus Pembelian (PMI) Pembuatan Malaysia S&P Global yang diselaraskan mengikut musim menurun di bawah paras neutral 50.0 kepada 49.9 pada September daripada 50.2 pada Ogos, mencatatkan penurunan pertama dalam tempoh empat bulan selepas meningkat secara berterusan. Pada peringkat serantau, PMI Pembuatan ASEAN S&P Global menurun kepada 52.1 pada September daripada 52.3 pada Ogos. Dalam kalangan saham wajaran tinggi, Maybank menurun empat sen kepada RM9.95, Public Bank berkurangan tiga sen kepada RM4.67 dan CIMB merosot 10 sen kepada RM7.69. Tenaga Nasional menyusut enam sen kepada RM12.90 dan IHH Healthcare menurun 13 sen kepada RM7.70. Dalam dagangan aktif, Zetrix AI meningkat setengah sen kepada 16.5 sen, VS Industry merosot satu sen kepada 27 sen dan Jaks Resources berkurangan 2.5 sen kepada 18 sen. GB Bond yang mula disenaraikan di Pasaran ACE menurun 4.5 sen kepada 20.5 sen dan HHRG naik setengah sen kepada 16.5 sen. Kaunter paling untung ialah Malaysian Pacific Industries melonjak 72 sen kepada RM41.12, Ayer Holdings meningkat 20 sen kepada RM7.70, Riverview Rubber Estates naik 12 sen kepada RM3.02, Dutch Lady Malaysia Industries menambah 10 sen kepada RM30 dan Vitrox menokok sembilan sen kepada RM10. Kaunter paling rugi termasuklah Kuala Lumpur Kepong menurun 78 sen kepada RM21.42, Allianz Malaysia merosot 62 sen kepada RM21.00, United Plantations berkurangan 60 sen kepada RM30.96, Fraser & Neave dan Hong Leong Industries, masing-masing menyusut 32 sen kepada RM21.42 dan RM16.14. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid70 berkurangan 215.69 mata kepada 17,358.98, Indeks FBM Emas merosot 148.48 mata kepada 12,143.53 dan Indeks FBM Top 100 menurun 151.29 mata kepada 11,933.15. Indeks FBM Emas Shariah menyusut 163.34 mata kepada 12,013.01 dan Indeks FBM ACE merosot 51.31 mata kepada 5,482.97. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk Perindustrian dan Perkhidmatan menurun 2.68 mata kepada 177.73, Indeks Tenaga berkurangan 10.69 mata kepada 454.03, Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan merosot 155.58 mata kepada 19,060.91 dan Indeks Perladangan jatuh 170.10 mata kepada 9,026.57. Jumlah dagangan Pasaran Utama menurun kepada 1.82 bilion unit bernilai RM2.42 bilion daripada 2.23 bilion unit bernilai RM3.28 bilion pada Rabu. Jumlah dagangan waran berkurangan kepada 618.78 juta unit bernilai RM72.71 juta daripada 887.74 juta unit bernilai RM138.36 juta sebelum ini. Jumlah dagangan Pasaran ACE meningkat kepada 650.13 juta unit bernilai RM226.92 juta daripada 510.54 juta unit bernilai RM201.45 juta semalam. Kaunter barangan dan perkhidmatan pengguna menyumbang sebanyak 225.90 juta saham diniagakan di Pasaran Utama, produk perindustrian dan perkhidmatan (404.80 juta), pembinaan (256.48 juta), teknologi (426.14 juta), perkhidmatan kewangan (69.01 juta), hartanah (133.11 juta), perladangan (25.25 juta), amanah pelaburan hartanah (12.87 juta), dana tertutup (16,100), tenaga (81.78 juta), penjagaan kesihatan (56.01 juta), telekomunikasi dan media (49.21 juta), pengangkutan dan logistik (52.50 juta), utiliti (36.12 juta) dan amanah perniagaan (60,200). -BERNAMA

title: 'FBM KLCI Rebounds at Midday, Driven by Utilities Stocks
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) saw a rebound at midday, gaining 10.18 points to reach 1,654.14, up from Tuesday's close of 1,643.96, driven by bargain hunting in selected heavyweight stocks, particularly in the utilities sector, although overall market breadth remained negative. According to BERNAMA News Agency, the index opened 2.53 points higher at 1,646.49 and moved within a range of 1,645.03 to 1,656.87 during the session. Utilities stocks were at the forefront of the gains, with Tenaga Nasional increasing by 32 sen to RM13.04, Petronas Gas rising by 20 sen to RM17.38, and YTL Corporation edging up by one sen to RM2.30. Despite the gains in the index, the broader market witnessed decliners outnumbering gainers by 603 to 350, with 521 counters remaining unchanged, 1,381 untraded, and 95 suspended. The turnover amounted to 1.92 billion shares valued at RM1.49 billion. Apex Securities Bhd noted in a statement that the energy sector, one of the only two sectors to gain, might experience a reversal of some gains following a dip in Brent crude oil prices overnight amid ongoing US-Iran talks. At the time of reporting, Brent crude had risen by 0.48 percent to US$103.08 per barrel. In terms of heavyweight stocks, Maybank increased by five sen to RM10.04, while Public Bank decreased by two sen to RM4.70. CIMB added one sen to RM7.79, and IHH Healthcare rose by three sen to RM7.90. Among active traders, Zetrix AI remained flat at 16.5 sen, V.S Industry increased by 1.5 sen to 25 sen, and Gamuda recovered by 20 sen to RM5.18. Jaks Resources and Tanco each rose by half a sen to 19.5 sen and 16.5 sen, respectively. Top gainers included Nestle, which rose by RM1.20 to RM90.12, United Plantations, which gained 28 sen to RM31.60, and UMS Integration, which added 20 sen to RM8.81. Ayer edged up by 18 sen to RM7.78, and Allianz Malaysia advanced by 14 sen to RM21. Hengyuan Refining led the decliners, falling by 57 sen to RM3.77, and its trading was suspended for the remainder of the day after breaching the prescribed price limit. Malaysian Pacific Industries dropped by 44 sen to RM40.36, Eurospan by 25 sen to RM2.99, Kuala Lumpur Kepong by 22 sen to RM22.28, and MI Technovation by 17 sen to RM5.22. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index decreased by 48.14 points to 17,561.95. In contrast, the FBM Emas Index rose by 40.32 points to 12,305.79, and the FBM Top 100 Index gained 46.83 points to 12,098.37. The FBM Emas Shariah Index increased by 69.56 points to 12,197.17, while the FBM ACE Index fell by 33.86 points to 5,494.72. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index saw a slight rise of 0.32 points to 181.18. However, the Energy Index fell by 18.32 points to 850.38. Meanwhile, the Financial Services Index gained 10.75 points to 19,271.60, and the Plantation Index added 16.55 points, reaching 9,232.89.

title: 'PublicInvest Research Headlines - 24 Sep 2026
body: 'Global: Inflation will linger and Fed will hike rates again, OECD says. Inflation around the world will be faster than forecast in 2027, an outlook that necessitates more tightening from the US to Australia. The Paris-based club of rich countries raised projections compared with June for consumer-price growth in every Group-of-20 economy apart from China and Saudi Arabia. Monetary policy across the globe may have to respond. The analysis underscores how the economic impact of the Middle East war unleashed by US President Donald Trump is now set to endure into the second half of his term in office. The OECD's assessment follows a round of tightening this month, with the US Fed, the ECB and BOJ all raising interest rates within little more than a week of each other. The organisation's officials reckon more such action is in the offing, while suggesting it won't match the aggressive policy moves seen in the wake of the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine. (Bloomberg) US: Business activity at more than five-year high; inflation pressures building. US business activity raced to a more than five-year high in Sep, fueled by a surge in new orders, though strong demand strained supply chains and pushed prices higher. S&P Global's flash US Composite PMI Output Index, which tracks the manufacturing and services sectors, increased to 58.4 this month. That was the highest level since July 2021 and followed a reading of 56.0 in August. A reading above 50 indicates expansion in the private sector. The rise in the PMI reflected strong gains in both the services and manufacturing sectors. The PMI was consistent with the economy growing at around a 5% annualised rate. It also noted a sharp rise in work backlogs and supply chain delays, pointing to a lack of operating capacity which fed through to higher prices. (Reuters) EU: Eurozone business activity hits three-year high on services. Private-sector activity in the euro area grew at the fastest pace in more than three years as the service sector unexpectedly improved. The Composite PMI compiled by S&P Global increased to 53.1 from 52 in August, well above the 50 threshold separating growth from contraction. Analysts in a Bloomberg survey had anticipated a small decline to 51.7. The region's two largest economies both exceeded expectations, with activity in Germany growing at the fastest pace since Oct 2025 and France unexpectedly expanding at the quickest in more than two years. The euro-area economy is showing greater resilience than expected to the Middle East conflict and the resulting jump in energy costs. How long it can resist such headwinds remains uncertain, however, with inflation at its highest level in almost three years and borrowing costs rising. (Bloomberg) UK: Business activity cools as inflation pressure ramps up ahead of budget. Growth in British business activity cooled this month and inflation pressure built, an awkward backdrop for Finance Minister John Healey ahead of his first budget next month. The S&P Global UK services PMI fell in Sep to 51.7 from 52.5 in August, a three-month low. A Reuters poll of economists had pointed to a reading of 52.0. Prices charged by services companies, the backbone of Britain's economy, rose at the fastest pace in four months. title: 'CIMB raih tiga anugerah perbankan Euromoney 2026
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: CIMB Bank Berhad dan CIMB Investment Bank (CIMB) terus mengukuhkan kedudukan dalam industri kewangan apabila meraih tiga anugerah utama pada Euromoney Awards for Excellence 2026. CIMB dinobatkan sebagai Bank Runcit Terbaik Malaysia, Bank Digital Terbaik Malaysia untuk Perusahaan Kecil dan Sederhana (PKS) serta Bank Pelaburan Terbaik Malaysia. Pengiktirafan berkenaan mencerminkan prestasi, inovasi dan impak kepada pelanggan yang dicapai CIMB, selain usaha berterusannya dalam menyediakan penyelesaian kewangan berorientasikan pelanggan menerusi inovasi, keupayaan digital dan kepakaran pasaran yang kukuh. Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Kumpulan CIMB, Novan Amirudin berkata, kejayaan itu membuktikan kepercayaan pelanggan serta komitmen pasukan bank dalam memenuhi keperluan individu dan perniagaan. “Pengiktirafan ini adalah bukti kepercayaan pelanggan serta dedikasi pasukan kami di seluruh bank. “Ia mengukuhkan semula tujuan CIMB untuk memacu kemajuan pelanggan dan masyarakat dengan menjadikan penyelesaian kewangan lebih mudah diakses, relevan dan memberi impak kepada individu serta perniagaan yang kami berkhidmat,” katanya dalam kenyataan. Menurut beliau, CIMB akan terus menjadi rakan kongsi dipercayai dalam membantu individu merealisasikan aspirasi mereka, selain menyokong perniagaan mencapai matlamat pertumbuhan melalui penciptaan nilai yang bermakna dan berkekalan. Dalam perbankan runcit, CIMB terus memperkukuh segmen perniagaannya menerusi penawaran diperibadikan, pengalaman digital serta penglibatan lebih kukuh dengan kumpulan pelanggan utama. Prestasi pendapatan dan keuntungan turut meningkat sepanjang tahun, disokong pertambahan bahagian pasaran dalam pembiayaan kenderaan, kad kredit dan deposit runcit, selain peningkatan jualan digital serta penawaran silang kepada pelanggan. CIMB turut memperkukuh penawaran pengurusan kekayaan menerusi penyelesaian pelaburan yang berbeza, kepelbagaian produk lebih luas, khidmat nasihat diketuai Ketua Pegawai Pelaburan (CIO) serta platform pengurusan kekayaan digital yang dipertingkatkan. Momentum itu khususnya ketara dalam segmen Preferred, mencerminkan penglibatan lebih mendalam dengan pelanggan berkemampuan tinggi serta tumpuan bank terhadap khidmat nasihat dan hubungan pelanggan dalam pengurusan kekayaan. Bagi segmen PKS pula, CIMB terus memperluas perbankan digital menerusi pelancaran CIMB OCTO Biz, yang menghubungkan pembukaan akaun, pembiayaan dan perbankan transaksi dalam satu perjalanan digital hujung ke hujung. Platform itu telah menarik lebih 280,000 pelanggan setakat ini, dengan menawarkan kemudahan melihat aliran tunai secara masa nyata, pembayaran, pertukaran asing, perdagangan serta perkhidmatan pembiayaan. Bank turut memperluas akses pembiayaan menerusi kemudahan pembiayaan pedagang bersepadu dengan TNG eWallet, selain pembiayaan fleksibel melalui SME FlexiCash. Kemudahan berkenaan menggunakan rekod sejarah akaun dan corak transaksi untuk menentukan had pra-kelayakan serta menghubungkan pembayaran balik kepada sebahagian daripada hasil perniagaan, sekali gus membantu perniagaan yang mempunyai aliran tunai tidak sekata. Sementara itu, kepimpinan CIMB Investment Bank dalam pasaran modal ekuiti dan hutang Malaysia, penggabungan dan pengambilalihan (M&A), serta penyelesaian nasihat kewangan khusus turut mengukuhkan kedudukannya sebagai bank pelaburan utama. Pada 2025, CIMB Investment Bank menduduki tempat pertama dalam pasaran modal ekuiti dan hutang Malaysia berdasarkan nilai urus niaga serta bahagian dompet (share of wallet). Bank itu turut menduduki kedudukan teratas dalam pasaran modal ekuiti dan hutang ASEAN berdasarkan nilai urus niaga, dengan kejayaan melaksanakan transaksi rentas sempadan yang mengukuhkan kedudukannya sebagai peneraju M&A dan khidmat nasihat di rantau ASEAN. Tiga anugerah berkenaan turut mengukuhkan janji jenama CIMB, Moving You Forward, yang mencerminkan komitmen berterusan bank dalam memperkasa pelanggan dan komuniti menerusi penyelesaian kewangan yang mudah diakses, inklusif serta berteraskan tujuan. Euromoney Awards for Excellence, yang telah berlangsung lebih 30 tahun, mengiktiraf institusi kewangan yang menetapkan penanda aras global dari segi prestasi, inovasi dan impak kepada pelanggan. Program anugerah itu menilai institusi kewangan menerusi rangka kerja penanda aras Euromoney dengan menggunakan metrik yang boleh dibandingkan, penyerahan maklumat berstruktur serta proses penyelidikan telus bagi menilai prestasi institusi berbanding pesaing masing-masing.-UTUSAN

Sementara itu, kepimpinan CIMB Investment Bank dalam pasaran modal ekuiti dan hutang Malaysia, penggabungan dan pengambilalihan (M&A), serta penyelesaian nasihat kewangan khusus turut mengukuhkan kedudukannya sebagai bank pelaburan utama. Pada 2025, CIMB Investment Bank menduduki tempat pertama dalam pasaran modal ekuiti dan hutang Malaysia berdasarkan nilai urus niaga serta bahagian dompet (share of wallet). Bank itu turut menduduki kedudukan teratas dalam pasaran modal ekuiti dan hutang ASEAN berdasarkan nilai urus niaga, dengan kejayaan melaksanakan transaksi rentas sempadan yang mengukuhkan kedudukannya sebagai peneraju M&A dan khidmat nasihat di rantau ASEAN. Tiga anugerah berkenaan turut mengukuhkan janji jenama CIMB, Moving You Forward, yang mencerminkan komitmen berterusan bank dalam memperkasa pelanggan dan komuniti menerusi penyelesaian kewangan yang mudah diakses, inklusif serta berteraskan tujuan. Euromoney Awards for Excellence, yang telah berlangsung lebih 30 tahun, mengiktiraf institusi kewangan yang menetapkan penanda aras global dari segi prestasi, inovasi dan impak kepada pelanggan. Program anugerah itu menilai institusi kewangan menerusi rangka kerja penanda aras Euromoney dengan menggunakan metrik yang boleh dibandingkan, penyerahan maklumat berstruktur serta proses penyelidikan telus bagi menilai prestasi institusi berbanding pesaing masing-masing.-UTUSAN

title: 'The Makeover Guys and RHB Bank Introduce the Makeover Flexi Loan with Up to 120% Financing for Home Purchase and Renovation
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA – Media OutReach Newswire – 15 September 2026 – The Makeover Guys has partnered with RHB Bank Berhad as RHB Bank’s Home Makeover Partner to introduce the Makeover Flexi Loan– an integrated financing solution that enables eligible customers to finance both their home purchase and renovation under a single facility, with financing support of up to 120% of the property’s value. Demand for home renovations continues to rise in Malaysia. The home improvement and renovation market was valued at RM47.7 billion in 2024 and is projected to grow to RM59.2 billion by 2029, as more homeowners invest in upgrading their living spaces to suit changing lifestyles and personal preferences. While home financing is widely available, renovation financing is often treated as a separate borrowing decision. This means many homeowners need to secure additional financing or rely on personal savings after purchasing a property before they can begin renovations. The Makeover Flexi Loan, Powered by RHB Bank offers a different approach by enabling eligible customers to finance both their home purchase and renovation under a single facility. Instead of managing separate financing arrangements, homeowners can plan both from the outset, providing greater financial certainty and a more seamless homeownership journey. The Makeover Flexi Loan, Powered by RHB Bank offers: - Up to 120% financing under a single facility for home purchase and renovation - Up to 90% financing for the property purchase, with an additional up to 30% for renovation works, Mortgage Reducing Term Assurance or Takaful (MRTA/MRTT), and legal and documentation fees - Financing tenure of up to 35 years, or until the borrower reaches the age of 70, whichever comes first - Full Flexi features, allowing customers to make additional repayments and redraw funds based on their financial needs - Progressive disbursement of renovation financing according to contractor milestones throughout the renovation process and is suitable for both homeowners and property investors “Every month, we meet homeowners who are excited to receive the keys to their new homes, only to realise that renovation requires another significant financial commitment. A typical renovation can cost anywhere between RM50,000 and RM150,000, depending on the property type, and many buyers simply are not prepared for that additional expense immediately after purchasing their home,” said Gavin Liew, Founder & CEO of The Makeover Guys We have seen customers delay moving in, renovate room by room over several years or compromise on what they originally wanted because the renovation budget was not available upfront. The Makeover Flexi Loan changes that by allowing homeowners to plan both their property purchase and renovation together from day one. It gives them greater financial certainty and makes it easier to create a home that reflects the way they want to live,” Gavin added. “As homeownership needs evolve, financing solutions must evolve as well. Traditionally, property financing and renovation financing have been treated as separate decisions, even though both are fundamental to creating a home. We saw an opportunity to bridge that gap by bringing these financing needs together under a single solution,” said Sien Vee Loc, Head of Consumer Finance, Group Community Banking, RHB Bank Berhad. Partnering with The Makeover Guys allows us to combine RHB’s financing expertise with trusted renovation capabilities to address a growing market need. Together, we are making it easier for eligible customers to move from purchasing a property to creating a home that meets their lifestyle and investment goals,” Vee Loc added. As Malaysia’s housing market continues to evolve and more buyers enter the market, expectations are shifting beyond financing the purchase of a property to supporting the homeownership journey as a whole. The residential segment remained the largest contributor to Malaysia’s property market in the first quarter of 2026, accounting for 58.8% of all property transactions, with nearly 53,000 residential transactions worth more than RM22 billion. The collaboration connects customers with The Makeover Guys’ end-to-end renovation expertise, providing a complete renovation experience spanning consultation, curated interior design, project management and construction, allowing customers to move from financing their property to completing their home through a single, connected journey.Rather than managing financing, renovation and project delivery separately, customers can now plan every stage together, providing greater certainty over costs, timelines and the overall renovation experience. The partnership further strengthens its commitment to making quality renovations more accessible by combining trusted renovation expertise with financing solutions that support customers from the moment they purchase a property through to the completion of their home. Through this collaboration, The Makeover Guys and RHB Bank are bringing financing and renovation closer together, giving homeowners and property investors a more connected way to plan, finance and complete one of life’s most important investments. For more information regarding the Makeover Flexi Loan, Powered by RHB Bank, kindly visit https://www.themakeover.my/contact to drop your enquiry. Well-loved for its track record of comprehensive and sophisticated approach to design, The Makeover Guys has helped over 7,000 homeowners transform their homes into designer, fully-furnished units through smart renovation — a formula that balances both the aesthetics and practicality of an interior space. The brand currently operates in four key areas in Malaysia: Klang Valley, Johor Bahru, Kuching, and Kota Kinabalu.

title: 'Aktiviti buru saham pacu Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi, sentimen positif
body: 'Bursa Malaysia meningkat selepas mengalami pemulihan kecil pada akhir dagangan Jumaat, dipacu oleh aktiviti memburu saham-saham berharga rendah susulan jualan ketara baru-baru ini, kata penganalisis.  Lantunan itu bagaimanapun kekurangan momentum ketika pasaran Asia kekal diasak tekanan menjelang pengumuman data pasaran tenaga kerja Amerika Syarikat (AS).  Pada 5 petang, indeks penunjuk utama FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) menokok 0.51 mata atau 0.03 peratus kepada 1,630.87 daripada paras penutup 1,630.36, semalam.  Indeks penanda aras itu yang dibuka menokok 3.51 mata kepada 1,633.87, bergerak dalam jajaran 1,630.63 hingga 1,640.78 sepanjang sesi dagangan.  Sentimen pasaran positif dengan kaunter untung mengatasi rugi iaitu 585 berbanding 541 manakala 558 lain tidak berubah, 1,089 tidak diniagakan dan 24 lain digantung dagangannya.  Jumlah dagangan meningkat kepada 4.23 bilion unit bernilai RM2.70 bilion daripada 3.1 bilion unit bernilai RM2.7 bilion, semalam.  Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd Thong Pak Leng berkata aktiviti penjualan pada baru-baru ini menyaksikan penilaian saham mewah yang lebih menarik, sekali gus berpotensi menggalakkan usaha pengumpulan saham secara berperingkat.  Namun pada masa sama, katanya, pelabur terus mengambil langkah untuk kekal bertahan berikutan perkembangan seperti hasil bon dan harga minyak mentah yang kekal tinggi.  “Bagi bursa tempatan pula, kami berpendirian berhati-hati di disebalik peningkatan berikutan risiko cabaran luar yang mungkin mengekalkan ketidaktentuan pasaran pada tahap tinggi,” katanya kepada Bernama.  Saham wajaran tinggi menyaksikan Maybank naik tujuh sen kepada RM10.02, Public Bank susut satu sen kepada RM4.66, CIMB berkurangan empat sen kepada RM7.65, Tenaga Nasional meningkat enam sen kepada RM12.96 dan IHH Healthcare meraih 10 sen kepada RM7.80.  Saham paling aktif menyaksikan Zetrix AI susut lima sen kepada 11.5 sen, Jaks Resources tidak berubah pada 18 sen, JCY International menokok 10.5 sen kepada 66 sen, V.S Industry naik dua sen kepada 29 sen dan PUC menambah satu sen kepada 4.5 sen.  Bagi saham paling untung, Malaysian Pacific Industries melonjak RM1.28 kepada RM42.40, UWC naik 47 sen kepada RM7.57, Vitrox menokok 46 sen kepada RM10.46, United Plantations meraih 42 sen kepada RM31.38 manakala UMS Integration meningkat 38 sen kepada RM9.03.  Saham yang mencatatkan penurunan ketara diterajui oleh Nestle yang susut 48 sen kepada RM89.52, Kuala Lumpur Kepong turun 42 sen kepada RM21, Enra berkurangan 25.5 sen kepada 72.5 sen manakala Allianz Malaysia dan Hong Leong Bank masing-masing menguncup 20 sen kepada RM20.80 dan RM22.64.  Di papan indeks pula, Indeks FBM Mid 70 meningkat 122.94 mata kepada 17,481.93, Indeks FBM Emas menokok 27.04 mata kepada 12,170.57 manakala Indeks FBM Top 100 naik 24.52 mata kepada 11,957.68.  Indeks FBM Emas Syariah meningkat 47.31 mata kepada 12,060.32 manakala Indeks FBM ACE menokok 46.49 mata kepada 5,529.46.  Prestasi sektor menyaksikan Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian naik 0.79 mata kepada 178.52, Indeks Tenaga susut 1.98 mata kepada 833.03, Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan menguncup 20.40 mata kepada 19,040.51 manakala Indeks Perladangan meningkat 29.97 mata kepada 9,056.55.  Jumlah dagangan di Pasaran Utama meningkat kepada 2.67 bilion unit bernilai RM2.34 bilion daripada 1.82 bilion unit bernilai RM2.42 bilion, semalam.  Waran melonjak kepada 973.40 juta unit bernilai RM160.21 juta daripada 618.78 juta unit bernilai RM72.71 juta sebelum ini.  Di Pasaran ACE, jumlah dagangan susut kepada 593.05 juta unit bernilai RM205.21 juta daripada 650.13 juta unit bernilai RM226.92 juta sebelumnya.  Kaunter produk pengguna dan perkhidmatan menyumbang sebanyak 241.01 juta saham yang diniagakan di Pasaran Utama manakala produk dan perkhidmatan perindustrian (266.57 juta), pembinaan (183.37 juta), teknologi (1.41 bilion), perkhidmatan kewangan (50.26 juta), hartanah (152.37 juta), perladangan (19.73 juta), amanah pelaburan hartanah (15.78 juta), dana tertutup (214,200), tenaga (99.69 juta), penjagaan kesihatan (103.06 juta) telekomunikasi dan media (28.89 juta), pengangkutan dan logistik (47.35 juta), utiliti (46.61 juta) dan amanah perniagaan (119,600) .

title: 'The socialist tinge running through Malay society and politics
body: 'By Murray Hunter A CONSISTENT thread of light, humanitarian socialism, the social-democratic and developmental variety, has long run through Malay society and politics in Malaysia. It appears in traditional cultural traits, interpretations of Islamic social ethics, the policies of major Malay parties including UMNO and PAS, and the structure of the modern economy. This form of socialism today is focused on mutual help, social justice, state intervention for equity, and protection of the community, especially the Malay majority. Private ownership, markets and individual enterprise remain, but they operate within a framework of collective responsibility and guided redistribution, through both the New Economic Policy (NEP) and reserved Malay land. Several deep-rooted Malay cultural traits help explain why such ideas found fertile ground throughout Malaya’s contemporary history. Almost forgotten traditions in the traditional kampong, gotong royong was a practical expression of communal cooperation. Villagers regularly came together to build or repair houses, plant and harvest rice, clear drains and paths, maintain the surau or cemetery, and assist with weddings, funerals and other life-cycle events. The familiar proverb “berat sama dipikul, ringan sama dijinjing” captured the expectation that burdens should be shared. More broadly, Malay society has tended to favour communalism rather than strong individualism. Group harmony, collective responsibility, loyalty to kin and community, and the avoidance of open confrontation often take precedence over assertive personal autonomy or pure self-interest. This cultural orientation creates a natural affinity for policies that stress mutual support, shared welfare and the idea that the community’s well-being is more important than unchecked individual gain. This is partly explained by Malaysia’s high power-distance score on widely used cultural dimensions such as those developed by Geert Hofstede. In high power-distance societies, hierarchy is accepted as normal, and people are generally more willing to follow authority without extensive public questioning. Among many Malays, this has historically translated into relatively high deference to traditional leaders, the state, religious figures and those in positions of formal power. When government programmes are presented as serving the uplift of the Malay community, this readiness to accept direction from above has made large-scale state intervention more readily accepted than it might be in strongly individualistic, low power-distance cultures. The combination of communalism and hierarchical acceptance helped legitimise ambitious top-down social and economic programmes. Islamic teachings have reinforced the same outlook for many. Obligatory zakat functions as a structured redistribution of wealth from those with surplus to the poor, the needy, debtors and other designated categories. The duty to care for orphans, widows and the vulnerable, the prohibition of riba (usury), and the repeated Qur’anic emphasis on adl (justice) have been interpreted by some Muslim thinkers as containing important socialist elements. Early PAS leader Burhanuddin al-Helmy explicitly combined Islamist, nationalist and socialist ideas in the struggle against colonialism and inequality. Malaysian sociologist Syed Hussein Alatas, in his work Islam and Socialism, argued that Islam’s principles of anti-exploitation and social justice made it compatible with non-Marxist forms of socialism focused on fairness and community welfare rather than atheistic materialism or the abolition of private property. In formal politics, the pattern is clear. Early Malay leftist and populist groups drew on ideas of uplifting ordinary people (marhaen). Within UMNO, the decisive shift came after the 1969 racial riots under Tun Abdul Razak. title: 'Tengku Ampuan Pahang rasmi Kejohanan Golf Wanita, The Ladies 2026
body: 'PETALING JAYA: Kejohanan golf wanita, The Ladies 2026 rasmi membuka tirai kelmarin menerusi acara Pro-Am Diraja yang dirasmikan oleh Tengku Ampuan Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah Almarhum Sultan Iskandar Al-Haj di The Mines Resort and Golf Club. Kejohanan yang berlangsung selama tiga hari itu menyaksikan penyertaan seramai 50 pemain merangkumi kelompok profesional dan amatur termasuklah kemunculan semula juara bertahan, Liyana Durisic serta atlet Olimpik negara, Kelly Tan. Menurut The Mines Resort & Golf Club, matlamat utama kejohanan itu adalah untuk melahirkan lebih ramai pemain berwibawa tempatan selain bertindak sebagai batu loncatan penting sebelum saingan bertaraf antarabangsa menjelang kejohanan Maybank Championship tidak lama lagi. Katanya, penganjuran itu membawa mesej yang jelas kepada generasi muda bahawa kerjaya dalam bidang sukan golf profesional bukan mustahil untuk dicapai oleh wanita Malaysia. “Ia adalah satu jemputan kepada generasi baharu untuk melihat golf profesional bukan sekadar sesuatu yang dimainkan di tempat lain di dunia tetapi sebagai laluan kerjaya yang boleh diceburi oleh wanita Malaysia,” katanya dalam kenyataan. Dalam pada itu, saingan Pro-Am Diraja hari ini menyaksikan pasukan yang dibarisi Dianna Lee, Ang Bee Ee, Jojo Goh dan digandingkan bersama pemain profesional Kelly Tan dinobatkan sebagai juara keseluruhan. Tempat kedua diraih oleh pasukan Miran Shin, Raina Azene Ramli, Nur Azreen dan pemain profesional Tan Ying Ying manakala kedudukan ketiga disandang oleh Yang Amat Mulia Che Puan Besar Kedah, Che Puan Hajah Hamimah Haji Hamidun, Datuk Norfaizah Zainal, June Yap bersama pemain profesional, Zulaikah Nasser. Menurutnya lagi, selain memperkukuh pembangunan bakat tempatan, penganjuran edisi kali ini turut mendapat sokongan padu pelbagai syarikat korporat terkemuka seperti Prudential, 100PLUS, Power Root dan Delon. Jelasnya, pihak penganjur turut mempunyai perancangan jangka panjang untuk meningkatkan kualiti kejohanan itu dengan sasaran hadiah terkumpul mencecah kira-kira RM12.5 juta pada masa hadapan. “Objektifnya bukan sekadar meningkatkan wang kemenangan tetapi untuk mewujudkan acara yang mempunyai status kukuh bagi menarik perhatian antarabangsa, di samping memberikan pemain Malaysia platform yang lebih berkesan ke pentas global,” katanya. – UTUSAN The post Tengku Ampuan Pahang rasmi Kejohanan Golf Wanita, The Ladies 2026 appeared first on Utusan Malaysia.

title: 'Mandat Pengurus Keselamatan Kebakaran Bomba bagi 9,451 Bangunan Tonjolkan Permintaan Pematuhan untuk Unique Fire
body: 'Langkah Malaysia menjadikan pemilik bangunan bertanggungjawab secara langsung terhadap keselamatan kebakaran dijangka meluaskan pasaran pematuhan bagi pembekal perlindungan kebakaran, sekali gus meletakkan Unique Fire Holdings Berhad (“Unique Fire”) antara syarikat yang berpotensi mendapat manfaat. Mulai 1 April 2027, pemilik 9,451 bangunan yang ditetapkan di bawah Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba akan diwajibkan melantik Pengurus Keselamatan Kebakaran (FSM) dan Pegawai Keselamatan Kebakaran (FSO), serta menubuhkan Organisasi Keselamatan Kebakaran (OKK) di premis masing-masing. Ketua Pengarah Jabatan Bomba dan Penyelamat Malaysia (JBPM), Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad berkata, keperluan itu selaras dengan Seksyen 27A Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba (Pindaan) 2025. Menurut beliau, mana-mana bangunan yang diperiksa dalam tempoh satu hingga dua tahun akan datang dan diwajibkan memiliki Perakuan Bomba perlu melaksanakan struktur baharu tersebut. Beliau berkata demikian selepas melancarkan program FSM dan FSO di Menara Merdeka Maybank, Kuala Lumpur pada 6 Oktober 2026, di mana kumpulan pertama seramai 174 FSM dan 324 FSO menerima sijil masing-masing. Perubahan utama melibatkan kaedah pembaharuan Perakuan Bomba. Selepas ini, JBPM akan menilai laporan pemeriksaan tahunan yang disediakan oleh FSM bagi tujuan pembaharuan perakuan, tanpa perlu menjalankan pemeriksaan fizikal ke atas setiap bangunan setiap tahun. JBPM kini mempunyai 13 penyedia latihan berdaftar dan telah mengeluarkan tender bagi menambah bilangan penyedia latihan serta jurulatih. Tanggungjawab pematuhan beralih kepada pemilik bangunan Rangka kerja ini memindahkan tanggungjawab keselamatan kebakaran harian daripada pihak berkuasa kepada pemilik bangunan dan kakitangan dalaman mereka yang bertauliah. Di bawah program ini, FSM menjalani kursus lima hari merangkumi pemeriksaan bangunan, perancangan pemindahan, pelaporan dan penyelenggaraan, manakala FSO menjalani kursus teknikal selama tiga hari. Dengan FSM bertanggungjawab ke atas laporan tahunan yang menjadi asas pembaharuan Perakuan Bomba, pemilik bangunan dijangka memberi penekanan lebih besar untuk memastikan alat pemadam api, gelung hos, pili bomba, sistem pemercik, peranti pengesan dan penggera serta sistem pemadaman kebakaran sentiasa berfungsi dengan baik. Ini menunjukkan permintaan yang lebih stabil bagi penggantian, penyelenggaraan dan pengisian semula peralatan di seluruh 9,451 premis yang ditetapkan, termasuk bangunan berpenghuni tinggi dan berisiko tinggi. Unique Fire, yang ditubuhkan pada 1997 dan beribu pejabat di Shah Alam, Selangor, terlibat dalam pemasangan, pembuatan dan pengedaran sistem, peralatan dan aksesori perlindungan kebakaran aktif untuk persekitaran terbina. Rangkaian produknya merangkumi alat pemadam api mudah alih, gelung hos, sistem pili bomba dan pemercik, sistem paip naik basah dan kering, peranti pengesan dan penggera kebakaran, serta sistem pemadaman kebakaran termasuk sistem kimia basah dan karbon dioksida. Kumpulan memasarkan produk di bawah jenama sendiri iaitu Unique, Unique227, Yama dan Commander, di samping jenama pihak ketiga seperti Kidde, serta menyediakan perkhidmatan penyelenggaraan peralatan perlindungan kebakaran dan mesin pengisian semula alat pemadam api kimia kering. Kumpulan telah pun mengenal pasti akta yang dipinda itu sebagai pemacu permintaan. Bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 31 Mac 2026, hasil Unique Fire meningkat 6.2% kepada RM114.7 juta, disokong oleh jualan pemasangan dan pengedaran yang lebih kukuh, terutamanya sistem pemadaman kebakaran. Pengarah Eksekutif, Marcus Liew berkata perniagaan teras perlindungan kebakaran terus berkembang dalam persekitaran kawal selia yang menyokong, dipacu oleh penguatkuasaan Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba (Pindaan) 2025 serta pelaksanaan projek di bawah Rancangan Malaysia Ketiga Belas, dan Kumpulan menjangkakan permintaan yang berterusan hasil keperluan pematuhan peraturan dan penganugerahan kontrak yang sedang berjalan. Kumpulan turut meluaskan jangkauan ke luar negara melalui Unique Mosafe Sdn Bhd, usaha sama 60:40 dengan Shanghai Mosafe Equipment Co Ltd untuk mengeluar dan membekalkan pemercik kebakaran, dengan Shanghai Mosafe menyediakan sokongan teknikal ke arah pensijilan Underwriters Laboratories (UL). Dengan keperluan FSM dan FSO berkuat kuasa dalam tempoh kurang enam bulan lagi, rejim pematuhan baharu ini dijangka mengubah keselamatan kebakaran daripada pemeriksaan sekali setahun kepada tanggungjawab berterusan bagi pemilik bangunan, satu peralihan yang selari dengan tawaran produk dan perkhidmatan Unique Fire.

Dengan keperluan FSM dan FSO berkuat kuasa dalam tempoh kurang enam bulan lagi, rejim pematuhan baharu ini dijangka mengubah keselamatan kebakaran daripada pemeriksaan sekali setahun kepada tanggungjawab berterusan bagi pemilik bangunan, satu peralihan yang selari dengan tawaran produk dan perkhidmatan Unique Fire.
